Prime minister Andy Burnham has hit out at President Vladimir Putin during his first state visit to Kyiv, amid mounting tensions between Russia and the UK.

The British leader chaired his first meeting of the so-called Coalition of the Willing to emphasise Britain’s continued support for Ukraine through the provision of long-range missile blueprints.

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said that the move would add “fuel to the fire” and “prevent any progress in the peace process”.

“Who started the fire? That’s the question isn’t it?” Burnham hit back in an address to Ukraine’s European allies on Monday.

“Putin is now hoping he can win through a campaign of terror using ballistic missiles against Ukrainian civilians.

“This can never be the route to victory, and we need to be clear in sending that message. It means doing everything we can all do, and working with our allies as well, beyond this coalition, to dig into our own stocks of air defence... to protect Ukraine from the missiles that are falling now.”

open image in gallery Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky, right, greets British Prime Minister Andy Burnham during a ceremony to mark Independence Day in Kyiv ( AP )

Both Zelensky and Burnham delivered speeches outside Kyiv’s St Sofia cathedral on the anniversary of the country’s 35th year of independence.

“Despite Russia’s outrageous threats to my country, we will continue our support for Ukraine,” he said.

The prime minister compared Ukraine’s battle with Russia to the British fight against Nazi Germany, saying: “My nation kept the flame of European freedom alive in the 20th century, you hold that flame in the 21st.”

It marked his first foray on the international stage, heading the coalition of the willing group of 34 countries, that was set up by his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer in support of Ukraine.

Tensions between London and Moscow have been mounting for weeks with it emerging over the weekend that Russia had withdrawn its ambassador to the UK, Andrei Kelin, last month after seven years in the diplomatic post.

The lower-ranking charge d’affaires has taken the lead in his absence, according to an embassy spokesperson who spoke to The Times.

open image in gallery President Zelensky has warned his country faces a tough winter without further support from allies ( Reuters )

The latest announcement of support by Burnham means that the British government has agreed to allow defence firm MBDA to release classified information and blueprints on UK components for the long-range Scalp missile. The weapons are the equivalent of the French-produced version of the UK’s storm shadow.

Last Tuesday it was reported that British-made drones had been used in Ukraine prompting Moscow to threaten “consequences” for the support. It said ominously that the deeper the assistance that Britain provided “the higher price it will pay”.

At the time, Burnham doubled down saying: “This is the UK doing what it has long said it would do, which is to support Ukraine 100 per cent against this illegal war led by Vladimir Putin.”

The European Commission, meanwhile, has approved a further €6.1 billion ($7.12 billion) in financial aid for Ukraine for the purchase of defence systems, such as air defence, missiles, ammunition and radars.

open image in gallery Russia has warned that the UK will suffer ‘consequences’ for supporting Ukraine ( Reuters )

The latest aid package came on top of €16 billion of previously approved procurement plans, of which €8.35 billion had already been disbursed, according to the EU.

"As Russia intensifies its attacks, we are stepping up to help Ukraine protect its people and defend its skies. Europe stands with Ukraine and we will deliver what it needs, when it needs it," president Ursula von der Leyen said in a statement.

In other developments in the ongoing war, Russian attacks killed three people near Kharkiv overnight, according to the region’s governor, while Moscow claimed debris from a Ukrainian drone killed two children in Russia’s Krasnodar on Sunday.

Not all physical activity is equal when it comes to protecting the brain from dementia. Where and why we move may matter more than most people realise.

A large new review of studies published in The Lancet Public Health found that leisure-time physical activity – such as sport, dancing or going to the gym – was linked to a 24% lower risk of dementia. Housework was linked to a 15% lower risk, although this finding came from just one study.

Occupational physical activity, on the other hand, was linked to a 20% increased risk of dementia.

The study compiled data from 74 studies involving more than 4.2 million people in 30 countries, making it one of the largest studies of its kind.

open image in gallery Occupational physical activity was linked to a 20% increased risk of dementia ( Getty Images )

Brain protection is well established

Physical activity may protect the brain in several ways. It improves blood flow, helping to deliver oxygen and nutrients to the brain. It also causes muscles to release molecules that can reduce inflammation, help the brain use energy and encourage the growth of new brain cells.

That is one reason why reducing physical inactivity is a key part of the World Health Organization’s recently updated dementia prevention guidelines.

There is plenty of evidence that being active can help protect against dementia. A UK Biobank study tracked people’s activity using wearable devices for four years. Even less than 35 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity a week was linked to a 41% lower risk of dementia compared with no such activity.

More vigorous exercise – the kind that leaves you too breathless to talk – was linked to a 63% lower risk of dementia compared with being inactive.

Meanwhile, the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing followed people for 17 years and found that the more active people were, the lower their risk of dementia. The most active group had about half the risk of the least active group.

Walking outdoors – even as little as two miles a day – and gardening have also both been linked to a 25 to 36% lower risk of dementia.

But the new Lancet study suggests that physical activity at work or while travelling to work may not offer the same protection. It may even be linked to a higher risk of developing dementia.

Physical activity paradox

Physical activity at work, based on the combined data from five studies, was linked to a 20% higher risk. And active commuting, such as walking or cycling, based on just two studies, was linked to a 10% higher risk.

Researchers call this the “physical activity paradox”. It is well documented in heart disease research: physical activity at work fails to deliver the same protective effect as the same activity done during leisure time, and can sometimes increase risk instead. Several explanations have been proposed.

People in physically demanding jobs may have had fewer opportunities for education than people in office jobs. Education and mentally stimulating activities throughout life are linked to greater reserve capacity in the brain – its ability to cope with damage and keep working normally.

Manual workers may also be more likely to work in polluted environments, such as factories or building sites. And commuting, particularly by bicycle or on foot, can mean greater exposure to air pollution. Air pollution has separately been linked to a higher risk of Alzheimer’s disease.

About the author Eef Hogervorst is a Professor of Biological Psychology, Loughborough University. This article was first published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article .

Recreational exercise accounts for just 4% of active time in low-income countries, but 28% in high- and middle-income countries. So differences in income may shape the factors that influence dementia risk around the world.

The researchers say more research is needed, particularly in low-income countries, to understand what is behind the link between physical activity at work and dementia.

Not all physically demanding jobs are the same. Two physically demanding jobs can involve similar amounts of activity but very different exposures to noise, pollution, stress, heat and other hazards.

These findings point to a deeper inequality: leisure time itself is a resource – one that isn’t distributed evenly. People in low-income countries and those who do physically demanding jobs often have the least opportunity for the kind of activity that seems to protect the brain, while facing the working conditions that may undermine it. Understanding and addressing that imbalance may matter as much for dementia prevention as encouraging people to move more.

Carl Froch has backed heavyweight sensation Moses Itauma to “pass” his Filip Hrgovic “test” with ease, citing the unique qualities that have kept Itauma unbeaten so far.

On Saturday, 21-year-old Itauma faces Hrgovic in his toughest fight yet, but the Briton is still the favourite to emerge victorious and claim the vacant IBF heavyweight title.

Southpaw Itauma will enter the fight at London’s O2 Arena with a record of 14-0 (12 KOs), while Croatia’s Hrgovic is 20-1 (15 KOs).

open image in gallery Moses Itauma at a press conference for his fight with Filip Hrgovic ( Getty )

Last time out, Itauma stopped Jermaine Franklin in five rounds, building on a first-round knockout of Dillian Whyte. Meanwhile, Hrgovic has bounced back from his first loss – a 2024 stoppage by Daniel Dubois – with a hat-trick of wins over Britons.

The 34-year-old outpointed Joe Joyce and David Adeleye before stopping Dave Allen in three rounds, but Froch does not expect Hrgovic to extend that streak against Itauma.

“Moses Itauma is very naturally talented,” the former super-middleweight champion told The Independent via Betpack. “The way he moves and evades shots appears to happen almost subconsciously. It is an automatic reflex.

“He is a gifted fighter with ridiculously fast hands for a heavyweight, and he has shown power at the level he has competed at so far. The obvious question is that his chin has not really been tested yet. Hrgovic should ask some of the questions that need answering.

“He will probably catch Itauma, because Hrgovic is a serious operator who gets in there to win. We saw that against Daniel Dubois and, more recently, Dave Allen. He means business.

“It is a very good step-up for Itauma and by far the biggest test of his professional career. I believe Itauma passes it with flying colours, but it is still an interesting and legitimate test.”

News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Frustrated Russell fails to make up ground as Norris wins incident-packed Dutch GP
News.content:
George Russell had another frustrating Sunday as the Dutch Grand Prix weekend slipped by with him failing to reduce his deficit to leader Kimi Antonelli. In a thrilling finale to the 72-lap race at the Dutch seaside, Lando Norris took his second victory in a row with two bold overtakes in one lap.

Yet compatriot Russell was irritated by Mercedes team orders for him to let Antonelli through into second place in the closing stages. It was a decision he believed risked a double podium for the team and threatened to put him even further behind his team-mate in the standings, with two charging Ferraris close behind. It was a race that, once again, fell away, despite Russell doing little wrong.

“Is he [Antonelli] fighting for the win or is he planning to catch Norris?” he asked, when the McLaren driver was 11 seconds down the road – the margin he would win by. “Yeah – we just lost a double podium here, mate,” was his response after moving aside.

Whilst Norris, who lost his lead from pole to Antonelli on the first lap, sealed the victory with two superb overtakes on lap 54 – first the Italian and then Lewis Hamilton – Russell had to mount a stout defence from Hamilton to secure third. It was against the odds, as both Ferraris, like Antonelli, were on fresh rubber after pitting under a late virtual safety car. Like Russell, Hamilton was critical of his team for their strategy choices.

Russell’s first podium finish since Silverstone – with his sprint victory on Saturday – means he at least retakes second place in the championship from Hamilton, but trails Antonelli by the same 59 point-gap he had after Hungary. That is despite him looking the faster and more comfortable Mercedes driver on Friday and Saturday.

News.title: Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win
News.content:
Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

News.title: How to spend a perfect weekend in Lake Como
News.content:
An hour drive north of Milan, Lake Como is the most glamorous of Italy’s lakes, hemmed in by the snow-capped Alps with picture-perfect villages on the water. Milanesi pop here for the day for a breath of fresh air and to soak up the fabulous vistas, while international visitors – the Clooneys, the Kennedys – have long been drawn by the grand lakefront hotels and the elegant mahogany Riva boats that zip along the lake’s deep blue waters.

Smart hotels and expensive boats aside, Lake Como is rich in culture, with opulent villas that once belonged to artists, writers, opera singers and explorers. Pliny the Elder, author of the first encyclopaedia, was born here, while 19th-century soprano Giuditta Pasta is known to have entertained composers Bellini and Donizetti in her lakefront residence on the eastern shore.

Though famous spots such as pretty Bellagio still pull in the majority of visitors, the lake has retained its authenticity, with plenty of sleepy fishing villages, such as Laglio, Torno and Nesso, home to rustic, family-run trattorias serving up traditional hearty fare, including risotto al pesce persico (risotto with perch).

News.title: Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair
News.content:
It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

Sports.title: Is £130m Alvarez an upgrade on Gyokeres? In many ways yes, but Arsenal will miss parts of their current striker’s game
Sports.content:
JULIAN ALVAREZ could be the final piece of Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal jigsaw, but the stats suggest Viktor Gyokeres would leave some pretty big boots to fill.

The Gunners are ready to make a move for the Atletico Madrid and Argentina star in the final week of the transfer window if they get encouragement from either the player or his club that a deal can actually be done.



Although Alvarez is said to prefer a move to Barcelona, Atletico have strongly resisted the idea of selling him to their La Liga rivals – report The Athletic.

That potentially leaves the door open for a move to Arsenal, with some reports suggesting that they could even throw Gyokeres in as part of a sensational player plus cash offer.



The Gunners are prepared to go beyond their club-record £105million fee that they paid to sign Declan Rice from West Ham in 2023, with Atletico reportedly wanting as much as £130m to even consider selling their star man.

Alvarez was booed yesterday when his name was read out before Atletico’s 2-2 draw with Villarreal and was jeered again when he came on as a 66th-minute substitute.

That backlash could yet force Atletico to soften their stance – particularly with reports in Spain suggesting Alvarez’s position on only wanting Barcelona is beginning to change.

The former Manchester City man is still hoping for that dream move, but crucially, he is no longer thought to be completely closing the door on a return to the Premier League.

Gary Neville certainly believes Alvarez would take the Gunners, and indeed captain Martin Odegaard‘s game, to another level.

After Arsenal’s 3-0 win against Coventry on Friday night, eight-time Premier League winner Neville told Sky Sports: “What a squad [Mikel Arteta] has built. If he puts another forward into that, if they could get Julian Alvarez somehow, that would light this place up as you’d have a world-class striker to go with all the world-class defenders and midfielders.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“They wouldn’t just become Premier League title winners they’d go the next step and win a Champions League. He needs a bit of magic up front – someone that can win a game for you when you don’t play well.

“Odegaard is exceptional. If there was an Ian Wright-type player up front for Arsenal who makes those short runs he’d be even better.

“As [Kai] Havertz and [Viktor] Gyokeres always come to the ball, Odegaard has to play possession rather than playing the slip passes. If Arsenal were to sign Julian Alvarez then he’d go up a level as it would be perfect for the style of play.”

There is certainly an argument for that as Alvarez is more creative than Gyokeres, registering ten assists last season compared with the Swede’s three.



His 127 minutes per goal or assist also beats Gyokeres’ 145, but that is where the idea of Alvarez being a straightforward upgrade starts to become a little more complicated.

Gyokeres scored 21 goals in 3,481 minutes, while Alvarez managed 20 in 3,549 minutes – meaning the Arsenal man was more prolific in terms of minutes per goal — 165.7 compared with Alvarez’s 190.5.

Gyokeres, who only signed for Arsenal last summer for £55m from Sporting Lisbon, also had a superior shot conversion rate, scoring with 22.6 per cent of his efforts compared with Alvarez’s 15.9 per cent.

There was a period between December and February when Alvarez went 11 games without scoring – something which clearly damaged his goals-per-minute and conversion rate numbers.



The idea that Alvarez simply lives in the space behind defenders is also not quite the complete picture.

Although he can make clever runs in behind, Alvarez also likes to come towards the ball and get involved in build-up play – something he showed with Argentina at the World Cup when he often dropped deeper to allow Lionel Messi to stay higher up the pitch.

That helps explain why his passing accuracy is a whopping 82.8 per cent compared with Gyokeres’ 63.8 per cent.

In that sense, Alvarez can be more of a Harry Kane-style striker – dropping deep, linking play and dragging defenders around, while having the ability to get on the end of things too.

His low centre of gravity also makes him incredibly difficult to knock off the ball and helps explain why he completed 65 dribbles last season compared with just 13 for Gyokeres.



But if Alvarez does come with Gyokeres heading in the other direction, what Arsenal would lose is equally important.

Gyokeres is 6ft 2in, while Alvarez is only 5ft 7in – a physical difference that is reflected in their aerial numbers.

Gyokeres won 44 aerial duels compared with just 13 for Alvarez.

The Swede also won considerably more fouls – 54 to 32 – as his power and physicality makes him a nightmare for defenders.



Perhaps the biggest surprise is possession won in the final third.

Alvarez has a reputation as a pressing monster, but Gyokeres actually won more possession in the final third last season – 34 times compared with Alvarez’s 31.

Gyokeres also recorded more touches in the opposition box – 219 to Alvarez’s 198.

Alvarez did, however, take more shots – 126 to Gyokeres’ 93 – largely because of the way he becomes involved in more phases of the attack by dropping deep.

So, Neville’s prediction that Alvarez would be the perfect fit is not necessarily wrong.



However, the statistics suggest it isn’t quite as simple as swapping one striker for another and watching Arsenal improve across the board.

Arteta could give Alvarez a slightly different role, asking him to prioritise making more runs beyond the defence.

If that happens, Alvarez’s movement could indeed take the Gunners up another level – as Neville eluded to.

But it would also mean sacrificing the aerial threat, physical presence and penalty-box dominance that Gyokeres brings.



Arteta’s caveat to that could be that he also has Havertz, who brings the same qualities.

Alvarez, on the other hand, would give Arsenal something different – a more rounded footballer who offers more creativity.

But Gyokeres was the more efficient goalscorer last season and provides qualities Alvarez simply does not possess.

The numbers, therefore, suggest Alvarez is an upgrade in some ways, rather than the complete upgrade many expect.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

For Arsenal, the question is whether Arteta values what Alvarez adds more than what he would lose by replacing Gyokeres.



With just eight days of the transfer window left, that could be the £130m question which decides whether the Gunners make one final blockbuster move.

Sports.title: Arsenal ‘plot ANOTHER raid on Dortmund for chief scout with ace behind Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham transfers’
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are reportedly hoping to poach Borussia Dortmund’s chief scout Sebastian Krug.

The 43-year-old is highly rated after his impressive work snapping up players like Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham and Jadon Sancho at a young age.



In recent years he has masterminded deals for youngsters like Samuele Inacio, Mathis Albert and Enzo Duarte.

Arsenal have already raided Dortmund for one scout previously after hiring Sven Mislintat in 2017.



And now they are eyeing up Krug in the hopes he can replicate his portfolio of top deals, according to Sky in Germany.

Talks are said to have already taken place between Arsenal and Krug over a possible move.



And it’s claimed there is a “growing sense” that Krug may be headed towards the next step in his career.

German outlet Bild claim officials at Signal Iduna Park are “relaxed” about the situation and are yet to be “officially informed” about an approach.

It goes on to say Arsenal would have to make an “exorbitant” offer to Dortmund for the club’s top brass to consider his exit.

The German club “wont let him go without a fight”, the report claims, saying he is “simply too important”.

Most recently he was responsible for bringing Jobe Bellingham to the club from Sunderland, as well as Jamie Gittens.

Arsenal currently have Andrea Berta as sporting director with Maurizio Micheli as chief scout.

It’s unclear how Krug would work with Berta and Micheli if he was appointed by the Gunners.

Micheli – who was instrumental in bringing Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to Napoli – has been part of the scouting team that picked out stars like Christos Tzolis this summer.



Berta, meanwhile, has been mostly well received for his signings after securing the likes of Martin Zubimendi, Viktor Gyokeres, Cristhian Mosquera, Eberechi Eze and Bruno Guimaraes.

Sports.title: Arsenal, Man Utd and England heroes among football icons blasting Gianni Infantino and fume ‘we will be silent no more’
Sports.content:
A HOST of football legends including Emmanuel Petit and Lucy Bronze have shared an open letter turning on Gianni Infantino.

The statement was also posted by ex-Manchester United defender Mikael Silvestre, who is on Fifa’s Players’ Voice panel.



Infantino is on thin ice in his role as Fifa President following his deeply controversial plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other tournaments for £20billion.

The Swiss chief, 56, backtracked and U-turned on his money-grabbing scheme but has lost the support of much of football – including some inside Fifa and its member associations and confederations.



Now in the latest blow to Infantino, they have turned on him with a bruising statement – although opted against naming him directly.

The post reads: “As players, football has given us everything, and we have given our lives to it.

“Between us, we have played on its greatest stages and worn our national shirts with pride.

“But we know that none of our achievements would’ve been possible without the fans, whose passion and commitment is the foundation of this game.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world. Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership.

“For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s transfer window verdict and what’s still needed before deadline after Ezri Konsa deal
Sports.content:
ARSENAL’s transfer window is nearly over as they look to build a squad that can defend their Premier League title.

The Gunners have had a difficult window with several key targets proving out of their reach even after their Premier League triumph last campaign.



But that hasn’t stopped them from getting some massive signings over the line, which will surely give them an edge as they look to hold onto their crown.

There is still business to be done in the closing days of the window, but Mikel Arteta has given himself a strong base on which to build.



Here’s SunSport Arsenal reporter Simon Collings’ verdict of Arsenal’s transfer window so far…

KEY SIGNING: BRUNO GUIMARAES

The gruelling nature of last season led to Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi being run into the ground.



Arsenal have solved that problem by adding genuine depth to the midfield — and a player who is proven in the Premier League.

Guimaraes, 28, will also free Martin Odegaard to play higher up the pitch as a No 10.

WHAT’S MISSING OR STILL NEEDS TO BE DONE?

A left-winger is needed, especially if Gabriel Martinelli is sold.

The Gunners failed in their pursuits of Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Jr, so they could pivot to signing a striker instead.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Greek winger Christos Tzolis, 24, impressed in pre-season and looked bright in the Community Shield, but the attack could use fresh blood.

VERDICT

Arsenal are in a better position than last term — and that is down to the signings of Ezri Konsa and Guimaraes.

England centre-back Konsa, 28, is a real statement of intent and gives the North London side unrivalled depth when it comes to defence.

The squad is also in a healthy position, especially concerning the attacking players at Mikel Arteta’s disposal.



The Gunners were without Bukayo Saka, Kai Havertz and Odegaard for large chunks of last term — but all three are ready for the new campaign as they defend the title.

Sports.title: Man Utd transfer window verdict with at least two more signings needed and one player who needs to be sold
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED entered their first transfer window with Michael Carrick as permanent manager with clear goals.

Their cumbersome midfield especially needed a revamp if the Red Devils were to compete in the Champions League this season.



Casemiro‘s departure and Manuel Ugarte‘s ACL injury at the World Cup drove the point home that new blood was needed in the middle of the park – a need which Carrick and Co rose to address.

But with just days left in the window, and after a disastrous 2-0 opening loss at Hull, attentions have to turn to other areas of concern that would help the Old Trafford side stake their claim back amongst Europe’s top clubs.



Here is SunSport Manchester United reporter Katherine Walsh’s verdict on the Red Devils’ transfer window so far…

KEY SIGNING

YOURI TIELEMANS has the potential to be the pound-for-pound signing of the summer.



Manchester United triggered Tielemans’ £35million release clause last month and Aston Villa might otherwise have asked for double that.

The Belgium captain, 29, brings the experience United’s midfield needed after Casemiro’s exit — boasting 244 Prem appearances and goals in finals for both Leicester and Villa.

WHAT’S MISSING OR STILL NEEDS TO BE DONE?

Andrey Santos and the incoming Carlos Baleba rounded out the midfield rebuild, but a left-back to compete with Luke Shaw is a priority as United return to the Champions League after two seasons out.

Shaw, 31, is entering the final year of his deal and it will be difficult for him to handle the workload alone, even if right-backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui fill in at times.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Marcus Rashford looks set to stay, which would solve depth in attack but the England star’s future has not been confirmed.

Ideally, United would sell Joshua Zirkzee and sign proper support for Benjamin Sesko.

Meanwhile United have also revamped their goalkeeping depth with Andre Onana and Altay Bayindir loaned out and Radek Vitek sold, with free agent Karl Darlow arriving from Leeds to back up Senne Lammens.

VERDICT

United are in a distinctly better position than previously, having shifted on major wages.



Carrick has a younger, more athletic midfield core, a clear tactical direction and recruitment built on top-four stability.

But as the defeat at the weekend showed, the pressure could quickly ramp up if the new arrivals take time to gel.

Sports.title: Meet the new generation of Nepo babies set to conquer the football world, from an Arsenal kid to a rugby legend’s son
Sports.content:
IT’S nepotism, quite literally, at its finest.

These nepo babies are making a name for themselves in the football world.





From a teen who is rising up the ranks at Arsenal’s youth academy to a huge talent at Spurs tipped for the top, SunSport has unearthed the next generation of kids following in their famous parents’ footsteps.

Incredibly, one of them made their debut for Liverpool in the opening weekend of the 2026/27 Premier League season.

And another could play alongside his very famous dad in Saudi Arabia…

Gabriel Arteta

The 17-year-old son of Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta signed a scholarship contract with the Gunners in June 2026.

Gabriel, who is a winger, made his Under-18s debut in April of the same year against Reading in an U18 Premier League game.

He has since gone on to train with the U21 team.

The youngster previously travelled to Arsenal’s first-team pre-season training camp in the United States a couple of years ago.

Aged just 14 at the time, he did not take part in any sessions and instead watched from the sidelines with the coaching staff.





Phoenix Offiah

Big things are expected of the teenage son of rugby league icon Martin Offiah.

Phoenix, 16, is making huge waves at Tottenham’s academy, where he is a goalscoring machine.

The 6ft 2in forward found the net 26 times in youth football last term, and scored in the Under-16s Premier League Cup final win over Fulham.

Earlier this month, he bagged all four goals for the U18s in a 4-1 win over Wolves.

Dad Martin famously notched 501 tries during an incredible oval-ball career with Widness and Wigan, so he’s got some way to go.

Cristiano Ronaldo Jr

It’s some pressure to follow in the footsteps of your dad when he’s won the Ballon d’Or five times.



But, Cristiano Jr doesn’t appear to be fazed. The 16-year-old is already playing for Saudi Pro League outfit Al-Nassr’s youth team, taking on penalty and free kick duties and scoring plenty of goals.

Of course, his dad plays for the senior team – and it has been suggested that the pair could eventually line up together, unless Cristiano Ronaldo does retire in 2027.

However, Cristiano Jr is his own man and has received call-ups to Portugal’s national youth teams at U15 and U16 level.

Kai Rooney

Wayne Rooney’s son Kai, 16, is on the books at Man Utd and was flying in their U18s, before a foot injury set him back last season.

But, he is now fit and raring to go after recently competing in the eight-team Otten Cup in Eindhoven with the Red Devils’ youth side.

A speedy winger, Kai broke into Darren Fletcher’s Under-18s as a 15-year-old in January.

He scored two goals and laid on one assist in six U18 Premier League fixtures.

Time will tell if football is his calling, but proud mum Coleen Rooney revealed last week that Kai had also passed all his GCSEs.



Lewis Koumas

With Liverpool trailing Newcastle 2-1 in their Premier League opener, a forward with a familiar last name entered the fray.

It was Lewis, son of Premier League cult hero Jason Koumas, who turned out for West Brom and Wigan in the top flight, who the Reds turned to for a goal in the 78th minute from the bench.

Now 20, Lewis enjoyed a successful loan at Hull City in the Championship – as they gained promotion to the Premier League – last season.

He has also been capped 12 times by Wales.

Jacey Carrick

Another Premier League manager with his son in his club’s academy is Michael Carrick.

Jacey stars in the same Man Utd youth side as Kai Rooney, in what must be a nepo babies U18s super-team.



The 16-year-old signed scholarship terms with the Red Devils in the summer and is cut from a similar cloth to his dad.

According to United fan site United In Focus, he is a defensive midfielder with the ability to dictate the tempo of a game.

Jack and Tyler Fletcher

Proving to be the ultimate nepo babies youth set-up, Man Utd also boast the very talented Fletcher twins, Jack and Tyler, 19.

They controversially joined the club from Man City in 2023, and are both midfielders.

Jack made his debut for the first team as a substitute against Aston Villa in December 2025.

Tyler appeared for the first time in February 2026 against Tottenham.

Their appearance made history. It is the first time a set of twins and their father have ever played in the top flight since it began in 1888.



Elijah Upson

Another nepo baby to make headlines this summer was Elijah, who snubbed a deal at Spurs and signed a professional contract with Arsenal in July.

He is following in the footsteps of his dad, Matthew Upson, who played 56 times for the Gunners from 1997 to 2003.

An U18 England international, the ball-playing defender is considered a very promising talent.

The likes of Man City, Chelsea, Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund, and more were all said to be interested in signing the 18-year-old.

Damian Cech

Dad Petr Cech was one of the Premier League’s greatest ever goalkeepers.

So, son Damian has some huge gloves to fill.



But he has plenty of talent inherited from his old man, and signed his first first professional contract with Fulham in July 2025.

Last season, he became a hero on loan at Epsom & Ewell, where he saved two penalties in a shootout and won Player of the Match on his debut.

He also turned out for the Czech U18 team at just 15.

Lorenz and Tate Ferdinand

Lorenz and Tate, sons of England and Man Utd legend Rio Ferdinand, are both on the books at Brighton.

20-year-old Lorenz is a goalkeeper, who joined the Seagulls aged 12. He spent last season on loan at Havant & Waterlooville, but has returned to star for Brighton’s U21’s.

18-year-old Tate, who has been described as a natural leader, plays as a centre back, like dad Rio.

He signed a pro contract this summer and is captain of the U18s.



Beau Redknapp

Beau, 17, can count on two generations of his family playing football at the highest level.

Grandad Harry starred for West Ham in the 60s and 70s, while dad Jamie came through the ranks at Liverpool, before moving to Spurs.

Oh and there’s another big name superstar in the family… Frank Lampard is Beau’s second cousin.

Beau, whose mum is singer Louise, signed a scholarship deal with Brentford for the 2025-26 season.

An intelligent midfielder, he recently earned headlines for the Bees – scoring twice in a 4-2 defeat to Southampton in the U18s Premier League.

Which one of these talents do you think will make it?

Sports.title: Michael Owen admits Liverpool star is 'running out of excuses' after latest showing
Sports.content:
Michael Owen admits Liverpool star is 'running out of excuses' after latest showing

Alexander Isak led the line in Liverpool's draw at Newcastle with the Swede again underwhelming as Michael Owen insists the striker has to start producing

View 2 Images Michael Owen is running out of patience with Alexander Isak (Image: 2023 Getty Images)

Michael Owen says Alexander Isak is "starting to run out of excuses" after the Liverpool striker produced another below par performance.

‌



The Swede led the line for the Reds as they drew at Newcastle, in what was Isak's first return to St James' Park. The forward proved himself to be among the world's best strikers when he was with the Magpies, which prompted Liverpool to pay a record £125million for him.

‌



Isak endured an injury-hit first season at Anfield, which limited his involvement and meant he only scored four times. Now he's enjoyed the benefit of a pre-season ahead of his second year at Liverpool, with onlookers now adamant he has to produce.

‌



Owen was once Liverpool's main poacher and knows first hand how challenging it can be to recover from injury. However he believes time is running out to afford Isak any leeway following his latest below par showing.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Owen told talkSPORT: "I had plenty of injuries in my career so I know how hard it is to get back and you do need a bit of time. We’ve given him time, everyone has given him time and understood that. But he’s finished the season, then he’s gone to the World Cup and now he’s had a pre-season and you just think OK, now we’re starting to run out of excuses.

‌



"We need to see the real Isak and we know how good he is. Wow, we saw him for Newcastle and he’s absolute class. We haven’t seen it for Liverpool just yet and questions will come now. As I say, always give him the benefit of doubt in the past but at the start of this season we’re expecting.

‘Liverpool absolutely need him, they’ve lost Salah, Ekitike is out, there’s not that many options in attacking areas. They absolutely need him in top form and yesterday he was far from it, I thought he was a yard off and that’s worrying."

View 2 Images Alexander Isak struggled to have an impact in Liverpool's draw at Newcastle

‌



Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai were the two men on target for Liverpool. Isak, who was regularly booed by the Newcastle crowd, had his best chance in the second-half, but blazed over from the edge of the area.

Isak scored 62 times in his three years at Newcastle but has never looked like replicating that form whilst at Anfield. Liverpool are looking to justify their outlay, especially with Hugo Ekitike, who cost around half Isak's fee, scoring 17 times in his debut season.

Man Utd can still sign Myles Lewis-Skelly as Arsenal open door to transfer

Myles Lewis-Skelly has been the subject of interest from Manchester United this summer, and the Red Devils are still reportedly hopeful of signing the Arsenal midfielder

View Image Myles Lewis-Skelly could be on the verge of an exit from Arsenal (Image: Justin Setterfield, Getty Images)

Manchester United are still keen on signing Myles Lewis-Skelly this summer, as per reports. And the Red Devils have been given a glimmer of hope in that Arsenal are willing to sell under a strict condition.

‌



Michael Carrick has been looking for reinforcement in midfield and at left-back this summer, two positions in which Lewis-Skelly thrives. Although, with Carlos Baleba set to arrive at Old Trafford imminently following the striking of a £70million deal with Brighton and Hove Albion, it appears as though the left-hand side of defence is now United's priority.

‌



A move for Lewis-Skelly seemed clear cut when Arsenal brought in Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United in a £75m move earlier this month, threatening the 19-year-old's prospects of playing in the heart of midfield.

‌

It had previously been assumed that Lewis-Skelly was firmly off the table at the Emirates Stadium, but recent developments point in a different direction, with just over a week remaining in the summer transfer window.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk sends Liverpool chiefs transfer message with Andoni Iraola in agreement
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk sends Liverpool chiefs transfer message with Andoni Iraola in agreement

Liverpool have one week left to make more signings, with Andoni Iraola yet to get his hands on the marquee winger that he's been craving since taking over at Anfield

View 3 Images Virgil van Dijk wants a stronger dressing room (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

Virgil van Dijk wants to see Liverpool make 'quality' signings in the final week of the transfer window. It comes after Reds boss Andoni Iraola promised fans that the club will 'definitely' add to their squad before next Monday's 11pm deadline, having admitted in pre-season that he needed more options.

‌



Liverpool have only made one permanent signing this summer in the form of Victor Munoz, with Ronald Araujo's move from Barcelona only a loan and their £60million deal for Jeremy Jacquet being agreed with Rennes back in February. Iraola has been desperate to sign a winger all window, with Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola top of his shortlist.

‌



But with PSG demanding £145million, Liverpool are being forced to consider alternatives. The Reds saw two bids for Brighton star Yankuba Minteh rejected last week, the latest of which was £60m.

‌



Speaking after Liverpool's dramatic 2-2 draw away to Newcastle on Sunday, Van Dijk affirmed that he has 'full trust' in the club to get their recruitment right The Reds captain also made it clear that he and his team-mates need to shoulder the responsibility for improving on last season's 'very unacceptable' campaign.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Everyone wants to see quality arrive regardless," Van Dijk said. "I fully trust the club and the board to make the right decisions, that's the only thing I can say. Let's see what they do.

"Regardless of what happens, we are Liverpool and we have to give everything. For us, we have to show a reaction from last year. We have nothing to prove to the outside world, in my opinion. It is to ourselves. The way we train, the way we approach games, it is down to us to show a reaction.

"Last year it was very unacceptable, but that was last year. I don't want to talk about that - we are looking forward and looking to improve. Hopefully, next week it will be very close to what [Iraola] wants us to do."

‌



Having snatched a point at Newcastle in their first outing, Liverpool continue in the Premier League with a home game against Nottingham Forest in Saturday's early kick-off. And Van Dijk knows that their new manager will make sure they've put in the hard yards on the training ground first.

Who should Liverpool sign before the transfer window closes? Let us know your pick in the comments section.

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is still waiting on a winger (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

‌



"Like I say, we work on it every day," the Dutchman reiterated. "We do long hours on the training ground and that will only benefit all of us, including our loyal and trusted supporters. It is so early in the season that if we start panicking regardless of what could have happened today then we won't be in a good place.

"It is down to us to make sure we improve quickly, and that is what we try to do on the training ground. There were some good things, but also things that we have to improve.

"I think if we have to answer questions from the outside world, I don't think that's on us. What we have to do as players at Liverpool Football Club is be much better than we were last year. That is the responsibility everyone has to feel.

‌



View 3 Images Liverpool have bid £60million for Yankuba Minteh (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images)

"Obviously, there are some changes that are happening in the club and that is clearly visible. Some players have left, some players have come to the club, and it is down to us to be as good as we can as soon as possible, and challenge on all four fronts, hopefully as soon as possible.

"I think it is absolutely normal in any type of profession or work that if you come in new and you have new plans and ideas that it takes a bit of time. It is down to us to do it as soon as we can. We want to improve, we want to win, we want to do better. That is what we are going to try and do from tomorrow."

Sports.title: Arsenal's brutal treatment of three stars can unlock more signings for Mikel Arteta
Sports.content:
In the build-up to Arsenal’s first game of the season, three players were very noticeable by their absence. Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Fabio Vieira left on the sidelines just waiting while their futures are resolved.

This is the cruel nature of football. They have been left out in the cold, knowing realistically they would not be involved. Like many other managers, Mikel Arteta often does “shape” the day before a game and so if you are not involved, you know you will not even make the bench.

Sadly for Martinelli, he was left doing keepy-uppies while the rest did a final training session and the ever-popular Brazil winger is clearly on his way out. Martinelli is a really nice, likeable character who has been hanging around with Vieira quite a bit while the Portugal midfielder - almost a forgotten man - waits for his next move.

Jesus has a year left on his contract and it has been his ambition to play 10 years in English football - which would also help his residency status - and being a free agent next summer would also open more doors for him.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

It feels particularly harsh on Martinelli but, realistically, there has been a general acceptance since the end of last season that - if the right deal comes along - then he could go. Inter Milan have flirted with Martinelli but would struggle to meet his current contract and now, having been reluctant at first to move to the Saudi Pro League, there is a real chance of Al-Hilal now completing a move.

Jesus has been a target for Napoli while Hamburg are pushing to get a deal done for Vieira. If all three go, then Arsenal may yet do more in the market. They are monitoring Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz while Arteta loves Julian Alvarez, even though the Atletico Madrid forward looks unlikely at this point.

‌



But that story may yet have legs because the Atletico fans have turned on Alvarez and suddenly they may have to sell. Watch this space. Meanwhile, why on earth have they not been able to get better value on Martinelli? If Savinho goes to Tottenham in an £85m deal, why is Martinelli cheaper? The £50m price just does not seem enough.

Who should Arsenal sign and sell before the deadline? Have your say in the comments section.

5 View 5 Images Fabio Vieira is a target for ex-loan club Hamburg (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images) 5 View 5 Images Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus both have options (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images)

‌



This is a player whose stats measure up against the likes of Yildiz. So any deal has to actually be worth it - rather than just for the sake of it. Spending £100m to keep fans happy would be a bad move. Spending it on the right player would bolster the squad.

Martinelli has pace, is dangerous but has he really kicked on in the past two seasons? Let’s be honest, fans have been quick to turn on him so there is an element of revisionism here. Also, this notion that he has been kept in the dark… One former player was less sympathetic than some. “This is elite sport - every player knows what happens. If you want to improve, win trophies, that’s life.”

Where that argument falls down is with Myles Lewis-Skelly. But what does being offered actually mean? It might be that his name cropped up in conversations with other agents around the Bruno Guimaraes deal. IIf you know agents, they will always try to do deals. The first question will be: who will leave to make way - and can they muscle in and find a club to get the commission?

5 View 5 Images Juventus' Kenan Yildiz is a target (Image: Ivan Romano/Getty Images) 5 View 5 Images Julian Alvarez only wants to join Barcelona (Image: Sheng Cheng/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



The reality is that Lewis-Skelly did not play much last season - until his amazing transformation in the run-in. Now it would be unthinkable to sell. But at some point, Arsenal’s owners do want to balance the books and that is pure financial planning, getting a balanced squad and being responsible rather than being in danger of breaking the Profit and Sustainability Rules.

Ethan Nwaneri was another obvious candidate. But he has been so good in pre-season that he has moved up the pecking order. If he goes, it will be on loan rather than permanent. And ideally Arsenal want a good Premier League if they sanction a loan.

It is not a shock to see players being linked with Turkey after Leandro Trossard’s move to Besiktas. Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta clearly has good links there - what’s wrong with that?

Arsenal now have a huge, strong squad. And it would not be a huge surprise if they do not do more business. Ezri Konsa was a great signing. Terrific defender, brilliant personality.

‌



But if Arsenal can do business, there may yet be more deals to be done.

Sports.title: Premier League clubs get transfer wake-up call as top-four hopefuls exposed
Sports.content:
The Premier League's opening weekend provided some telling signs as each club's summer business - the ins and the outs - were magnified.

Arsenal remain the club to catch but several of their rivals were dealt reality checks. Manchester United and Aston Villa were top four finishers last season but both opened their campaigns with a defeat.

Michael Carrick's side were stunned at newly promoted Hull despite their midfield recruits being present. Unai Emery has seen his Europa League winners gutted amid talk of a need for transition, but Villa were ripped apart at Brighton with more exits on the cards.

Liverpool's midfield deficiencies were exposed at Newcastle, who themselves showed plenty of promise after summer that saw their top players leave, casting doubt over the project at St James' Park.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Chelsea and Fulham will round out the weekend on Monday night, they're yet to show their hand, but whilst there's no need to panic after one game the weekend's action certainly showed that some teams may have more work to do than they realised.

Mirror Football's writers takes a look at which club will need to have a massive week as the summer transfer window draws to a close.

Nathan Ridley - Aston Villa

It may seem obvious but it's impossible to ignore the scale of Villa's task in the final week of the window. Not only have they lost Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, there's a real possibility that Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez could follow them out the exit door.

‌



Although Sunday's drubbing at the hands of Brighton was probably a freak result, the warning signs were there. The biggest reason they need to make signings and do their best to retain both Watkins and Martinez is to keep Unai Emery happy.

View 5 Images Unai Emery could end up losing six of his Europa League-winning starting XI

Leaving the Spaniard with a threadbare squad on their return to the Champions League could cause him to lose faith in Villa's ambitions at a time when his stock is at an all-time high. There aren't many clubs in world football who'd turn Emery down, and he remains Villa's greatest asset.

John Cross - Liverpool

With just over a week to go of the transfer window, Liverpool are most in need of reinforcements. This is a crossroads moment for Andoni Iraola because they so obviously need new signings to be a club challenging for the title this season.

‌



Without major new recruits, Liverpool would be in serious danger of falling away with the season becoming all about a scrap for a Champions League place.

Liverpool boss Iraola was a really exciting appointment because he plays with intensity, pace and speed. It feels obvious that Liverpool need more in central midfield and the wide areas.

View 5 Images Liverpool have chased Bradley Barcola all summer (Image: Getty Images)

There is no surprise that they want Bradley Barcola and Yankuba Minteh because they are fast, quick and dangerous wingers who would fit into the Iraola style.

‌



If they get one or both of those players then maybe Liverpool can step up into being genuine challengers but they do also lack something in midfield. Iraola is all about pressing, intensity and, at Newcastle, Liverpool lacked some of that energy to allow Florian Wirtz to really excel.

Sky pundit Gary Neville was spot on: Liverpool do need more from Wirtz and Alexander Isak this season. No-one can doubt Liverpool’s ambition or backing in the market.

Other clubs could do with the odd player. But not like Liverpool. For Liverpool, this is all about defining their season and immediate future. But they really need to invest again to stop the club flatlining this season. They are better than that.

James Whaling - Crystal Palace

Of all the results on the opening weekend, I think Crystal Palace's 2-0 defeat by Everton probably went under the radar.

‌



I fear for Palace. Their manager is untested in the Premier League, they have sold Maxime Lacroix to Chelsea and could yet lose Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta. The swap deal involving Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson is headscratching to say the least.

View 5 Images Jean-Philippe Mateta is looking to get out of Selhurst Park (Image: PA)

Everton fans will tell you they themselves need to do business before the window slams shut, so for them to swat aside Palace so easily should set alarm bells ringing. The Eagles have enjoyed probably the best couple of years in their history winning the FA Cup and UEFA Conference League. But with Europa League football to contend with as well as the grind of the top flight, their squad needs desperate reinforcements if they are to avoid a relegation scrap.

Sam Meade - Aston Villa

All this talk of a rebuild. It is only a rebuild if you bring in the type of quality you've let go, and the Europa League winners have simply not done that.

‌



Not only have they lost bucket loads of quality, but they've lost the continuity they'd enjoyed for so many years. Starting with Emi Buendia as your No 9 on the opening day of the season is just unforgivable, even if Ollie Watkins is seemingly taking matters into his own hands to force an exit.

Villa have punched above their weight to achieve what they have over the last three years or so, but they are now greatly under resourced. You cannot have your best manager in a generation and not give him the tools. It won't end well and they need to act with some serious conviction in the coming days.

Alex Richards - Brentford

There are a lot of teams that the opening day proved need to do some very good business in the coming week or so. Liverpool need another game-changer in attack, Spurs need all manner of help despite all the money they've spent already and Aston Villa, particularly if Ollie Watkins is becoming the latest out the exit door, pretty much need a new centre-back, No.10 and centre-forward.

View 5 Images Brentford could only be a signing away from securing a European spot

‌



But the one I'd really like to see make a move is Brentford. Go and get the kind of midfielder that will get you 10-15 goals this season. I don't care if you break your transfer record or find another uncut gem for a fraction of the cost. Just go and get someone that plugs straight into that midfield and will feast off the chaos that Kevin Schade, Igor Thiago and Dango Outtara cause in attack.

Because that Spurs win, the comparative ease with which they dealt with their London neighbours and the Bees ability to both go direct and now play on the floor, really more than they ever have before, tells me Keith Andrews' side can be in the Champions League mix.

They were't far off nabbing a European spot last term, only missing out on the final day. A midfielder who hits double figures would get them there.

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid dressing room stance on Julian Alvarez transfer noise as Arsenal chase heats up
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid dressing room stance on Julian Alvarez transfer noise as Arsenal chase heats up

Arsenal transfer target Julian Alvarez was booed on his return to action for Atletico Madrid with Jan Oblak speaking out on his situation

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez has the support of the Atletico Madrid squad after being booed amid his uncertain future (Image: (Photo by Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

Julian Alvarez has the support of the Atletico Madrid squad according to goalkeeper Jan Oblak after he was booed on his return. The Arsenal transfer target has been pushing for a move away but Atletico have no plans to sell to his dream club Barcelona which has opened the door for a return to the Premier League.

‌



The Argentine was absent for their La Liga opener earlier this week but was named in the squad for the visit of Villareal. Diego Simeone brought him on in the second half with Atletico scoring a late equaliser in front of their home supporters.

‌



While the majority of Atletico's players went around the pitch and clapped their fans, Alvarez was instructed to leave the pitch. As he trudged down the tunnel accompanied by club officials, he was heavily booed and jeered.

‌



Oblak has now spoken out on the incident and his future while also confirming he has the support of Atletico players despite the uncomfortable situation.

He told DAZN: "We all need to be united. Julian is here, he's with us in the team and while he's with us, we're going to support him and we want him in the best way.

"Unfortunately, it's a situation that isn't comfortable for anyone, but hopefully all that is sorted out and at the end of the season we can all be happy."

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

When pressed about the whistles directed at Alvarez and what advice he might offer him, Diego Simeone said: "I'm not here to give advice. What I have to do is concentrate on my work, which is, from a sporting sense, to give my best for Atletico Madrid.

"The only thing I know is that if Atletico Madrid want to win a title, we need to be together, we need to have forwards, and we need to have important forwards. And for that, we need to work on it as a result, everyone, on what we need."

‌



View 2 Images Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone has spoken about the Julian Alvarez situation

Simeone also disclosed that the decision to prevent Alvarez from approaching the home supporters came from senior figures at the club.

He added: "People at the club told me that the club decided he shouldn't go near the stands or the fans. It was the club's decision to keep him away and separate him so he could go to the locker room."

Article continues below

Atletico have no intention of selling to Barcelona and would apparently only authorise a transfer to Arsenal for a nine-figure sum.

The Gunners seem unlikely to meet that valuation, but offloading Gabriel Martinelli to Al Hilal for a record fee could provide them with sufficient funds to table a bid that Atletico might accept, given the Alvarez situation is becoming increasingly difficult to manage.

Sports.title: Jarrod Bowen could land Premier League return in £50m transfer despite contract vow
Sports.content:
Jarrod Bowen could land Premier League return in £50m transfer despite contract vow

Jarrod Bowen has pledged his future to West Ham but the winger is still the subject of Premier League interest as Crystal Palace consider a move

View 2 Images Jarrod Bowen only signed a new deal this summer, but could still have offers to leave West Ham (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

West Ham talisman Jarrod Bowen could be handed a route back into the Premier League with Crystal Palace eyeing a £50million bid.

‌



The forward has, so far, chosen to remain with the Hammers despite their relegation to the Championship. Bowen has more than proven himself to be top-flight quality, earning England caps whilst at the London Stadium, and has pledged his future to the club.

‌



The 29-year-old signed a new deal to continue captaining West Ham in the summer, but the Eagles are still ready to test his resolve by tabling an offer. The Hammers still need to toe the line financially and landing a sizeable transfer fee would prove beneficial, but Bowen remains their star man and is a fan favourite.

‌



Palace are ready to test the water and want Bowen to replace Ismalia Sarr, who is keen to leave for Galatasaray, reports The Sun. The Turkish side are looking to secure a £34m switch for a player who scored 21 times last term and is clearly pushing for the exit door.

New Eagles boss Pierre Sage left Sarr out of the squad that lost 2-0 at Everton on the opening weekend of the season and Galatasaray want to wrap up a deal within a week, which would leave Palace seeking a replacement.

Bowen scored 11 times for West Ham last season but the south Londoners have been long-time admirers of the Englishman. Palace were frontrunners to sign Bowen from Hull back in January 2020 before the Hammers ended up winning the race for his signature.

‌



West Ham supporters are already frustrated having seen their team, who were pre-season favourites for promotion, fail to win either of their two games.

View 2 Images Ismaila Sarr is looking to leave Crystal Palace

Charlton secured a 2-1 win at the London Stadium on Saturday. Taty Castellanos missed a stoppage-time penalty to rescue a point for West Ham and supporters were left puzzled as to why Bowen did not take it.

‌



The winger's legacy at the Hammers is secure - he was the man who scored the last-minute winner as the club won the UEFA Conference League back in 2023, which was their first European trophy since 1965.

Bowen has since come out and claimed he didn't want to leave the club off the back of a relegation, which motivated him to sign a new deal at West Ham.

Sports.title: England's Carse unavailable for Lord's Test after nightclub incident
Sports.content:
England fast bowler Brydon Carse has been withdrawn from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan at Lord's from Thursday following an incident outside a Derby nightclub that is being investigated by the Cricket Regulator.

Video footage emerged of a handcuffed Carse being led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship.

Carse was seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background.

England squad for second Test against Pakistan at Lord's Joe Root (captain), Gus Atkinson, Jofra Archer, Sonny Baker, Shoaib Bashir, Harry Brook, Jordan Cox, Ben Duckett, Matthew Fisher, Emilio Gay, Dan Lawrence, Ollie Pope, Ollie Robinson, Jamie Smith, Josh Tongue. The second Test is live on Sky Sports Cricket and Sky Sports Main Event from 10am on Thursday (11am first ball).

An ECB statement read: "Following a referral from the ECB, the Cricket Regulator have confirmed that they will investigate events on Saturday night in Derby. Brydon Carse will no longer be available for selection for the Second Men's Rothesay Test Match while this investigation is ongoing and the full facts are obtained."

Sonny Baker - who made his Test debut against New Zealand at The Kia Oval in June - replaces fellow seamer Carse in England's squad.

The Carse situation comes less than two weeks after new England captain Joe Root removed the midnight curfew that had been installed following a number of drink-related issues across the winter tours of New Zealand and Australia.

Image: Carse was seen in handcuffs outside a nightclub in Derby on Saturday night

Carse did not make the England XI for the thumping three-day win over Pakistan in the series-opening Test at Headingley and was subsequently released to play for Durham against Derbyshire, a game in which he took two wickets and scored 26 runs.

Carse was England's leading wicket-taker during their 4-1 Ashes hammering but has not played for his country since due to injury.

Another off-field issue for England to manage

The paceman's nightclub incident is another off-field episode for England to negotiate.

Image: Carse (pictured) has been replaced by Sonny Baker in England's squad

White-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer while out the evening before a one-day international in New Zealand last autumn.

Then, during The Ashes, an unverified video appeared to show batter Ben Duckett drunk while the team were on a mid-series break in the beach resort of Noosa.

Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson missed the second Test of the 2-1 home defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after breaking the curfew to attend a Chelsea nightclub as they celebrated victory in the first game of the series at Lord's.

Stokes and Atkinson were cleared of violent conduct but hit with written warnings after "breaching specific contractual obligations".

Root had called for his players to "be adults" while announcing the removal of the curfew, so the Carse situation will raise further questions about the side's relationship with alcohol.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England Test captain Joe Root explains why he has removed the curfew that was previously imposed on his England team

Broad: Carse 'pretty daft' to be caught up in nightclub incident

Speaking on his For the Love of Cricket podcast, before Carse's withdrawal from the squad for the second Test was announced, former England bowler turned Sky Sports pundit Stuart Broad said: "We can't really make a judgement apart from it being, whatever's happened, pretty daft.

"We'll wait and see. We don't know, it could have been 10 o'clock in the evening, it could have been two o'clock, but whatever.

"This is not really anything that anybody wants to be talking about any more, to be brutally honest."

Sports.title: What has gone wrong for Pakistan cricket with 'alarm bells ringing'?
Sports.content:
It must be hard being a Pakistan cricket fan right now.
