Both organisations are understood to reserve the right to take legal action against Football TV and whoever is supplying it with access to their matches.

An SPFL source said the league was investigating the matter in conjunction with its broadcasting distribution rights holder, Infront.

The EFL and SPFL declined to comment.

Sports.title: Chelsea change course with Alonso primed to banish the chaos of youth
Sports.content:
It is a necessary reset. Although it would be pushing it to say that Chelsea have switched from development centre to retirement home, even after the signings of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, there has been a clear shift in strategy this summer. Some grownups are in the room at last and, for Xabi Alonso, the hope is that bringing in more experience will help a squad still packed with youngsters show more composure when adversity strikes.

Discipline was a problem for Chelsea last season: they had 11 red cards in all competitions and a lot of the wounds were self-inflicted. Chelsea were impetuous, on the receiving end of too many bookings for dissent and prone to collapsing at the first sign of trouble. No wonder Alonso, who was the epitome of calm during his playing career, has focused on maintaining “emotional control” before opening his tenure as manager with Monday’s trip to Fulham.

It will be a test of Chelsea’s mentality. Craven Cottage has been the setting for some spectacular implosions during the BlueCo era, the path to two 2-1 victories for Fulham over their neighbours smoothed by João Félix earning a red card on his Chelsea debut in 2023 and by Marc Cucurella getting himself sent off after 22 minutes last season.

Chelsea need to change, and hiring Alonso was a tacit admission that their approach required fine-tuning. Internally there was a recognition that the club had undervalued the importance of aura when it came to hiring coaches.

They blundered with Graham Potter and Liam Rosenior, neither of whom were capable of standing the heat. Alonso is a different breed. The 44-year-old burnished his reputation by leading Bayer Leverkusen to the Bundesliga title in 2024 and he wowed Chelsea during his discussions over the role, so much so that they broke with the past by naming him manager rather than head coach.

Now the players can look to the dugout and see an authority figure. Alonso has not seized absolute power – he is still part of a wider structure, collaborating with an extensive recruitment team – but there is no doubt that his arrival has lent credibility to a project that was in danger of falling apart when the Rosenior experiment ended.

View image in fullscreen Liam Rosenior struggled at Stamford Bridge, lasting less than four months. Photograph: Javier García/Shutterstock

Of course, it remains to be seen if success in Germany means Alonso can dominate in England. Leverkusen was special but Real Madrid left him with a scar. Then again, the Bernabéu is not exactly where managers go to develop. It makes Álvaro Arbeloa, who stepped in at Madrid after Alonso’s sacking last season, a similar unknown after replacing Marco Silva at Fulham.

Yet there is optimism around Chelsea. Can they mount a title challenge for the first time in a decade? There is a lot of ground to make up after finishing 10th last season. Weaknesses linger, particularly in goal, and a push for the top four looks likelier.

However, no European football could be a blessing, giving Alonso more time in training. He looks tactically flexible. Chelsea switched between a back four and a back three during pre-season. Cucurella has joined Madrid but Marco Palestra, signed from Atalanta for £43m, and Pep Chavarría, a £16.3m arrival from Rayo Vallecano, could play as wingbacks.

The recruitment looks purposeful. After years of buying promising youngsters Chelsea have targeted ready-made players. Maxence Lacroix, the 26-year-old France centre-back, is a sensible signing from Crystal Palace. Morgan Rogers, signed from Aston Villa for £117m, can play in a range of positions in attacking midfield and could form an exciting partnership with a rested Cole Palmer, who has a point to prove after missing out on England’s World Cup squad.

There is talent here. There always has been, though. The flaw has more been around mindset. It is a footballing norm to have wise heads around to protect young players. Chelsea went too far in the opposite direction and it is one of the first areas Alonso has addressed.

Perhaps he has heard the tale of one of his predecessors having to deal with a player prioritising a haircut over a team meeting. Either way it did not feel on brand when Chelsea made an unsuccessful attempt to sign the 33-year-old Granit Xhaka from Sunderland in June. Yet it underlined their desire for more leadership and the box was ticked when Welbeck, 35, joined from Brighton in a cut-price deal and Henderson, 36, was brought in on a free transfer from Brentford.

View image in fullscreen New signing Danny Welbeck offers experience, maturity and a reliable source of goals. Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images

They could be canny moves. Perhaps there is an element of overkill, a sense of Chelsea taking their new direction too far, but Welbeck and Henderson still have something to offer. Welbeck scored 13 league goals for Brighton last season and will provide cover for João Pedro up front, while Henderson did not look out of place for Brentford and, according to Jude Bellingham, is someone coaching staff will always go to when there are problems to resolve.

Alonso needs order. There are still rumblings of instability off the pitch, with Todd Boehly and Mark Walter looking to sell their stakes in the club to the majority shareholder, Clearlake Capital. Quiet is rare. Chelsea need to shift a host of players before the transfer window shuts and questions hover over Enzo Fernández, who favours a reunion with Enzo Maresca at Manchester City.

There has been a lot of noise around Fernández. The midfielder has made no secret of his desire to leave but speaking out so much when Chelsea were wounded underlined the decline in standards. Alonso needs leaders. He needs trust. He still has to prove the hype is justified but his attempts to change Chelsea’s mentality is an encouraging first step.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 3: Birmingham City
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 12th (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 1st (WSL2)

Prospects

Founding members of the Women’s Super League when it launched in 2011, Birmingham are back in the top flight after four years in the second tier, having won promotion as WSL2 champions on the final day of last season. After a decent summer transfer window, Birmingham look to have a fighting chance of staying up, and perhaps even surprising a few teams, while off the pitch they are the best-equipped of the three promoted sides to cement themselves in the top division.

Forwards Lily Crosthwaite and Wilma Leidhammar and defender Neve Herron, are all 23-years-old and likely to continue improving. Birmingham have also added players with WSL experience, such as the former Brighton goalkeeper Sophie Baggaley and the centre-back Millie Turner.

Inconsistency was nearly their downfall last season; they won the most games in WSL2, but also lost six times. They delivered under pressure, boosted by the performances of Leidhammar after her club-record arrival in January, ensuring they avoided a repeat of the heartbreak of 12 months earlier when they missed out on promotion on the final day. Nonetheless, Birmingham are still a long way off from the days when they were runners-up in the top tier and their first two away fixtures are against Manchester City and Chelsea. They also host fellow promoted sides Crystal Palace and Charlton relatively early in the campaign and those home fixtures could be key to building confidence.

Off-field picture

Birmingham’s women’s team were sold to the club’s ownership group in February, with Shelby Companies Limited – an affiliate of Knighthead Capital Management – owning 97%. The remaining 3% was purchased by investors including the former England midfielder Karen Carney and the four-time grand slam tennis champion Kim Clijsters. The club appear to be in a relatively healthy position with ambitious owners determined to reestablish the 2012 FA Cup winners as a regular, competitive presence in the WSL. They train at the recently renovated Knighthead Performance Centre, on the same site as the men’s team’s former Wast Hills training base, with a new gym among other extensive refurbishments.

The manager

Amy Merricks has been in charge since April 2024 She holds a Uefa Pro Licence and was 30 years old when she was appointed by Birmingham. She has previously coached within the England youth setup as well as at Gillingham, Millwall and Brighton, where was stepped up to be interim manager three times.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Lisa Naalsund arrives from Manchester United to boost Birmingham’s midfield. Photograph: DeFodi Images/Getty Images

Birmingham have recruited players with international experience, including the Canada defender Marie Levasseur from Montpellier, but their two most eyebrow-raising additions are Turner and Lisa Naalsund from Manchester United. They were starting members of United’s FA Cup-winning side of 2024 and played in a Women’s Champions League quarter-final as recently as April. Naalsund will be an influential force in the midfield – she has won 39 caps and was part of Norway’s squad at last year’s Euros.

Stat attack

Birmingham topped WSL2 last season despite not scoring the most goals or conceding the fewest. One stat they led was big chances, Opta’s metric for opportunities where it is reasonable to expect the attacker to score. While their tally will be much harder to repeat in the top flight, their attacking process looks in good order.

Set for a breakthrough

There is plenty of excitement at Birmingham about another of their new signings, the 19-year-old France youth forward Chancelle Effa Effa, who arrived from Le Havre for a fee understood to be about €120,000 (£100,000) this month. She broke into Le Havre’s first team at the age of 15 and scored 17 times in 28 games for France’s Under-17 and Under-19 teams, having helped France win 2023’s Under-17 Euros.

What they say …

“We know it’s going to be a massive challenge, but it’s a challenge that, as players, you thrive upon. As long as we can take that togetherness, that relentlessness, into the games, I’m sure we’re going to be just fine” – Chelsea Cornet.

Where are they playing their home games?

Birmingham play their home fixtures at St Andrew’s, which has been the women’s team’s home since 2021. They set a club record attendance for a women’s game there on the final day of the 2024-25 season – 8,749. Long-term, the club have announced plans to build a new women’s team stadium as part of the ‘Sports Quarter’, which also includes the proposed 62,000-seater men’s team Powerhouse Stadium as well as an indoor arena, training ground facilities and a new railway station.

Sports.title: Ceferin brands Infantino’s failed World Cup plan as ‘even worse than the Super League’
Sports.content:
The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, has described Gianni Infantino’s doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup as “even worse than the Super League plan” and warned his embattled Fifa counterpart that he will face an opponent if he runs for re-election next March.

Ceferin has led Uefa’s firm collective stance against the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, which was shelved amid widespread opposition at the start of August. Uefa are pushing for Infantino to quit, also drawing on support from Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation, and are yet to drop a threat to boycott Fifa competitions while talks are under way with Concacaf to set up a combined Nations League tournament.

In an interview with the podcast The Rest is Politics: Leading, Ceferin denounced Infantino’s project as more damaging than the breakaway Super League that was shelved in 2021 after large-scale protests. “I think this plan is even worse than the Super League plan,” he said. “In the first case, super-important clubs wanted to do their own league, which is wrong and would destroy football. But in this case, football would be literally sold.

“I’m absolutely sure that the [FFE] plan is dead. For me, the most important thing is that we stopped another try to sell the sport. It’s hard to imagine what kind of people would sell the sport that belongs to everyone.”

Earlier this month it was reported that Infantino had held talks about running the Super League under Fifa branding. Ceferin is confident that any revival of that plan would be decades away. “It might happen in 20 years, you never know, but for now we cooperate with everyone in a great way. I’m sure it cannot happen in the next 10 years,” he said.

Infantino spent much of the weekend courting support from Concacaf members at a meeting in the Dominican Republic, infuriating many of those present. Ceferin, who revealed the pair had not been in contact since the FFE scandal broke, believes the Fifa president’s path to survival is narrowing.

“I didn’t speak with him, he didn’t contact me since this happened,” he said. “But there are two options. One option is that he realises that he doesn’t have the support, and that’s not only political support of the ones who vote, but the political support of the football community, the political support of fans, the political support of the players, former players, coaches.

“And the second option [is] that he goes to the elections in March, but in that case, I think he will have a candidate against him. I don’t know yet who.” The Concacaf president, Victor Montagliani, has been tipped as a potential opponent for Infantino if he chooses to run in Rabat.

Ceferin has proponents of his own but ruled out making his own bid for the Fifa presidency. “My credibility is much, much, much higher if I’m not interested in the position,” he said. The Slovenian is expected to run unopposed for a fourth term at the helm of Uefa, with the election due next April.

Asked whether Infantino had become too close to Donald Trump, with whom he forged a close relationship before the recent World Cup, Ceferin said: “To be honest, I think you are naive if you think that a politician like that, or any politician, is your good friend. The moment you are a problem, you stop being a friend of a politician.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

That friendship came under the spotlight last month when Trump said he had called Infantino to ask for a review of the red card given to the US striker Folarin Balogun, whose ban for the last-16 tie against Belgium was later suspended. “That was more than shocking,” Ceferin said. “We have rules and if you don’t respect your own rules, then the game doesn’t make any sense. That’s shocking and, trust me, almost everybody was shocked. Just not everybody dared to speak.”

Meanwhile, in a fresh show of European opposition to Infantino, the six Nordic football associations issued a statement saying they had “lost confidence in the Fifa president and have serious concerns about the governance and high-level decision making of the organisation”. They asked for binding assurances that Fifa will never again “open its governance or competitions to private ownership” and called for a full third-party review into the FFE scheme.

Earlier in August the Norwegian Football Federation was the first member association to call directly for Infantino to step down.

Infantino travelled straight from the Dominican Republic to Paris on Sunday, attending the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup. Television footage showed him exchanging greetings with the president of France, Emmanuel Macron.

Sports.title: 'I can answer only with my silence': Aston Villa boss Unai Emery hints Ollie Watkins refused to play for club in Brighton drubbing - as England striker's move to Saudi Arabia looms
Sports.content:
'I can answer only with my silence': Aston Villa boss Unai Emery hints Ollie Watkins refused to play for club in Brighton drubbing - as England striker's move to Saudi Arabia looms

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Unai Emery hinted heavily that Ollie Watkins had been reluctant to play for Aston Villa as they were hammered by Brighton amid interest in the striker from Al-Hilal.

Villa say they have rejected four offers from the Saudi Pro League club for Watkins, the latest of which is thought to be around £34million, a price the Premier League side will not sell at.

The England striker was not included in the squad for Villa’s 4-0 defeat even though the club’s only other forwards, Brian Madjo and Tammy Abraham, are out injured.

As far as Villa are concerned, it is understood Watkins is neither ill nor injured. However, he is not thought to have trained fully last week. Watkins representative has been contacted for comment.

On Watkins’ position, Emery answered: ‘This question is for him. I can answer only with my silence.’

Asked whether Watkins was refusing to play, Emery said: ‘I think you can call him, you can call his agent and he can respond.’ Did he feel let down by Watkins, who has improved greatly under Emery? ‘He can only explain his answer, I can’t. We had two strikers injured and another striker – it’s his answer.’

In one of their worst performances under Emery, new-look Villa were torn apart by Brighton, with Joao Gomes sent off on his Premier League debut for the club as the home side went 4-0 up in just over half an hour.

Ollie Watkins has been the subject of four bids from Al-Hilal this month

Unai Emery refused to elaborate on Watkins' future after he was left out of the squad beaten 4-0 by Brighton

Due largely to UEFA financial rules, Villa have sold about £250million worth of talent this summer. Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa have all departed, and Watkins and Emi Martinez (another absentee here) could follow. All six were mainstays of the Villa team who beat Freiburg 3-0 in May to lift the Europa League.

Villa have often struggled when the transfer window is open and Emery joked: ‘I think the transfer window should always be closed.

‘In the last three years, until the transfer window closes, we have had problems like we are having now. The players have the mentality I want – not complaining, not blaming, and trying to be patient, even with results like today.

‘We have had this problem (with the window) every season and we overcame it. But it’s something hard for us every year.’

Brighton have also lost key men and there are doubts about the futures of Yankuba Minteh, who boss Fabian Hurzeler says has an ankle injury, and Carlos Baleba. The pair are wanted by Liverpool and Manchester United respectively and did not feature.

Brighton were four up inside 31 minutes thanks to Victor Lindelof’s own-goal, Maxim De Cuyper’s tap-in and a rapid double from Jack Hinshelwood.

Hurzeler added: ‘The red card was another game changer and we played a mature second half, as it’s not that easy to find a good balance when you’re one man up. I was very happy with our performance.

‘Minteh has an issue with his ankle and he’s an important player for us but we saw today we were able to replace him. It’s important we don’t rely on one player.’

ends

Sports.title: Newcastle edge closer to signing Nico Gonzalez from Man City - as Newcastle rekindle interest in Lille forward Matias-Fernandez Pardo: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Gonzalez edges closer to Toon move Newcastle United are continuing to edge closer to agreement with Manchester City over a deal for Nico Gonzalez. Gonzalez is valued around £50million. The 24-year-old was an unused substitute in City’s win over Bournemouth on Sunday with Marc Guehi playing in midfield and it is clear that a move away may now be in his best interests. Nico Gonzalez is closing in on a move to Newcastle after falling out of favour at Man City Matthias Jaissle wants to add a midfielder with Premier League experience before the window closes. City agreed an £86m deal with Lille for midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi yesterday and want another before the window closes. Newcastle also admire Tottenham's Archie Gray though he has captained the side in pre-season and at the weekend in their 3-0 defeat to Brentford. Newcastle back in for Pardo Newcastle have rekindled talks over Lille forward Matias-Fernandez Pardo. The clubs have been discussing an offer worth around £40million for the Belgium international who can play across the front line. Daily Mail Sport has previously reported Newcastle's interest in the 21-year-old while Red Bull Leipzig and Atletico Madrid have made proposals recently too. Pardo was on Liverpool's watchlist previously and played for Belgium at the World Cup. Coventry pinning hopes on Pinnock Coventry are in talks to sign Ethan Pinnock from Brentford. The Jamaica international has been on the periphery of Keith Andrews' first team but has been attracting enquiries from a number of clubs including West Ham. However, Coventry manager Frank Lampard has recognised that the 33-year-old Pinnock's Premier League experience could benefit his side during what will be a testing season. If all goes well with talks, Pinnock could sign in the next 24 hours. Tigers target towering forward Hull are in talks for towering Union Berlin forward Ilyas Ansah. The Germany Under-21 international was considered for selection by Ghana ahead of the World Cup and Hull are offering £19m, including add-ons. The 21-year old is 6ft 6in tall and was a target for Besiktas earlier this year. He scored five goals and registered two assists in 26 games for Union Berlin last season. Hull had a £7m offer for Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas knocked back last week and are continuing to work on other options. Imps land Wheatley Manchester United striker Ethan Wheatley has joined Championship side Lincoln City. The 20-year-old agreed the move on Friday after seeing Everton pull out of a deal to sign him permanently earlier last week. Wheatley, who had a spell at Bradford last season, joins on loan for the rest of this campaign.

Sports.title: Brydon Carse dropped by England as investigation into nightclub incident - which saw him handcuffed by police - continues
Sports.content:
Brydon Carse dropped by England as investigation into nightclub incident - which saw him handcuffed by police - continues

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Brydon Carse has been dropped from England’s squad for Thursday’s second Test against Pakistan at Lord’s while the Cricket Regulator investigate the events that led to police handcuffing him outside a nightclub in Derby on Saturday.

Carse was quickly released without charge, with friends insisting he had done little wrong while out with team-mates celebrating Durham’s county championship victory over Derbyshire earlier in the day.

He has been replaced in the 16-man squad by Hampshire fast bowler Sonny Baker, who made his Test against New Zealand at The Oval in June.

A social-media video showed the moment Carse was handcuffed, with four policemen in attendance, and Durham team-mates Ben Stokes and Matthew Potts both featuring briefly on camera.

Brydon Carse has been replaced in the 16-man squad by Hampshire fast bowler Sonny Baker

And while Carse, who has not played a Test since the Ashes, was not arrested nor on England duty, he has an ECB central contract. After a year in which Harry Brook, Ben Duckett and Stokes have been involved in separate alcohol-related incidents, the sight of another England cricketer making headlines for the wrong reasons has not gone down well at Lord’s.

The ECB have now referred the case to the independent Cricket Regulator, who will investigate the events of Saturday night.

An ECB statement said: ‘Brydon Carse will no longer be available for selection for the Second Men’s Rothesay Test Match while this investigation is ongoing and the full facts are obtained.’

The Cricket Regulator has at its disposal a range of options, including no further action, caution or bringing a charge for a breach of the regulations – among them, bringing the game into disrepute.

Sports.title: New £18m Chelsea signing's WAG left terrified and trapped by a SQUIRREL - after ChatGPT told her it could attack - amid struggles with move to London
Sports.content:
The girlfriend of one of Chelsea's new stars came face-to-face with a sinister squirrel on one of her first days in London.

And the encounter left her shook like never before, to the extent that the ordeal required a 90-second TikTok debrief.

Influencer Pawgli, who has been dating £18million full-back Pep Chavarria since November, has moved to the English capital despite severe reservations over the switch.

In her previous videos, she spoke about the 'scary' prospect of leaving Madrid and the opportunities and family she has there.

Pawgli, 27, has more than 1.1 million followers on TikTok and creates fashion, beauty, and lifestyle content in Spanish.

But after taking the plunge with Chavarria, she has encountered a foe more fearsom ethan she could ever imagine: a furry chipmunkesque rodent, positioned menacingly on the path.

'How a 50-minute walk ended up taking an hour and a half... because of a squirrel,' she began in a TikTok video.

The influencer girlfriend of a new Chelsea star has recounted her horror at meeting a squirrel

She shared a picture of the offending rodent with her 1.1 million TikTok followers

Pawgli, the girlfriend of new Chelsea signing Pep Chavarria, was torn about moving to London

'But I was going to tell you about the other day when I made a vlog for you going to get my nails done in London for the first time. You have no idea everything that happened to me.

'Of course, we're still in the hotel because they don't give Pepo the house until the 28th.

'So I went to get my nails done; Google Maps showed 50 minutes to get to the nail place, but I thought, "go on, I'll walk a bit, get to know the area, etc."

'I had been walking for 45 minutes, okay? Because it took me through places that were just woods, woods, woods, and surrounded by lakes... super pretty landscapes, yes, but all forest, as if I were in the Hansel and Gretel movie.

'All kinds of animals popped up, and when I had only 20 minutes left to reach the nail place - and I was almost out of the forest because I could already see civilization - a squirrel in the middle of the path wasn't moving. Staring at me like this...

'I asked ChatGPT, "Do squirrels attack?" And it said, "Yes." And I... backed away.

'Wait until it leaves and don't pass through there," etc. That's what ChatGPT told me. I waited for about 10 or 15 minutes... and the squirrel wouldn't leave.

'I decided to turn all the way back the way I came, and I saw another path - also all forest -and I said, "Okay, I'll go through here," and the whole route recalculated, making me walk an hour and a half instead of 50 minutes.

The duo have been together since November last year but she may decide to continue the relationship long-distance

She broke down in tears, has described the situation as 'scary', and says she is 'panicking'

Perhaps the influencer has not encountered many squirrels before in Madrid, where their population has dwindled.

It is an uncomfortable start for Pawgli, who had been seriously weighing up whether or not to join her footballer boyfriend in London or continue their relationship long-distance from Madrid.

In one video, she broke down in tears at the situation.

She said: 'By moving to London, I'm kind of giving up on doing 100 per cent of my job. He has his job, I have mine; he earns his money, I earn mine. Nobody lives off anyone else; I don't live off my boyfriend.

'Therefore, by not living in Madrid, I'm losing opportunities - opportunities for me to keep growing in this - because absolutely everything is in Madrid.

'I want to keep holding on to my Spanish audience. I don't know how to speak English, at least right now, though I know I'll have to learn.

'But no matter how much English I know, I don't want to change my audience and have an English-speaking audience. I want to stay with my Spanish audience, which is why, all things considered, living in Madrid is so good for me.

'As someone who is ultra mega family-oriented and super sensitive, moving to a country I don't know, where I have nothing, no life, no job, and where I'm going to lose career opportunities...

Pawgli says she does not want to abandon her Spanish-speaking audience

The 27-year-old is 'mega-happy' for her partner but did not want to leave her family behind

'And I'm doing it out of love, because I love my partner and want to build a future and a family with him.'

Pawgli denied that she had broken down in tears over the prospect of losing work and going to free events in Madrid.

But in another video, she did clearly indicate that she is in some turmoil about the change.

Chavarria, a late bloomer who only made his LaLiga debut aged 24, has spent the last four seasons with Madrid-based club Rayo Vallecano.

Pawgli said: 'I have my life in Madrid; I have my job in Madrid, which luckily is going very, very well. I have projects, I have all the brands I work with there, I have daily events, I have my sister, my family, my friends. I have a life where I feel fortunate - it's a dream life for me and one that cost me a lot to build.

'So, when you start a relationship and your partner gets an opportunity like this, you're obviously ultra-mega happy for him and super proud of him, but you also have to sit down with yourself and think, "Okay, now what do I do?"

'And I swear until recently I was completely convinced that I wasn't going to move in with him. He has his life in London right now, I have mine in Madrid; I respect his life, he respects mine, and whenever possible, we'll see each other.

'A long-distance relationship. Something I would've never considered in my life, but if one thing was clear to me, it's that I will never in my life depend on anyone or live off anyone. I have my own income, and that's how it'll always be.

Pawgli, who has 1.1 million TikTok followers, insists that she wants a family with Chavarria

'All of this is scary for someone who has everything in Madrid. Right now I'm panicking, honestly, because I know it's a very tough decision.

'I also want to be able to experience this with Pep, because if I met my boyfriend and he's been here in Madrid for like 4 years and I met him, and precisely this year he has to go to London, maybe it's because fate also wants me to go.

'Because I'm obviously going to make content for you wherever I go, and being in London I can do even more, right? Because there are things there that aren't in Spain.

'I have a thousand ideas in my head because I can't stop thinking, honestly.'

Pawgli has never revealed her actual name and the nickname is apparently based off the Jungle Book character Mowgli.

Sports.title: Journey to Wembley: After a fortnight of fretting over floodlights on the fritz, Nelson's FA Cup journey ends at Witton Albion - where home fans toasted victory with pina coladas!
Sports.content:
It’s the annual pina colada festival in the Witton area of Cheshire – the song about the drink, which topped the US charts in the late 1970s, was written by someone local to the place and they’ve spotted the commercial opportunity – so there are people walking around dressed as pineapples and wearing big yellow glasses on Saturday lunchtime. But life has not exactly been a cocktail party for Nelson, an East Lancashire ninth tier club, just lately.

They breeze through one of the challenges which faces them after arriving to face opponents one step above them in the pyramid. Their new yellow away kits for the season haven’t arrived and last season’s issue, which they’re still using, don’t have a No 18 jersey – needed today because you’re allowed seven subs in the FA Cup. Someone finds a white marker pen and inks the number on to a plain yellow away shirt. Wearing numbers on your back is mandatory in the tournament.

This is a minor obstacle compared with the floodlight problems which have been testing Nelson minds since we left them celebrating extra preliminary round victory at their ‘Little Wembley’ ground two weeks ago. That was the first part of our journey to Wembley told in 13 instalments, following a club as far as they go and then picking up with the team who knock them out, all the way to the final.

They’d signed off on a £30,000 contract, helped by FA grants, to replace the system of lights which had started to fail during evening games, only to find that the new ones still didn’t work.

The approved contractors didn’t seem to have mentioned that the cables and wiring supplying the lights also needed ripping out, and yet were sending the club legal letters demanding payment, as Nelson’s directors sought advice from the FA about the black hole they risked disappearing into.

Inside the home dressing room at the Bedspace Trust Community Stadium

Nelson captain Bill Priestley receives some treatment ahead of kick-off

A home steward - proudly sporting Witton Albion's colours - tucks into a pie at half-time

When we caught up with Nelson at their league away game at Charnock Richard in Lancashire, last Tuesday night, the floodlights were the prime topic of conversation as the players arrived in the car park. There had even been talk of a temporary ground move, which did not exactly delight the North West Counties League. Nelson’s proactive club sponsor Monks Contractors had offered supplying temporary structures.

In the end, they just went to work again. Volunteers helped dig two 100m trenches to lay the new cabling to the new lights and on Wednesday, they flicked the switch once more. ‘Let there be light?’ The look on Nelson director Rob Doherty’s face as the visiting contingent are welcomed into Witton’s snug little boardroom suggests so. ‘As of three days ago, they were working,’ he relates. The FA provided emergency funding.

Both these teams badly want to win this FA Cup Preliminary Round game. In his extremely modestly proportioned office Witton manager Benny Harrison, whose day job is a teacher at a special educational school, reflects at 2pm on the profound effects Marine experienced after playing Tottenham in the Third Round in 2021. The windfall helped win them two promotions in three years.

But as the rival teams’ executives gather in that boardroom, there’s a sense of mutual empathy about the existential threats which can be just around the corner for any non-league club.

‘There’s what goes on out on the pitch, and the fans and all that the lovely stuff,’ says Witton director Paul Sanderson, when Nelson relate their floodlight troubles. ‘And then there’s survivability stuff that fans don't know about. Trying to navigate things that can threaten your existence if you’re not prepared for anything.’

Nelson were on a precipice before new co-owners Stewart Fort and Chris Price arrived three years ago, invested and built up the team of volunteers who are their lifeblood. But Witton’s excellent little club museum, charting a 139-year history and signposted ‘probably the best non-League football museum in the world’, shows that they’ve also ridden football’s rollercoaster.

The museum chronicles the club’s journey to the 1992 FA Trophy final at Wembley, where they lost to Colchester. That period, which included a brief stay in the Conference, saw them splashing the surplus earned after selling their old ground to Sainsburys and building a new one, on players. The rewards were painful temporary. Witton struggled when the money ran out and the new stadium required major repair sooner than anticipated.

The sun’s out, though, and the FA Cup is blowing everyone’s troubles away. ‘Welcome to the best football competition in the world by a long chalk,’ states the stadium announcer. The appropriately named Witton groundsman James Spruce is reversing his mower out onto the excellent playing surface, his partner Katy Hulse is nursing a pina colada and her friend Barbara Bazley is watching the warm-up.

Groundsman James Spruce applies the finishing touches to the playing surface

Katy Hulse (left) enjoys a pina colada with her friend Barbara Bazley

Albion statistician Phil Chadwick has helped to curate one of the best club museum's in non-League

Nelson's 87-year-old superfan Harry Manning’s immaculate handwritten notes will be converted into a match report for the local Nelson Leader

‘When you make s*** decisions, it goes pear-shaped, so if someone makes a s*** decision, back them up and help sort it out,’ shouts assistant coach Liam Lishman, as he puts the squad through their paces. Thursday’s training session focussed on not allowing Freddie Garbutt, Witton’s towering 22-year-old striker, the chance to control and shoot.

At Charnock Richard, Nelson won 2-0, led by their own dangerous target man Sefton Gonzalez, who scored and hurled himself through his trademark somersault. Today, goalkeeper Chris Thompson is back after a bout of sciatica. There’s optimism in the air.

Against the backdrop of the chemical plants in salt-mining territory, Nelson discover what they’re up against in Garbutt and Witton’s attacking pace.

Nelson wing-back Darren Holden, outstanding in the previous round and at Charnock in midweek, is operating in his own half far more, protecting Nelson territory, yet removing one of the Lancashire team's attacking dimensions.

Jamie Edwards, Nelson’s force field, draws a sharp save and Gonzales has just headed a great opportunity into the ground when Witton’s Garbutt leaps to meet a corner and send his team ahead.

He’s one of only two players Witton have signed up to a contract, protecting his match fee if he’s injured and protecting the club if someone else tries to sign him, Witton chairman Graham Wood relates, back in the boardroom at half-time.

The winners today will collect £1,444 in prize money and that would be just as precious to Witton, a fan-owned club with 400 registered shareholders, none of them hugely wealthy, who are currently trying to make a community football facility.

Nelson players warm up at the side of the pitch before kick-off

Witton Albion play in the Northern Premier League Division One West, one division higher than Nelson

Visiting goalkeeper Chris Thompson keeps a Witton player at bay

Freddy Garbutt's first-half goal settled the game and sent Witton through to the next round of the FA Cup

Home boss Ben Harrison addresses his players at full time

‘That will bring us an income to put back into the club,’ says Wood, who has helped bring a commercial sponsorship deal with a locally based homelessness charity.

Nelson dominate a second half in which Holden is pushed forward more, encouraged by his wife Abi, who is live tweeting the match for the club’s website with another volunteer, Amy Holden, and taking photographs for next week’s match programme and the website.

In the main stand, 87-year-old superfan Harry Manning’s immaculate handwritten notes, which will be converted into a match report for the local Nelson Leader, reflect the growing frustration. The ‘18’ inked onto sub James Hooper’s jersey is impressive. But it’s raining in Nelson hearts when the whistle blows and they tumble out of the competition.

Manager Arron Ripley stands in the sun-dappled centre circle ten minutes later and reflects on the way his ambitious side are evolving. ‘Last year we’d have kept launching it in a situation like that but we’re looking after the ball. We look like we’re enjoying it. We just weren’t clinical enough.’

Nelson can return fortified to their league campaign, confident, in so many ways, that the lights will stay on.

Sports.title: Aston Villa fans turn on Ollie Watkins and wife Ellie after manager hinted he REFUSED to play to force £34m move to Saudi Arabia's Al-Hilal
Sports.content:
Aston Villa fans turn on Ollie Watkins and wife Ellie after manager hinted he REFUSED to play to force £34m move to Saudi Arabia's Al-Hilal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Aston Villa fans have expressed their anger after Unai Emery hinted that Ollie Watkins refused to play amid speculation over his future.

Watkins, 30, was left out of Villa's squad for their 4-0 defeat by Brighton on Sunday in their first Premier League game of the season despite the club’s only other forwards, Brian Madjo and Tammy Abraham, being out injured.

Villa say they have rejected four offers from Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal for Watkins, the latest of which is thought to be around £34million, a price the Premier League side will not sell at.

As far as Villa are concerned, it is understood Watkins is neither ill nor injured. However, he is not thought to have trained fully last week. Daily Mail Sport contacted Watkins' representative for comment on Sunday.

Speaking after the game on Watkins’ position, Emery answered: ‘This question is for him. I can answer only with my silence.’

Asked whether Watkins was refusing to play, Emery said: ‘I think you can call him, you can call his agent and he can respond. He can only explain his answer, I can’t. We had two strikers injured and another striker – it’s his answer.’

Aston Villa fans have hit out at Ollie Watkins (pictured with wife Ellie) amid speculation over his future

Several fans expressed their anger at Watkins amid reports linking him with a move away

And, following those comments, several Villa supporters hit out at Watkins.

Commenting on photos of him and his wife Ellie on her Instagram account, one fan said: 'Ellie please don't let Ollie leave please.'

Another added: 'Tell Ollie to not leave,' with a further fan saying: 'The kids are better in England. Please don't go.'

On Watkins' post of his family holiday in the Bahamas, several Villa supporters also commented by posting multiple snake emojis.

Another shared: 'Congrats on selling your soul Ollie,' before a further supporter said: 'Respect totally gone.'

A further infuriated fan added: 'Saudi? Why bro?'

Their frustration came after Villa put in one of their worst performances under Emery as a new-look side were torn apart by Brighton, with Joao Gomes sent off on his Premier League debut for the club as the Seagulls went 4-0 up in just over half an hour.

Due largely to UEFA financial rules, Villa have sold about £250million worth of talent this summer.

Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa have all departed, and Watkins and Emi Martinez (another absentee on Sunday) could follow.

Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal are said to have had four offers rejected for the English forward

All six were mainstays of the Villa team who beat Freiburg 3-0 in May to lift the Europa League.

Villa have often struggled when the transfer window is open and Emery joked: ‘I think the transfer window should always be closed.

‘In the last three years, until the transfer window closes, we have had problems like we are having now. The players have the mentality I want – not complaining, not blaming, and trying to be patient, even with results like today.

‘We have had this problem (with the window) every season and we overcame it. But it’s something hard for us every year.’

Sports.title: OLIVER HOLT: Michael Carrick should have been backed to the hilt by Man United this summer. Instead the club's dawdling and crowded hierarchy has hung him out to dry
Sports.content:
OLIVER HOLT: Michael Carrick should have been backed to the hilt by Man United this summer. Instead the club's dawdling and crowded hierarchy has hung him out to dry

Read Oliver Holt's column every Monday with a DailyMail+ subscription - and unlock access to the best exclusives, interviews and analysis

It was, Hull City manager Sergej Jakirovic said, as easy and relaxing for his goalkeeper as drinking a cup of afternoon tea. Of all the analysis of the lack of threat posed by the updated Manchester United side as they stumbled into the new season with a defeat on Humberside, it was the most damning assessment of all.

In a 2-0 loss at the home of a promoted team widely tipped to go straight back down, Michael Carrick’s team were outmuscled in defence, overrun in midfield and as meek as mewling kittens in attack. It was the equivalent of ‘can’t bat, can’t bowl, can’t field’ on a football pitch.

It is way too early to make sweeping predictions about where United will finish this season but there was widespread and understandable dismay about the level of the performance, and worrying signs of an apparent failure to build on the progress that Carrick made with the team last season.

United had momentum on their side in May. They finished third. They were back in the Champions League. With Pep Guardiola leaving Manchester City, it was predicted that they would be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season. Instead, there has been a creeping feeling throughout the summer that momentum has been lost.

There has been a feeling that, yet again, the manager of the football club has been let down by the crowded hierarchy above him in the food chain. United had a rare chance to build from a position of relative strength this summer and the mood music already suggests that they blew it.

Michael Carrick can only watch as his Manchester United team are taken apart by promoted club Hull City on Saturday

A side that cannot move on from Harry Maguire, who is 33, is a side with issues

If it is not yet another false dawn, then it is a missed opportunity. The summer was a time for United to make an impression. Instead, it feels as if they have stood still. Youri Tielemans is a fine player but he is not the midfielder who will make the difference between third place and champions.

Are either he or new arrival Carlos Baleba an improvement on Casemiro, who has departed for Major League Soccer? Baleba, who is set to sign from Brighton for around £70million, is a player of rich potential who should bring energy and bite but his progress stalled on the south coast last season.

His last-minute acquisition suggests either confused planning or thwarted ambitions elsewhere. So does the failure to strengthen a defence that was twice undone by set-pieces at the MKM Stadium and looks like a weirdly debilitating mixture of creakiness and naivety. A side that cannot move on from Harry Maguire, who is 33, is a side with issues.

When the big players moved this summer, United missed out. Elliot Anderson went to Manchester City, Morgan Rogers went to Chelsea, Bruno Guimaraes went to Arsenal, Anthony Gordon went to Barcelona, Marc Cucurella went to Real Madrid and Sandro Tonali went to Spurs.

It is hard to shake the idea that United have been left behind. Or at least caught dawdling on the start line. This was the summer they could least afford that to happen. They had a good summer last year when they overhauled their attack with a clutch of good signings but so far, this has been an underwhelming window. They have been feeding off scraps.

It has refocused attention on minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and his lieutenants, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox, and a transfer policy that is starting to look flawed. They fixed the roof last summer and now they’re trying to install a new kitchen. But the foundations are built on shifting sands and they have ignored those completely.

After another tumultuous campaign last season, when Ruben Amorim was fired and Carrick performed such a fine rescue job, this was the summer when he should have been backed to the hilt and United should have shown the faith in him that his achievements in his four months in charge demanded.

Instead, it feels as if that support has been muted. The acquisition of Baleba is a step forward and United are now being strongly linked with Barcelona's 22-year-old Spanish left back Alejandro Balde, but they are shopping at John Lewis, not Harrods. It is hard to shake the feeling of anti-climax.

Youri Tielemans is a fine player but he is not the midfielder who will make the difference between third place and champions

United's summer signings, including Andrey Santos (right), feel underwhelming, as if the club is feeding off scraps

‘Come on, that’s ridiculous,’ Carrick said to former Middlesbrough and Swindon Town forward Jan Aage Fjortoft when Fjortoft, who is now an accomplished presenter for Viaplay, suggested that United had lacked Hull’s passion in the first half of the game on Saturday and conceded two goals before the interval.

It was rare to see Carrick bite like that. It did not feel like a loss of composure but more like a glimpse, ironically, of the passion that runs through him. He was right to stand behind his players, too: an away game at a newly promoted side in front of dedicated fans, hungry for a defrocking, has been the undoing of many an aristocrat.

United do not lack passion. But what is more worrying for Carrick is that they lack quality. They lacked the quality to withstand what Hull threw at them and they lacked the quality to offer more than the occasional threat to the newcomers’ defence. Konstantinos Tzolakis, the goalkeeper his manager referenced, supped on tea, not sympathy.

A beautiful tribute to King Kev

It has been, in many ways, an unnerving summer for the fans of Newcastle United. Liverpool supporters, too, are not quite sure what to expect after the arrival of a new manager to try to repair the disappointments of last season.

But all those concerns and even the result itself, a fittingly exciting 2-2 draw, were secondary to the tribute that the supporters of both teams provided for Kevin Keegan at St James’ Park on Sunday afternoon.

Keegan, who died last month, was one of the great figures of English football, a European Cup winner for Liverpool and a transformative character, both as player and manager, for Newcastle. He was adored in both cities and by both sets of fans.

And the joint farewell that the clubs gave him, both as a spectacle and in song, at their game was a beautiful and moving show of dignity and devotion to a man who brought so much joy to so many. Keegan represented much that was the best of our game and so did the tribute to him.

St James' Park nailed the tremendous and emotional tribute to Kevin Keegan on Sunday

Time running out for Wirtz

I want Florian Wirtz to succeed at Liverpool because I saw enough of him before his arrival in the Premier League to know that he is a sublime player.

Liverpool supporters did not see enough of that player last season, though, and he made an underwhelming start to the new season at Newcastle on Sunday.

Wirtz deserved the patience that was extended to him last season. He would not be the first player to struggle with the pace and the demands of English football. But time is running out for the £115million man to show what he can do.

Sports.title: A scary Alexander Isak issue, the punditry duo who outshone struggling Wayne Rooney and who from Man United's 'spine' is still on the beach? IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend
Sports.content:
Without doubt the worst moment of Liverpool's dismal title defence season came when Hugo Ekitike ruptured his Achilles at Anfield against PSG last April. Not only did it rule a talented forward out until 2027, it left Liverpool relying on Alexander Isak this season and that already feels scary.

Watching Isak at St James' Park yesterday was painful. Where once – during his time at Newcastle - there was certainty and instinctive confidence, there is now only hesitancy and doubt.

Isak used to take penalties for his old club but when Liverpool won one in the 96th minute yesterday, I almost hoped he wouldn't take it. He didn't.

But Liverpool need him. They really need him and that already feels like a problem for Andoni Iraola as he tries to navigate the early weeks of his time as Liverpool manager.

As Liverpool laboured in the latter stages against Newcastle, Isak offered absolutely nothing but he stayed on the field simply because Iraola didn't really have any other option.

Alexander Isak must succeed for Liverpool - their early season prospects depend on it

Last summer – the summer of 2025 – saw a number of No 9s arrive at our big clubs. Isak to Liverpool, Benjamin Sesko to Manchester United, Liam Delap to Chelsea and Viktor Gyokeres to Arsenal. None have had it easy so Isak is not alone.

Indeed as the Premier League returned this weekend, none bar Isak started for their teams. Sesko and Gyokeres were on the bench and Delap has been frozen out entirely by new coach Xabi Alonso at Chelsea.

The difference is that United, Arsenal and Chelsea have alternatives. They can afford to start their season with big name strikers as impact players. Iraola and Liverpool do not have that option.

Cody Gakpo – criminally under-rated by some members of the Liverpool fanbase – delivered with a big goal for Liverpool yesterday and could – at a push – play through the middle. Florian Wirtz – who faces challenges of his own at Anfield – could feasibly operate as a false nine. But neither is a convincing alternative.

What Liverpool really need is for Isak to start playing like a £125m centre forward – or indeed any kind of centre forward at all. Currently he looks miles off.

It was never going to be easy returning to St James' Park where even Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle was whipping up the crowd's vitriol towards a player who once scored 54 Newcastle league goals at more than a goal every other game.

It will feel more straightforward for him when Liverpool host Nottingham Forest at Anfield next Saturday lunchtime.

But at the moment Isak looks like a player who doesn't trust either his body or his mind and that has to change very soon.

Iraola doesn't have the option of asking him to find his form gradually. That was last season's luxury.

It really has to happen now. Liverpool's early season prospects may depend upon it.

Jaissle must look in the mirror

Newcastle coach Jaissle looks as though he will be a lively and entertaining presence on the touchline. But the German was wrong to blame referee Stuart Attwell for the late penalty decision that denied his team victory. The contact from the otherwise excellent Lewis Hall on Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz was clear.

Indeed Jaissle may wish to examine his own part in what happened given that the foul came in time added on by Attwell for a totally unnecessary Newcastle substitution.

Jaissle's decision to replace Yoane Wissa with Fabian Schar in the last minute of added time was clearly designed to waste some precious moments. But all it did was prompt Attwell to add 30 seconds on and it was after 15 of those that Munoz ran at Hall to win the spot-kick.

New guidelines this season mean that players must leave the field within 10 seconds of their number being raised or risk a booking. This means that the classic 'time wasting' substitution is even more pointless than ever.

Is MOTD losing its identity?

It felt strange to see Mark Chapman at Newcastle for Sky the day after he had hosted the season's opening Match of the Day. It is something that chips away a little at the identity of the BBC's flagship show.

TNT, meanwhile, chose to use The Athletic's ace news breaker David Ornstein as one of their pre-match panellists at the Hull-Man Utd game which felt a little like a desperate attempt to jump on the back of his enormous social media following.

As for Wayne Rooney, he continues to struggle to look truly comfortable in the MOTD chair. Joe Hart and Danny Murphy were on this occasion a better combination on the Sunday show than Rooney and Alan Shearer had been 24 hours earlier.

Joe Hart and Danny Murphy were better than Wayne Rooney and Alan Shearer as pundits

A wake-up call for Carrick

Michael Carrick will now know that it really feels like to be a Manchester United manager after his team's lame defeat on Humberside.

Last season was a free hit for Carrick after he succeeded Ruben Amorim as an interim at Old Trafford. Now that he has the job, it is completely different. This is his team and therefore his responsibility.

It was on the one hand hard not to admire Carrick's frankness in his post-match interviews.

When, for example, it was suggested by former Middlesbrough striker Jan Age Fjortoft – now an excellent analyst for foreign rightsholder Viaplay – that his team had lacked 'passion'. Carrick almost bit his head off.

'That is ridiculous,' said Carrick. 'You played football. You [should] understand.'

On the other, Carrick will soon come to learn just how every single word he utters – especially after defeat – will be picked apart by a fanbase that grows ever more impatient for a league title.

For example, he spoke ahead of the Hull game about his team's spine offering him cause for comfort only to see one of the players he name-checked – centre half Harry Maguire – start the season as though he was still on the beach.

The sooner central defenders learn to concentrate on the ball at set pieces the better. When the first Hull goal went in, for example, Maguire was still so intent on holding his man that he actually had both arms wrapped round team-mate Noussair Mazraoui.

It was schoolboy stuff.

Harry Maguire started the season as though he was still on the beach for Man United

Who can be the new Sunderland?

Hull's victory may yet transpire to be a rare highlight in a hard season but it is impossible not to be pleased for a group of supporters who have been through so much since they last watched Premier League football a decade ago.

Indeed both Hull and fellow promoted club Ipswich have followed Sunderland's example of last summer by recruiting heavily to try and repurpose themselves for top-flight football.

Sunderland fielded almost a new team as they flew high last season and a year on Hull have arrived in the Premier League with seven new players – three were in the team that beat United - while Ipswich fielded seven newbies as they beat the Wearsiders at Portman Road.

Ipswich are among the biggest spenders in the Premier League, having shelled out more than £150m. As Sunderland prepare to play European football this season, it seems they may have started something.

Savinho deal doesn't add up

Tottenham have also spent heavily but after their thumping at Brentford it may be a while until we see what they will actually look like under Roberto de Zerbi.

De Zerbi is still without a number of his best players – guys like Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro were not fit to start on Saturday – while one of his anticipated new signings – the Egyptian wide player Omar Marmoush – was actually on the bench for Manchester City yesterday.

So there is much still to come for Spurs fans even if there will be pressure on Tottenham's new executive team for their signings to work out.

Paying Newcastle £100m for Sandro Tonali feels rather top heavy but that pales when compared to the £75m Tottenham have agreed to give City up front for the Brazilian winger Savinho.

The 22-year-old arrived at the Etihad for £30m two summers ago and has made only a modest impact with two Premier League goals and twelve assists.

So who at Tottenham has decided that a 150 per cent increase on value feels like a good deal?

It already feels like one of the strangest transfers in recent Premier League history and if it doesn't work Spurs fans will want answers.

Roberto de Zerbi has seen a number of expensive additions arrive at Tottenham

Arteta spot-on with Martinelli

Arsenal's squad depth is increasingly impressive – the likes of Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke, Max Dowman, Gyokeres and Martin Zubimendi were all on the bench as the champions beat Coventry – which is why Mikel Arteta feels comfortable in moving on Gabriel Martinelli.

Gunners legend Ian Wright claims Arteta's treatment of the Brazilian has been unnecessarily brutal. Martinelli was not involved at all on Friday or indeed at the Community Shield a week earlier.

But Arteta's track record at ruthlessly shipping players out when they have served their purpose is there for all to see.

The likes of Kieran Tierney, Granit Xhaka and Oleksandr Zinchenko all played significant roles in Arsenal's gradual return to eminence under the Spaniard. Indeed all three captained the club at some stage.

But all were invited to further their career elsewhere once their shelf life was reached. It can feel a little cold-hearted at times. But it has worked for Arsenal and that's what matters.

New hope for England

England assistant manager Anthony Barry – last seen struggling to hold back the tears at half-time of England's World Cup win over France – was on his native Merseyside to watch Everton down wasteful Crystal Palace and there was lots to take in.

A fabulous goal from the talented Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and an assured display from Adam Wharton will have reminded Barry and his boss Thomas Tuchel that it's possible to do something other than pack an England squad with wingers.

But Barry will also (hopefully) have noted a decent afternoon from talented Everton central defender Jarrad Branthwaite.

The Cumbrian is one of the most naturally gifted centre halves in England but has seen his progress stalled by injury. He is 24 now and it would help England enormously if he stepped up.

Ezri Konsa and new Manchester City 'midfielder' Marc Guehi (what on earth was all that about yesterday?) were very much 6/10 at the World Cup and could do with competition that isn't called Dan Burn.

Glasner needs history lesson

Former Palace manager Oliver Glasner is now at Nottingham Forest and that still feels like an odd swap, given Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis goes through managers like I go through tissues in hay fever season.

After an opening defeat to Leeds at the City Ground, Glasner suggested that it was impossible for him to suddenly make his team play like Real Madrid in the 1970s.

It was a strange thing to say, not least because Real were not winning big European trophies in that era.

A team who were? Forest, of course.

The club's two European Cup wins came in 1979 and 1980.

Oliver Glasner made strange comments about how Nottingham Forest could play

Still too many kid gloves

It was heartening to see a Premier League weekend pass without any notable VAR moments. Long may Howard Webb's 'high bar for intervention' continue. But he said this last season, too, and we know what happened.

Much of the responsibility for change continues to rest with the players, though, and that's particularly the case when it comes to all the messing about at corners and other set pieces.

As we watched Man City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma wrestle with a Bournemouth player at a corner on the TV in the Newcastle press room yesterday, a voice from the back piped up.

'It's like watching kids in a playground,' she said. It was perfectly put.

Farewell King Kev

Alan Shearer – said to be scaling back his TV schedule this season – was in Newcastle to witness a fabulous and moving tribute to the late Kevin Keegan by two of his former clubs at St James Park.

It really was a super effort by Newcastle and Liverpool and it was fitting that Keegan's family and grandchildren were in the stadium to witness it.

Sometimes football manages to get things very right indeed.

Sports.title: Alexander Isak 'pretended he wasn't bothered' but Newcastle fans 'clearly upset him'
Sports.content:
Alexander Isak 'pretended he wasn't bothered' but Newcastle fans 'clearly upset him'

Liverpool striker Alexander Isak endured a tough time upon his return to St James' Park on Sunday

View 2 Images Alexander Isak was targeted by Newcastle fans on Sunday (Image: 2026 Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA)

It wasn't the return to St James' Park that Alexander Isak would have envisaged as Liverpool were held to a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United on Sunday. The Swedish star left the Magpies for the Reds last summer in a £125million deal, which stands as the British transfer record.

‌



Isak's expensive departure was acrimonious to say the least after he downed tools in order to engineer his move to Anfield. So, the stage was perhaps set for the forward to dish out retribution after he was verbally abused by sections of the Newcastle faithful upon arrival at his former stomping ground on Sunday afternoon.

‌



The Swedish international was jeered heavily when he left the Liverpool team coach to enter the stadium, with chants of 'rat' audible. Loud whistles and boos also accompanied his every touch during the game as he struggled to impose himself on proceedings.

‌



A body language expert has claimed Isak, upon arrival at Newcastle, was eager to "get away" from the fans who used to adore him. He's also been accused of trying to act as if he was unbothered by the hostility, when he "clearly was."

Darren Stanton said via OLBG: "Alexander Isak does something called lip suppression when he first arrives at St. James' Park. His lips are closed, pierced and slightly compressed. There's no arrival smile or anything like that from someone who is returning to his former home ground. He's very aware of the reception he's receiving and what is being chanted.

"The next thing I notice is that his eyebrows are slightly lowered, and he's looking downwards before entering the ground. This actually shows he wants to get away from the Newcastle fans as quickly as possible.

‌



"He's trying to act like he's not bothered by it, but he clearly is. When people don't look around, they try to imply that they are not bothered and that they don't care. It wouldn't surprise me if he wasn't actually listening to any music at all!

Sports.title: Ollie Watkins transfer saga has turned ugly - but loyalty is a two-way street
Sports.content:
Ollie Watkins transfer saga has turned ugly - but loyalty is a two-way street

Ollie Watkins' time at Aston Villa could be up with the player supposedly choosing not to play on Sunday - but clubs and players can be equally disloyal when it suits them

View 3 Images Ollie Watkins looks to be trying to force Aston Villa's hand (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

The transfer window can be a particularly bruising time for players, egos and reputations. And there is unlikely to be too much sympathy from Aston Villa fans for Ollie Watkins after Unai Emery ’s post-match comments.

‌



Villa lose 4-0 at Brighton, the club has been left in a bit of a mess (again) by a messy transfer window which has seen big-name departures like Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa, Lucas Digne and Morgan Rogers with Emiliano Martinez likely to follow.

‌



So, the Watkins story - a live transfer target for Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal - certainly meant people are talking about the Villa striker rather than a humiliating defeat. A distraction tactic?

‌



It has made Watkins the villain of the piece with Emery hinting heavily - but not quite saying it out right - that the England striker refused to play at Brighton.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Watkins, 30, is being offered a huge contract in the Saudi Pro League, it would be a fantastic pay day for a player who has reached the very top in his career having really battled his way up from non-league. This is a really nice, understated but determined player who does not really seek the spotlight but there have been ups and downs at Villa.

‌



It has largely always been up when he is on the pitch because he works hard, scores goals and gives his all for the team. He has enjoyed success with the Europa League and helping the club qualify for the Champions League.

The downs have been when he has been dropped, he has been left out on numerous occasions and when players are axed from the team no-one stands up for them.

It’s just when the suggestion comes they don’t want to play for the team. Emery is such a good manager and one of the reasons is because he’s a bad loser. He’s so determined to win. As the saying goes, show me a good loser and I’ll show you a loser. Emery is a winner.

‌



View 3 Images Unai Emery didn't shy away from addressing Ollie Watkins' situation (Image: Joris Verwijst/Soccrates/Getty Images)

After the Brighton game, you could see he was fuming, Watkins was caught in the crossfire and is now public enemy No.1. It was Villa who denied Watkins a move to Arsenal in January 2025 when the Midlands club did need to sell. Arsenal will always say that it was Villa who first sounded them out. Villa eventually sold Jhon Duran to balance the books.

Watkins was priced out of a move but, like all players, is a commodity who is owned by his club - until they don’t want him. Then he’s just discarded. Villa have sold so many players this summer that it must have created some uncertainty. If you look at what happened last season - they did not win any of their first five Premier League games and scored just one goal - this transfer carousel is not new.

‌



They have been prolific buyers and sellers. And so is Watkins so wrong? There is no way a player should go on strike to force a move when they are paid so well in the first place.

View 3 Images Morgan Rogers is one of several high profile sales made by Aston Villa (Image: Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

But is it always that black and white? You can be sure players up and down the country will be talking with their clubs, agents and managers about what the future holds.

‌



Many players will feel as if they need to move on. This is not the era of player power. But we have seen a shift of more clubs openly courting transfer targets - even if they are under contract.

Every club does it and if that turns the odd head - especially when a move would be for life-changing money - then they probably are not in the right frame of mind to play.

But equally, the player will probably recall the last time they were dropped and ask their own questions about loyalty. It must be a two-way street. Clearly, Villa fans might not agree right now. But this saga has probably happened at every club this summer - but not so publicly.

Sports.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan gives honest take on snooker future - 'There's nothing I can do'
Sports.content:
Ronnie O'Sullivan gives honest take on snooker future - 'There's nothing I can do'

Ronnie O'Sullivan is through to the last 32 of the Wuhan Open after beating Ashley Carty 5-2, but he was critical of his performance and feels powerless to do better

View 2 Images Ronnie O'Sullivan was typically candid in his assessment (Image: Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images)

Snooker legend Ronnie O'Sullivan has admitted that there's 'nothing he can do' to improve on his 'pretty bad' form. Despite winning his opening game at the Wuhan Open 5-2 against Ashley Carty, O'Sullivan was downbeat.

‌



The seven-time world champion made a high break of just 59 and was fortunate not to be punished by Carty, who missed a string of opportunities. O'Sullivan reckons that he hasn't been at his best for four years, with his performance against Carty coming as no surprise to him.

‌



"My performance was pretty bad really," the Rocket said. "You have to call it out. I'm not going to lie. I'm not going to try to delude myself and say there was some good stuff.

‌



"It has been pretty bad for a long time, so I expect to play pretty bad every time I go out there. I know I don't have anything to prove and that is what everyone keeps telling me.

‌



"However, for my own selfish reasons, I miss playing well and dominating the table, beating anyone who is in front of me. I miss that feeling, but there is nothing I can do about it."

O'Sullivan doesn't have long to wait until his next match, facing Chinah's Yao Pengcheng at 7am UK time on Tuesday in the last 32. His chances of making a deep run at the Wuhan Open have been boosted by Wu Yize's early exit.

The world champion suffered a shock 5-4 loss against Artemijs Zizins on Monday. Latvian youngster Zizins has been awarded a clash with Stephen Maguire at the same time slot as O'Sullivan's match.

‌



Last month, O'Sullivan revealed that he's set himself a deadline of 2028 to beat Stephen Hendry's record for World Championships. The 50-year-old is currently level with seven and told World Snooker Tour: " I'd love to win another World Championship.

Can Ronnie O'Sullivan get back to his best? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Ronnie O'Sullivan was unhappy with his display against Ashley Carty (Image: Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images)

‌



"I've got two attempts at it. Three years previous, I wasn't cueing well enough, so I feel like if I can find a bit of cueing find some form at Sheffield… if I don't do it this this season or the next season, then it'll definitely never happen.

"But I'm pleased with my career. I'm happy with how things have gone, and I just want to try and enjoy these next two years. I'll reassess it in 2028 and if things are really going well, and I've surprised myself, then maybe you can extend it but you have to be realistic. I'm definitely not going to be playing qualifiers put it that way.

"I'm not going to play qualifiers. You won't be seeing me go down to Barnsley trying to win qualifying matches and all that sort of stuff. I have to be realistic. If that happens, then obviously that's the end of my career. But hopefully, I can keep going for at least another two seasons."

Sports.title: Freddie Flintoff's life-changing injuries and facial scars as 'next Top Gear host in talks'
Sports.content:
Freddie Flintoff's life-changing injuries and facial scars as 'next Top Gear host in talks'

Top Gear is set to return to the BBC four years on from Freddie Flintoff's serious accident on set of the programme

View 2 Images Freddie Flintoff was seriously injured in the Top Gear crash (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

The BBC are set to reboot Top Gear and are reportedly in talks with comedian Jimmy Carr to become the new main host. The news comes four years after the show was taken off air following Freddie Flintoff's serious car crash.

‌



The former cricketer had been in the middle of testing an open-top vehicle when it flipped, and he was left with life-changing injuries. Despite the 48-year-old's lasting scars, BBC bosses believe it is the right time for the programme to make a return.

‌



A TV insider said: "Production have their sights set on Jimmy, he's the ideal host to take the show into a new era and revive Top Gear. He's keen to work on something mainstream after spending so many years fronting comedy panel shows.

‌



"He's a real car buff, too, so it would be a passion project. Casting directors are now working to find talent to join him in the new-look ensemble."

Andrew Flintoff releases statement after shock England departure and confirms next job READ MORE :

Top Gear first aired in 1977 but was cancelled by BBC in 2001, with Jeremy Clarkson and Andy Wilman bringing it back one year later. A number of presenters were included on the show, including Chris Evans, Eddie Jordan and Jason Dawe.

However, the main hosts between 2002 and 2015 - and the names most synonymous with the show - are Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May. Flintoff took over presenting in 2019 and was joined by Paddy McGuinness and Chris Harris.

‌



He spent three years as one of the main faces of the popular BBC programme. This came to a halt when Flintoff was seriously injured during a crash in 2022.

The accident took place at Top Gear's test track at Dunsfold Park Aerodrome in Surrey. Flintoff was left with serious facial injuries and later reached a £9million settlement with the BBC, who stated the show would be paused "for the foreseeable future" as a result of the crash.

In a statement in March 2023, the broadcaster said: "We have sincerely apologised to Freddie and will continue to support him with his recovery. We understand [halting the show] will be disappointing for fans, but it is the right thing to do, and we'll make a judgement about how best to continue later this year."

‌



Flintoff admitted he believed he "was dead" in the immediate aftermath of the crash and "remembers everything about it." Speaking in the Disney+ documentary, Flintoff, the ex-Top Gear host said: "I thought I was dead, because I was conscious but I couldn't see anything.

View 2 Images Flintoff was left permanently scarred from the crash (Image: MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

"I was thinking, is that it? Is that it? You know what I mean? Just black for the rest of my days? My hat came over my eyes - so I pulled my hat up and I thought, no I'm not [dead], I'm on the Top Gear track, this is not heaven."

Flintoff has recovered from the incident, although he still has scars across his chin and nose after revealing that he feared his face had been ripped off. He added: "I thought my face had come off. I was frightened to death."

The former England international has worked with the BBC since the Top Gear crash, producing the 'Freddie's Field of Dreams' show that was dedicated to creating a new cricket team in Preston.
