World.title: Oil Prices Fall Ahead of US, Iran Sanctions
World.content:
Oil prices fell more than one dollar on Monday as investors took profits and awaited expected new U.S. sanctions on Iran.

Brent crude futures fell $1.16, or 1.23 per cent, to $93.23 a barrel at 11:31 a.m. GMT.

U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude declined $1.55, or 1.78 per cent, to $85.51 a barrel.

Both contracts recorded a second consecutive weekly gain last week, rising more than five per cent.

The gains followed stalled U.S.-Iran peace negotiations, which have constrained oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

The waterway previously carried about one-fifth of global oil supplies and remains a major route for energy shipments.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is expected to announce new measures against Iran during a press conference later Monday.

Bessent has threatened to impose what he described as “the toughest sanctions in history” on Iran.

U.S. President Donald Trump has also threatened sanctions against countries trading with Iran.

PVM analyst Tamas Varga said an embargo could reduce regional oil supplies and prompt tighter restrictions on Iranian oil exports.

He added that Iran could retaliate with fresh attacks against oil installations across the Middle East.

Iran has condemned the planned U.S. sanctions, while President Masoud Pezeshkian has called for a diplomatic solution.

Pakistan’s army chief was visiting Tehran on Monday for mediation talks ahead of the expected U.S. announcement.

Shipping data showed fewer than 20 commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz during the weekend amid restrictions affecting energy shipments.

Iran, however, allowed some Iraqi oil tankers to pass through the strait following repeated requests from Baghdad, Iranian state news agency IRNA reported.

Traders said Iraq’s SOMO and QatarEnergy had also offered crude for loading inside the strait.

SEB analyst Bjarne Schieldrop said current Brent prices suggested that sufficient oil was still flowing through the Strait of Hormuz.

He said a major turning point could occur if Iran decided to completely close the waterway using rockets and drones.

Brent crude has risen to about $92 a barrel from $71 in June, driven by declining inventories and concerns over prolonged Middle East disruptions.

Morgan Stanley analysts said they had raised their Brent price forecasts, projecting prices could peak at $100 a barrel in the fourth quarter.

Meanwhile, the International Energy Agency is not currently considering another release of oil from strategic reserves, its chief Fatih Birol said. (Reuters/NAN)

World.title: Tunji-Ojo Calls for Stronger Partnerships to Secure Borders
World.content:
The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, has called for stronger collaborations among universities, security agencies, regional institutions and development partners to strengthen border security, migration management and regional integration.

Tunji-Ojo made the call at the opening ceremony of the African Borderlines Research Network (ABORNE) 2026 conference on Monday in Lagos.

The minister was represented by a Senior Special Assistant to the minister on Policy, Dr Kareem Olajoku.

The four-day conference was with the theme: ‘Connected Borderlands, Socio-Cultural Integration, and the Centrality of Policy, Research, and Security.’

He posited that the country must increasingly adopt evidence-based approaches to border management while ensuring that research remains responsive to practical realities.

The conference brought together scholars, policymakers, practitioners and development partners to examine issues surrounding Africa’s security, integration and development.

The partnership is particularly relevant as Nigeria continues to modernise its approach to migration and border management, through improvements in biometric identity systems, passport administration, automated border control and technology enabling border security.

He buttressed that the developments reflect the country ‘s determination to build a border management system that protects national security while facilitating legitimate travel and regional mobility.

He commended Lagos State University (LASU) and ABORNE for co-hosting the conference, describing the partnership as an example of how academic research and practical experience, when brought together could address contemporary security challenges.

According to him, the collaboration between the academia and practitioners is particularly important, as Nigeria continues to modernise approaches to migration and border management.

He highlighted ongoing improvements in biometric identity systems, passport administration, automated border control and technology-enabled border security as efforts to drive modernisation.

He noted that the developments demonstrate Nigeria’s determination to build a border management system capable of protecting national security while facilitating legitimate travel and regional mobility.

Tunji-Ojo further stressed the strategic importance of Lagos as the host location for the conference, describing the state as a major gateway for the movement of people and goods through its land connections, seaports and international airports.

He said Lagos provided an appropriate setting for discussions on the relationship between security, mobility, trade, community interaction and regional integration.

The minister called for greater attention to border communities, noting that they are often the first to experience the effects of insecurity and irregular migration.

He, however, said such communities should not be viewed merely as populations requiring protection, but as important partners capable of contributing to early warning, conflict prevention and effective border management.

“Building a resilient borderline therefore requires us to see border communities not merely as populations to be secured but as partners in security, peace and development.” he said.

Tunji-Ojo equally stressed that research should help governments anticipate emerging challenges rather than merely explain past developments.

He described ABORNE 2026 as more than an academic conference, saying it offered an opportunity to strengthen the relationship between knowledge and action, communities and institutions, as well as national security and regional cooperation.

According to him, the conference provides Nigeria with an important platform to contribute to the development of secure, integrated and resilient borders across West Africa and the wider African continent.

The minister urged participants to move beyond identifying challenges and focus on developing practical, collaborative and sustainable solutions.

He also expressed hope that the partnerships established during the conference would continue beyond the event and that knowledge generated through the gathering would contribute to policymaking and practice across Africa.

On her part, the Vice-Chancellor of LASU, Prof. Ibiyemi Olatunji-Bello, said that for the university, the gathering was much more than the hosting of an international academic conference.

Olatunji-Bello said that it was an affirmation of the university’s commitment to producing knowledge that responds to the country’s realities and continent and its development.

She noted that Africa needed a new generation of scholars and professionals who understand that borders are not mere communities.

According to her, they are also communities of people, livelihoods, identity, security, development and human mobility.

“The university must therefore do more than observe these realities. It’s more the help to understand them, interrogate them and contribute to shaping policies and practices that govern them,” she said. (NAN)

World.title: 2027: APC Disowns Hunye, Insists Yayi Remains Ogun Guber Candidate
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The All Progressives Congress (APC) has disowned a self-declared governorship candidate, Mr. Abayomi Hunye, insisting that Senator Adeola Olamilekan Yayi remains the party’s Ogun State gubernatorial standard-bearer for the 2027

The National Secretary of the party, Senator Ajibola Basiru, described his self-declaration as the Ogun State governorship candidate of the party for the 2027 elections as false, unauthorised and mischievous.

He added that Hunye is no longer a member of the APC because he had been suspended.

He noted: “The All Progressives Congress (APC), hereby informs the general public stakeholders, Ogun State chapter and the good people of Ogun State that Mr. Abayomi Hunye is an impostor who is currently on suspension as a member of APC.

“His recent self-declaration as the governorship candidate of our great party for the 2027 election is completely false, unauthorised, and a mischievous act aimed at misleading the public.

“For the avoidance o f doubt, Mr. Abayomi Hunye is not a member of the APC in good standing. He was suspended from the party on April 7, 2026, following a petition from his ward, Tube Ward, in Ipokia Local Government Area of the state.

“The suspension was not arbitrary. It was a grassroots decision driven by the ward executives in Tube Ward, ratified by the Ipokia Local Government Area, and formally approved by the Ogun State Working Committee.”

The party’s scribe explained that Hunye’s suspension was ratified by the Ogun State Working Committee and communicated to the national headquarters.

The reasons adduced for his suspension included: Engaging in activities injurious to the image of the party; and deliberate actions aimed at causing disaffection and division among loyal members.

Consequently, Basru said that Hunye lacks the legal and moral standing to represent the APC in any capacity.

He added: “We reiterate that following the validly conducted primary election of the APC, the duly nominated and elected governorship candidate for the 2027 Ogun State election is Senator Adeola Solomon Olamilekan with his running mate being Balogun Kudirat Abiodun.”

Basiru emphasised that in line with the provisions of the Electoral Act, 2026, and the guidelines of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the names and other particulars of Yayi and Abiodun have been successfully uploaded onto the INEC portal and the commission has issued official acknowledgement slips confirming them as the duly recognised flag bearers of the APC for the Ogun State governorship election.

He maintained that any person, group, or organisation that associates, collaborates, or transacts any political business with Hunye under the guise of the APC does so at their own risk.

The national secretary said the party would not be held liable for any financial loss, legal disputes or criminal liability that may arise from such dealings.

He stated: “We have instructed our legal team to initiate contempt proceedings and file a formal complaint with the relevant security agencies to address this gross misrepresentation and impersonation.”

Basiru warned the media and the public to disregard any publications, interviews, or documents originating from Hunye regarding the APC.

He also cautioned all media houses against granting Hunye a platform to propagate his false claims, as this could be interpreted as complicity in a fraudulent act.

World.title: Catalyst Symposium Holds “Alaigbo” Series in South-East, Empowers Youths
World.content:
The Catalyst Symposium, an initiative that empowers and nurtures emerging leaders across different sectors, has held its Alaigbo Series in Anambra and Imo States to ignite ideas, inspire creativity and empower youths from the region to make impactful contributions to nation building.

The Anambra event was held in Awka, the state capital, on Aug.13 , and was followed by the Owerri edition on Aug. 17 at the Guest House of the Federal University of Technology, Owerri (FUTO), Imo State, with both events attracting a vibrant audience of emerging leaders, entrepreneurs, young professionals, and students who filled the venues with energy and expectation.

These gatherings formed a powerful multi-city movement dedicated to catalyzing minds, igniting ideas, and empowering the sons and daughters of Alaigbo to move from survival to significance.

The atmosphere was charged with purposeful conversations as participants engaged deeply with practical insights on leadership, business growth, and regional transformation. The event set a strong tone for the entire Alaigbo Series and demonstrated the hunger for quality platforms within the South-East.

A major highlight of the Awka Edition was the combined contributions of Philip O. Ekwempu Esq., President of the Awka Chamber of Commerce, and Eze Chinonso, who served as a key speaker and panelist.

While Ekwempu delivered penetrating insights on “From Traders to Titans: Building Systems, Scaling Sustainably, and Creating Generational Wealth,” Eze Chinonso complemented the discourse with practical business perspectives that prepared the ground for his later special appearance in Owerri. Together, their sessions sparked meaningful dialogue on sustainable wealth creation and bold entrepreneurship in Alaigbo.

The smooth flow and high engagement of both editions were largely driven by the outstanding work of Dr Macaulay Barnabas, who served as the Event Host and Lead Moderator.

Behind the success of these editions stands the unwavering dedication and strong work ethic of the convener, Arogundade Dolapo. From meticulous planning and stakeholder engagement to hands-on coordination across cities, his commitment to excellence ensured that every detail was executed with precision.

Dolapo’s relentless drive continues to push The Catalyst Symposium beyond limitations and toward greater impact.

The Owerri edition, styled as the ‘Eze Chinonso Special’, carried unique emotional vibe as a homecoming for the special guest at his alma mater, the Federal University of Technology, Owerri (FUTO).

In addition to Eze Chinonso’s inspiring session, the edition featured “The Catalyst Pitch and Mentorship Programme, where 13 scholars from FUTO boldly pitched their business ideas.

These young innovators have been selected to undergo a structured three-week mentorship programme designed to refine their concepts, build practical skills, and position them for real growth.

Across both cities, the quality of engagement, the free access model, and the sense of community stood out clearly, as participants left with renewed clarity, expanded networks, and a stronger belief in the possibilities within Alaigbo.

These two editions have further strengthened The Catalyst Symposium’s growing footprint, bringing the total number of successful editions to over ten.

According to the organisers, as the sparks ignited in Awka and Owerri continue to spread, The Catalyst Symposium remains committed to expanding this movement, creating more platforms, and supporting the next generation of leaders who will drive the sustainable development and generational wealth of the South-East and beyond.

World.title: UNIPGC Africa, JodelaTV, EduCore to Train 2026 Batch of Content Creators ahead of Nigeria at 66
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

As Nigeria prepares to mark its 66th Independence anniversary, the African Continental Chapter of the United Nations International Peace and Governance Council, UNIPGC AFRICA, has announced plans to host an intensive capacity building masterclass for social media and content creators across the country.

The 2026 Social media & Content Creator Capacity Building Masterclass is being organised in collaboration with JodelaTV and EduCore Impact Organization. It will be held live in Lagos as part of activities lined up for Nigeria at 66 Peace and Governance Conference/Awards.

According to the organisers, the workshop is designed to radically elevate the skills, professionalism, and income potential of digital content creators, and to position Nigerian talent to compete effectively in the global digital economy.

The Global President and Chairman of the UNIPGC Supreme Council, His Excellency, Ambassador Jonathan Ojadah, said in a statement that the initiative was borne out of the need to bridge the gap between creativity and structure in Nigeria’s fast-growing creative sector.

“The Nigerian creative industry is overflowing with talent, but talent alone is no longer enough to compete globally,” Ambassador Ojadah said. “This masterclass bridges the gap between raw creativity and structural competence.”

He added that the programme will equip participants with the technical optimization and narrative power required to build sustainable, influential digital enterprises from Nigeria, while also aligning with global standards of digital governance and storytelling.

The masterclass will take place during the Nigeria at 66 Peace and Governance Conference / Awards, a high-level dialogue focused on strengthening democratic governance, investment promotion and peace building systems in the country. The theme for this year’s commemoration is: From Conflict to Consolidation: Strengthening Democracy & Traditional Institutions through Solidarity.

Organisers said the training will cover key areas including content strategy, platform algorithm mastery, monetization, brand partnerships, digital storytelling for impact, and professional ethics for content creators and digital journalists.

Applications are now officially open to eligible participants. To qualify, applicants must be active content creators, digital journalists, bloggers, podcasters, or video editors based in Nigeria, with a verifiable online platform or portfolio of at least six months of active content.

World.title: UNICEF Mobilises Katsina Religious Leaders for Child Health, Vaccination Drive
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has enlisted Imams, pastors and other religious leaders across the 34 local government areas of Katsina State to leverage their influence and religious platforms to promote child vaccination, nutrition, education, healthcare and protection.

The interfaith leaders were enlisted during the unveiling of UNICEF’s Faith for Life initiative in Katsina, designed to harness scriptural teachings from the Bible and Qur’an to promote behaviours that improve the survival and development of children.

Addressing the clerics, the UNICEF Social and Behavioural Change Specialist, Kano Field Office, Dr Ogu Enemaku, said the initiative launched in collaboration with the Katsina State Government, seeks to improve children’s health, education, vaccination and protection.

He explained that the interfaith-based initiative provides relevant scriptural messages on health, nutrition, education and child protection that religious leaders should incorporate into their sermons, teachings and community engagements.

He urged the religious leaders to obtain, study and effectively utilise the Faith for Life materials to educate their followers and encourage families to make informed decisions on issues affecting the wellbeing of women and children across the state.

Also speaking, the Deputy Director, Community Outreach and Development, National Orientation Agency (NOA), Abuja, Amaka Aninta, challenged religious leaders to leverage their platforms to prevent avoidable deaths among children and pregnant women.

She said when religious teachings emphasise on the protection and wellbeing of mothers and children no child will die from vaccine-preventable diseases and no expectant mother will lose her life due to poor access to antenatal care or malnutrition.

She therefore urged the religious leaders to lead campaigns encouraging parents to vaccinate their children, pregnant women to attend antenatal care and families to take action against malnutrition and other challenges affecting mothers and children.

She admonished the enlisted religious leaders to also use Friday prayers, Islamic schools and church services to sensitise their communities on child protection, family welfare and responsible parenting.

Earlier, the Acting Executive Secretary of the Katsina State Primary Health Care Agency, Dr Shema’u Kabir Abba, described religious leaders as “special guides and advocates” and critical partners in driving positive behavioural change in communities.

She said the government could not address the challenges confronting primary healthcare alone, stressing that influential and respected voices within communities were needed to improve maternal and child health and nutrition outcomes.

She commended the religious leaders for their continued partnership with the government and urged them to sustain their support for initiatives aimed at strengthening healthcare delivery across the state.

World.title: Bandits Abduct Monarch, Another Monarch’s First Wife, Others in Kwara Communities
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

About 10 suspected bandits have reportedly abducted the traditional ruler of Igbesi town and other residents of the town in Isin Local Government Area of Kwara State.

Also, a woman identified as Iya Ayoka, the first wife of the Baale of Dabu community in Ifelodun Local Government Area of the state, was reportedly kidnapped in the town.

The latest attack on Kwara South senatorial communities happened despite the recent establishment of the Nigeria Army battalion formation in Omu-Aran town in Irepodun LGA of the state.

THISDAY checks revealed that the monarch was said to have been abducted during a fierce attack by the suspected bandits over the weekend in the town.

It was gathered that the monarch and other residents were said to have been taken to an unknown destination while the suspected bandits were yet to call any of the families for ransom.

Also, the first wife of the monarch of Dabu community, popularly called Iya Ayoka, was said to have been abducted in the town in Ifelodun LGA of the state by suspected bandits.

The abduction of Iya Ayoka, according to THISDAY checks over the weekend, has further increased fears among residents of Dabu and surrounding communities, particularly amid concerns over the activities of armed groups operating in parts of Kwara South.

Residents have continued to call for urgent intervention by security agencies to prevent further attacks and rescue those already in captivity.

Sources also disclosed to journalists in Ilorin yesterday that the bandits were said to be using the TikTok account of another kidnap victim, a 23-year-old woman identified as Babatunde Fasilat, to make posts while demanding a ransom for her release.

Fasilat was reportedly kidnapped on July 26, 2026, in Wande community.

According to a source familiar with the incident, the bandits invaded the community and abducted Fasilat after her father attempted to defend her.

“Her father was shot, and the bullet penetrated the other side of his body.

“The bandits were four. While her father was trying to defend himself, they went to her room and kidnapped her,” the source said.

The source added that the kidnappers have demanded N20 million as ransom before Fasilat would be released.

“Now, they are demanding N20 million before they can release her, and they are using her TikTok account to make a post,” the source said.

The use of the victim’s social media account has raised further concerns among residents, as the kidnappers appear to be using the platform to communicate and put pressure on the victim’s family to meet their ransom demand.

When contacted, senior police officers in the Ifelodun and Isin LGAs of the state who spoke with journalists in Ilorin yesterday on condition of anonymity confirmed the ugly development.

They, however, said: “We have sent a signal to the state Police Command on the ugly development and the Command has swung into action.

World.title: YPP Raises Concern over Citizens’ Exclusion, Calls for Extension of Voter Registration
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

The Young Progressive Party (YPP) has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to extend the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise over fears that eligible Nigerians who are yet to register could be excluded from participating in the 2027 general election.

The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Chairman of the YPP, Hon. Abraham Simon Adedotun, and the party’s FCT senatorial candidate, Blessing Ufedojo Benyeogor, who made the call at the weekend, appealed to the electoral umpire to reconsider the closure of the registration exercise and provide another opportunity for eligible citizens to register.

In a joint statement issued to journalists in Abuja, Adedotun and Benyeogor claimed that the closure of the CVR could disenfranchise many Nigerians, particularly young people who had not yet completed the registration process.

Meanwhile, they charged INEC to remain an impartial umpire and take steps that would strengthen public confidence in the electoral process and Nigeria’s democracy.

Recall that the Commission had initially scheduled the 2025–2026 CVR exercise to run until August 30, 2026. The Commission subsequently revised the timetable, setting an earlier operational deadline and later extending the final phase to July 26, 2026.

On July 26, INEC said the registration exercise would close that day, urging eligible Nigerians who had not registered to take advantage of the remaining time. The Commission later ruled out another extension, saying further delays could affect its preparations for the 2027 elections.

Meanwhile, INEC had also introduced a self-service online registration option during the final phase, allowing eligible first-time voters to complete the registration process electronically.

It should be noted that besides YPP, other political actors and civil society groups have expressed concern about access to voter registration and the need to ensure that eligible citizens are not left out of the electoral process.

They urged that the electoral umpire consider the appeals of Nigerians who were unable to register and to explore measures that would give eligible citizens another opportunity to be captured on the voters’ register.

As preparations for the 2027 elections continue, the debate over voter registration is likely to remain a significant issue, particularly given the importance of ensuring broad participation and public confidence in the electoral process.

World.title: ‘Absolute greediness’: South Africans slam SASSA claims after R31 000 review
World.content:
The story of a woman ordered to repay R31 000 to SASSA sparked outrage among Facebook commenters, many of whom accused grant beneficiaries of claiming support they were never entitled to.

Thabiso Khayisa did not hold back, writing, “Absolute greediness, how can one get a salary, child maintenance and still carry on receiving child support grant??” The comment struck a nerve, drawing support from others who feel SASSA’s income threshold rules, currently set at R5 800 a month, are too often ignored or manipulated.

Political corruption raised as a bigger concern

Not everyone directed their anger at grant beneficiaries. Dineo Dee redirected the conversation toward government accountability, asking, “What about the politicians who stole millions? Why are they not paying anything back?”



Her comment reflects a recurring frustration among South Africans who argue that ordinary grant recipients face harsher consequences than officials who are allegedly implicated in far larger corruption scandals involving public funds.

A middle-ground take on greed, fraud, and fairness

Sidwell Qalinge offered one of the more detailed responses, arguing that someone with a secure income who also claims a SASSA grant is taking money away from more deserving pensioners. He pointed out that grant amounts, referencing figures around R1 600 rising to R2 400, are modest sums that should go to those who genuinely need them, concluding that “fraud is fraud whether you are 60 or 16.” Daniel Louw echoed the broader call for accountability, repeating his view that stricter checks are “about time.”

The exchange reflects SASSA’s own data, which shows close to 495 000 people have been flagged as potentially ineligible through its expanded verification partnerships with banks, SARS, and payroll systems, a process that has already resulted in tens of thousands of suspended grants nationwide.

World.title: Here’s how much the Southern Guards GC earned at LIV Golf Indianapolis
World.content:
From a South African point of view, the LIV Golf Indianapolis event proved to be a mixed bag for the Southern Guards team. Image: X @SouthernGuards

Rookie Michael La Sasso pipped Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau to win LIV Golf’s season-ending Indianapolis event on Sunday, as the breakaway series faces a deeply uncertain future.

Questions remain about whether and how the divisive LIV Tour – which for years lured golf’s top stars with billions of Saudi dollars – will return next season, after losing its Middle Eastern funding.

READ | How much does it cost to: Attend the Nedbank Golf Challenge



Fate of star players uncertain

The fate of star players like Rahm and DeChambeau is critical and remains uncertain, with speculation swirling that many could seek to return to the PGA Tour.

The 2026 season ended with 22-year-old La Sasso, the youngest player on the tour and now its youngest-ever winner, executing a perfect chip on the final hole for a tap-in birdie and victory.

He ended on 18-under with a round of 65, a stroke clear of a surging Rahm, who finished a round of 63 with a costly bogey on his final hole.

DeChambeau and Sergio Garcia finished third on 16-under par.

Spain’s Rahm had already clinched his third consecutive season-long points title.

Rahm’s Legion XIII also sealed the season-long team championship, for a second year running.



Prize pot half the size

LIV Golf’s team championship event in Michigan, which had been scheduled for next week, was cancelled, meaning the Indianapolis event concluded the 2026 campaign.

The Indianapolis prize money pot was roughly half the usual LIV amount, with $10 million spread across players, including just over $2 million for the winner.

Organisers insist a “LIV 2.0” will emerge with a slimmed-down schedule, smaller prizes and new investors.

Mixed bag for Southern Guards

From a South African point of view, the LIV Golf Indianapolis event proved to be a mixed bag.

Dean Burmester finished eighth on 14-under par and earned $265 125 (R4.2 million), while Branden Grace ended in a tie for 17th place on 10-under par which saw him bank $116 431 (R1.87 million).

For Louis Oosthuizen and Charl Schwartzel it was more of a struggle over the 72 holes.

Oosthuizen finished in a tie for 43rd on 3-under par and earned $64 893 (R1 million), while Schwartzel ended on 2-under par in a tie for 45th in the 57-player field and went home $44 693 (R716 000) richer.

In the team competition, the Southern Guards finished eighth (out of 13 teams) on 29-under par and shared $1 500 000 (R24 million) equally, giving them an extra $375 000 (R6 million) each.

World.title: DA councillor among four suspects arrested for alleged murder
World.content:
The Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) has called on the Democratic Alliance (DA) to suspend its councillor Kabelo Mahonko, who was arrested in connection with the alleged kidnapping, assault and murder of a man accused of breaking into a house.

Mahonko, a councillor in the City of Ekurhuleni, was arrested on 17 August and appeared before the Benoni Magistrate’s Court on 19 August. He faces charges of kidnapping and murder.

DA COUNCILLOR ARRESTED FOR ALLEGED MURDER

The DA has reportedly referred the matter to its Federal Legal Commission.



Reacting to the arrest, the EFF called on the DA to immediately suspend Mahonko from all public responsibilities pending the finalisation of the legal process.

“As a DA PR councillor in the City of Ekurhuleni, this matter cannot be reduced to internal party processes concerning an ordinary member. We also call on the Ekurhuleni City Council to suspend Mahonko from any municipal work,” the party said.

According to Gauteng police, Mahonko allegedly tortured and assaulted two men, aged 33 and 36, after accusing them of breaking into her house and stealing items.

Unfortunately, one of the men later died from his injuries.

ACCUSED SET TO APPEAR IN COURT

Three more suspects have been arrested in connection with the matter. They appeared in court on 21 August and are expected to appear alongside DA councillor Kabelo Mahonko on 27 August for a bail application.

World.title: ‘Must work to stay alive’: South Africans defend working SASSA recipients
World.content:
While many South Africans criticised grant recipients following the R31 000 SASSA repayment story, others raised a different concern entirely: why pensioners earning substantial salaries are able to claim grants at all.

June Pillay questioned SASSA’s enforcement directly, asking why the agency does not investigate companies employing pensioners who reportedly earn as much as R10 000 a month while still collecting SASSA payments, and why oversight bodies do not check employer records more closely.

Others say grant amounts don’t cover survival

Carole Jones Delcie pushed back against the idea that claiming a grant while working reflects greed, arguing instead that SASSA payments simply are not enough to cover a household’s basic needs.



“Some have to work to be able to survive otherwise it’s out on the streets,” she wrote, a view shared by pensioners’ rights groups who have previously marched to demand the Older Person’s Grant be increased from R2 400 to R5 000 a month.

A stark reality facing older South Africans

Johan Willemse summed up the sentiment shared by several commenters in blunt terms: “Old people must work to stay alive.” His comment reframes the debate around SASSA’s compliance crackdown, suggesting that for many elderly South Africans, holding down a job alongside a grant is less about exploiting the system and more about basic survival amid rising living costs.

SASSA maintains that its review process exists to protect the integrity of the grant system, having already flagged hundreds of thousands of cases nationally. But as these comments show, many South Africans believe the deeper issue lies not with beneficiaries bending the rules, but with grant values that have failed to keep pace with the cost of living.

World.title: New Home Affairs office officially opens in Cape Town – and you’ll need to book
World.content:
Home Affairs Minister Dr Leon Schreiber opened the new Home Affairs office on Monday, 24 August. Image: file / canva

Cape Town residents now have another option for accessing Home Affairs services, with a new modern office officially opened at the Cape Town Civic Centre.

Home Affairs Minister Dr Leon Schreiber opened the new facility on Monday, 24 August, describing it as part of the department’s efforts to make services more accessible while reducing the long queues traditionally associated with Home Affairs offices.

“For too long, visiting Home Affairs has been associated with travelling long distances, standing in queues and losing hours of your day,” Schreiber said.



He said the department was working to change that experience through its reform agenda, including by bringing services closer to places people already visit.

New Home Affairs office will operate by appointment

The Civic Centre office has been designed as a modern and welcoming space and is located alongside existing City of Cape Town services.

It is also close to public transport options, making it more convenient for residents who need to visit Home Affairs.

Importantly, the office will operate on a bookings-only basis.

This means residents will need to make an appointment before visiting, with the system intended to allow clients to plan their visits and avoid spending hours waiting in queues.

Appointments can be made through the department’s upgraded online booking system.



The new approach forms part of the department’s broader Home Affairs @ home vision, which aims to decentralise services and make them available closer to where people live, work and carry out their daily activities.

More pressure taken off busy offices

The opening of the Civic Centre office is also expected to help ease pressure on existing Home Affairs facilities in Cape Town.

Schreiber said the new facility would take additional pressure off busy offices such as the one in Barrack Street.

The department has increasingly been turning to digital services and partnerships to reduce the need for people to visit traditional Home Affairs offices.

One of the biggest changes has been its partnership with the banking sector, which has expanded access to Home Affairs services at participating bank branches.

According to Schreiber, South Africans can already access Smart ID replacement services at more than 450 bank branches across the country, including dozens in Cape Town.

World.title: South Africa’s next moon event has one timing detail worth knowing
World.content:
South Africa will see a deep partial lunar eclipse peak at 06:12 SAST on 28 August 2026: Image ChatGPT

South Africa will get a front-row seat to a deep partial lunar eclipse in the early hours of Friday, 28 August, with the Moon slipping almost entirely into Earth’s shadow just before sunrise.

When exactly to look up

The eclipse unfolds in stages, converted to South African time.

Earth’s outer shadow first touches the Moon at 03:23 SAST, though this phase is barely noticeable.



The visible partial eclipse begins at 04:33 SAST, when a dark section starts creeping across the Moon’s surface.

Maximum eclipse lands at 06:12 SAST, with around 96% of the Moon’s surface sitting inside Earth’s darkest shadow, the umbra.

What you’ll actually need

Unlike a solar eclipse, no special glasses or filters are required here.

This is entirely safe to watch with the naked eye, and a pair of binoculars will only sharpen the view.

Find an elevated spot with a clear, unobstructed western horizon, since the Moon will be low in the sky and setting as the eclipse builds toward its peak.

Where in the country you’ll have the best shot

Your odds may depend on where you’re standing.



South Africa’s interior plateau, including Gauteng, the Free State, and the Karoo, tends to see clearer skies during late winter, which could work in favour of these regions.

Cape Town and other coastal areas carry a higher general risk of winter rain or cloud cover this time of year, so it’s worth checking closer to the date rather than relying on this seasonal pattern alone.

Waking up before sunrise for anything is a big ask, hey, but a 96% eclipsed moon definitley feels worth the alarm.

Are you planning to catch this one, or is your bed winning this round?

Let us know in the comments below, Mzansi…

World.title: Ramaphosa says ANC deserves credit for ‘ending load shedding’
World.content:
President Cyril Ramaphosa says the African National Congress (ANC) deserves credit for ending load shedding in South Africa.

Ramaphosa said this while delivering the ANC’s manifesto for the 4 November local government elections at Riverside in Diepsloot, Gauteng, on Sunday, 23 August.

RAMAPHOSA HAILS ANC FOR ENDING LOAD SHEDDING

During his address, Ramaphosa said the country had recorded 460 consecutive days without load shedding, describing it as a major achievement for the ANC-led government.



“This is the work of the ANC… Seven of our provinces are now free from load reduction and work is continuing in the remaining affected areas in Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal. We know that while load shedding has largely ended there is load reduction and yes, our Department of Electricity is solving that problem on an ongoing basis,” he said.

South Africa experienced some of its most severe periods of load shedding in recent years as Eskom struggled to meet electricity demand because of ageing power stations, breakdowns and insufficient generation capacity.

WATCH🚨



ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa says the ANC deserves credit for ending load shedding in South Africa. pic.twitter.com/MvpzQvEqdX  August 23, 2026

COMMUNITIES CONTINUE TO EXPERIENCE LOAD REDUCTION

Load shedding is the controlled interruption of electricity supply to prevent the national grid from becoming overloaded when available generation is insufficient to meet demand.

However, South Africa has now gone more than a year without load shedding. Eskom says the country has been without load shedding since 16 May 2025, with improved generation performance and fewer unplanned outages contributing to the sustained improvement.

The utility has attributed the improvement to its Generation Recovery Plan, which has focused on improving the performance and availability of its power stations. Eskom has also reported lower reliance on diesel-fired generation and improved energy availability.



Despite the end of load shedding, some communities continue to experience load reduction.

Unlike load shedding, load reduction is primarily aimed at protecting overloaded local electricity distribution networks and infrastructure. Eskom says the programme was introduced in areas where overloaded networks posed a risk to infrastructure and supply reliability.

Ramaphosa said load reduction would also eventually end and argued that the progress demonstrated what could be achieved through effective leadership and cooperation.



“Load reduction will end and this achievement shows what can be achieved when there is clear leadership, skilled management, disciplined execution and cooperation across government, public institutions and business, labour and society,” he said.

Eskom has been progressively removing areas from load reduction schedules, with Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal among the provinces where work remains ongoing. The utility is targeting the eventual elimination of load reduction nationally.

Ramaphosa also praised Eskom’s improved performance.

World.title: Predicted Kaizer Chiefs XI vs Richards Bay: Change of shape?
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs are looking to extend their unbeaten run in the Betway Premiership this season. How will their starting XI look away at Richards Bay?

Predicted Kaizer Chiefs XI vs Richards Bay

Chiefs boss Fernando Da Cruz opted for a back three against Sundowns and it worked relatively well. They got a 1-1 draw, and limited Sundowns to an xG figure of 0.63 and just two shots on target. Langelihle Phili was on the score sheet and should keep his place in the attack. Siphesihle Ndlovu provided the assist.

Chiefs travel to Princess Magogo Stadium on 26 August at 19:30 to meet Richards Bay. Is this how they could line up?



3-5-2: Petersen; Kwinika, Moloisane, Miguel; Monyane, Ndlovu, Mthethwa, Maboe, Mmodi; Phili, Baartman.

Ngcobo’s Kaizer Chiefs future, writing on the wall already?

Meanwhile, Nkosingiphile Ngcobo’s dismal Chiefs stats merit closer observation. The attacking midfielderhasn’t managed more than two goals in a single season since 2020-21. He’s only scored two goals in his last three Betway Premiership seasons combined, and was excluded altogether against Sundowns in a recent 1-1 draw. The writing could be on the wall for Mshini.

Da Cruz must fulfil key criteria as the boss

Chiefs’ board will insist that Fernando Da Cruz elevates Chiefs to at least a runners-up spot during his tenure there. That would take them back into CAF competition and make them relevant on the continent again. Success in a cup competition will also be a priority. After MTN8 heartbreak, they’ve already lost one opportunity on that front. On the plus side, Chiefs remain unbeaten in the Betway Premiership. They’ve won matches against Kruger United and Sekhukhune, and held Sundowns to a 1-1 draw on Saturday. Seven points from a possible nine see Chiefs sit atop the embryonic table. Next up for the Glamour Boys is a trip to Richards Bay on 26 August. Let’s also remind ourselves that Chiefs won their opening three league clashes last term.

World.title: 'It was not yet Zolani's time' | Boxing world mourns Tete
World.content:
MDANTSANE - The death of former two-time boxing world champion Zolani Tete has been described as a huge loss, not only to the boxing fraternity but to the Eastern Cape at large.

Former boxer-turned-pastor Masibulele “Hawk” Makepula says the whole continent is devastated.

"People across the world are mourning Zolani's passing. Words cannot describe how we feel.

"No one came and said this was the will of God. No one can say Zolani ran his race and completed it, and no one can say his time came," Makepula said.

"It was not yet Zolani's time. His life was taken prematurely, and brutally so. Zolani died before his time."

July marked the end of Tete’s four-year ban following a doping scandal, which he denied. Makepula says Tete was ready to return to doing what he loved most.

"He kept himself fit and ready the whole time during the ban so that when the time came, he would be ready to get back in the ring.

"He was not selfish with his time and talent. He was training other boxers. It was only a matter of time before he became a world champion again. He was going to fight one or two fights and move on to a title fight because he was destined for greatness."

Boxing promoter Ayanda Matiti says what makes Tete’s death even more difficult to come to terms with is the way he was killed.

"It was a brutal assassination. No assassination can ever be accepted. Zolani was like a sheep; he did not deserve this.

"His body was full of bullets. Logic tells us that if it was a robbery, then they would have taken something. They did that to an unarmed man."

Matiti thanked authorities for acting swiftly but said this would be a difficult loss to overcome.

"We are all very sad. We are all mourning, not just his family or the boxing fraternity, but the whole province. In fact, the whole country," he said.

Tete was killed on Friday night while waiting for his gate to open. He was with a 27-year-old woman who was wounded and taken to hospital.

On Saturday, two people were taken in for questioning. One suspect, aged 30, was later released, but police spokesperson Brigadier Nobuntu Gantana said he remains a potential suspect.

The remaining 22-year-old suspect is appearing in the Mdantsane Magistrate’s Court. He has been charged with murder and attempted murder.

Two additional suspects, both aged 27, were arrested in Scenery Park on Sunday. They are expected to appear in court on Tuesday.

World.title: Springboks change half-backs for second All Blacks Test
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Springboks have changed their half-backs for the second Test against New Zealand on Saturday in Cape Town, promoting experienced duo Handre Pollard and Cobus Reinach.

Fly-half Pollard and scrum-half Reinach replace Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, now on the bench, and Grant Williams, who is unavailable due to a "niggle".

The changes were predictable as Feinberg-Mngomezulu, playing only his second match after injury, and Williams performed poorly in a 33-16 first Test loss last Saturday.

A third alteration to the team that fell in Johannesburg is Ethan Hooker coming in on the left wing in place of Kurt-Lee Arendse.

Arendse, who went off concussed early in the match at Ellis Park, moves to the right wing in place of Cheslin Kolbe, another "niggle" casualty.

There could yet be a fourth change to the starting line-up. If flanker Siya Kolisi is passed fit after a hamstring injury, he will replace Paul de Villiers.

"Handre has delivered for us under extreme pressure, and we feel that is what he and Cobus have the potential to bring at the beginning of the game," said head coach Rassie Erasmus.

"Then we have Morne (van den Berg) and Sacha coming on later with their different styles of play that will be good for us this weekend.

"Cheslin and Grant suffered niggles last weekend, which ruled them out of contention for selection.

"We have bracketed Siya alongside Paul to allow us time to monitor how Siya comes through training this week."

Loose forward Pieter-Steph du Toit will continue as captain and is set to win his 100th cap on Saturday, one week after centre Damian de Allende reached the milestone.

Ox Nche, widely regarded as the best loosehead prop in the world, will make his 50th appearance for the Springboks.

The bench has been reshuffled with only two survivors from the first Test -- 'hybrid' player Andre Esterhuizen, a centre who can play as a loose forward, and prop Gerhard Steenekamp.

Among those promoted is Deon Fourie, who will celebrate his 40th birthday in September. He can operate as a hooker or flanker.

Should he take the field, Fourie will become the oldest Springbok to play in a Test, surpassing Victor Matfield and Schalk Brits, who were 38 years old in their final Tests.

South Africa (15-1)

Damian Willemse; Kurt-Lee Arendse, Jesse Kriel, Damian de Allende, Ethan Hooker; Handre Pollard, Cobus Reinach; Jasper Wiese, Pieter-Steph du Toit (capt), Siya Kolisi or Paul de Villiers; Ruan Nortje, Eben Etzebeth; Wilco Louw, Malcolm Marx, Ox Nche

Replacements: Deon Fourie, Gerhard Steenekamp, Thomas du Toit, Lood de Jager, Andre Esterhuizen, Cameron Hanekom, Morne van den Berg, Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu

Coach: Rassie Erasmus

World.title: Four arrested for Tete murder
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Police say they have arrested four people in connection with the murder of two-time boxing world champion Zolani Tete, who was gunned down last week.



Tete, 38, was attacked on Friday evening as he returned to his home in Mdantsane in the Eastern Cape.



A 27-year-old woman who was with him in the car survived but is in hospital, police said.



The four suspects arrested over the weekend are aged between 22 and 28, police said in a statement.

One has been formally charged with murder.



Tete won the IBF junior-bantamweight world title in 2014 and the WBO bantamweight world title in 2017.



In 2017, he entered boxing history when he took just 11 seconds to flatten his opponent with his first punch to retain his WBO bantamweight crown.



It was the fastest knockout victory in a world championship bout.



In 2023, the UK Anti-Doping Agency hit Tete with a four-year ban that ended on July 29 and he was preparing to return to professional boxing.



"South Africa has lost one of the finest fighters it has ever produced," Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie said in a statement.



"He was training for a return to the ring. He believed he still had something to give this country. He was right, but he will not get the chance now. He, and all of us, have been robbed."

World.title: Still on old SASSA card? Here’s what you need to do before 31 August
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Social grant beneficiaries have until 31 August to migrate to the new black card.

Postbank says more than 1.8 million beneficiaries have already migrated.

It is urging those who have not yet done so to act quickly.

Postbank says additional measures have been put in place at card replacement sites, to manage the expected increase in beneficiaries in the final days.

READ | SASSA faces growing demand as grant beneficiaries near 20 million

The card migration process is free of charge and beneficiaries are required to have a valid or temporary ID.

Cards can be collected from any province, even if that is not the province in which a person’s SASSA grant was approved.

To migrate from an old SASSA Gold Card to the new Postbank Black Card, take your valid South African ID (or temporary ID) and your current gold card to a designated card replacement site, major retailer (such as Shoprite, Checkers, Usave, Boxer, Pick n Pay, or Spar), or participating Postbank site.

World.title: Devi | Rentoza | 23 August 2026
World.content:
Need a new phone? A laptop? A fridge? It’s rarely as simple as adding something to your cart and checking out – with credit hard to come by and the cost of living only climbing.

Enter Rentoza, with a simple pitch: why buy when you can subscribe? Monthly payments give South Africans access to the tech they need – with ownership at the end.

But hundreds of clients say the dream subscription became a monthly nightmare.

From refunds missing in action to contracts with apparent end dates – yet the debits keep rolling, month after month.

Initially, Rentoza’s management seemed eager to lay it all bare. But that enthusiasm quickly hit the rocks. So, we did things the old-fashioned way – and set up a sting.

Let’s just say… our surprise wasn’t exactly well received.

World.title: Bring back the VAR money, Gayton McKenzie tells SAFA
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Sports Minister Gayton McKenzie has slammed the South African Football Association (SAFA) over delays in implementing the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) system and now wants the association to pay back the money he provided for the project.

McKenzie says he has asked SAFA to return the R13 million he gave the association to help fund the implementation of VAR.

“I wrote a letter to SAFA and said they must return the money. They asked for 21 days’ grace. I am just as angry, because what more can I do? I asked them to bring back the money of the state because I am responsible for it,” McKenzie said.

READ | Disputed decision set to reignite calls for VAR in SA

McKenzie had previously promised that VAR would be implemented during the current season, but the technology has yet to be introduced.

The Minister insists he has done his part and says SAFA has failed to act.

“FIFA’s rules state clearly that it has to happen through SAFA. I took journalists and administrators to Spain and the UK to compare which one is the best for us. I can’t do more as a minister. What else can I do?”

World.title: ‘ANC cannot be trusted to fix what it has broken’ - DA
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The Democratic Alliance has slammed the ANC’s manifesto as "implausible".

The party says the ANC cannot be trusted to fix what it has broken.

The ANC launched its manifesto at the weekend ahead of the 4 November Local Government Elections, promising to turn around municipalities.

But the DA says the manifesto asks South Africans to believe that the same party that has presided over the collapse of municipalities across the country will suddenly fix them again.

“These promises are implausible and lack all integrity,” DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis said in a statement.

“The ANC cannot be trusted to fix what it has broken."

“South Africans deserve a different future with local governments that work, and ultimately a DA-led national government that brings the same culture of accountability, competence and service to the whole country,” Hill-Lewis added.

READ | ANC launches election manifesto in Diepsloot

While admitting his party’s failures over the years, ANC president Cyril Ramaphosa promised South Africans that they will do better.

“There are municipalities, we must admit, that are in financial trouble. There are municipalities that have been weakened by poor leadership, political instability, corruption and the appointment of people who do not have the skills required for the work that they must perform.

“Now, as the ANC, we comrades accept responsibility both for the progress that has been made, but we also accept responsibility for the failures and shortcomings where we govern,” Ramaphosa said.

He added that if citizens vote for the party, work will begin immediately after election day.

But the DA maintains the ANC will not perform miracles in 100 days and fill every critical municipal vacancy within 120 days.

World.title: Relief for schools as government releases Sh18.5b capitation
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Education CS Julius Ogamba. [File, Standard]

The government has released Sh18.5 billion in capitation to support operations in public basic education institutions during the third term of 2026, as schools reopened across the country on Monday.

Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba said the funds have already been released and will support learners in pre-primary, primary, junior and senior schools.

The allocation is intended to facilitate smooth school operations and ensure learning activities continue without disruption.

The Sh18.5 billion has been distributed across three major capitation programmes, with Free Day Secondary Education (FDSE) allocated Sh10.963 billion, accounting for the biggest portion of the Term Three capitation.

The money will support operations in public day and secondary schools and comes as institutions prepare learners for a busy academic term.

Free Day Junior School Education has received Sh6.1 billion, to support learners in the second tier of basic education and help institutions meet operational requirements as the Competency-Based Education system continues to expand.

Meanwhile, Free Primary Education has been allocated Sh1.4 billion to support learning in public primary schools.

The funds come as a relief to school heads who had raised concerns on the insufficient funds disbursed to schools this year.

However, Ogamba said the disbursement demonstrates the Government's commitment to ensuring that learners have access to free and compulsory basic education as provided for under Article 53(1)(b) of the Constitution.

“The Government affirms its commitment to fulfil its duty to learners and educational institutions,” said the CS.

Ogamba also warned school heads and principals against misuse of the funds, directing them to ensure the money is spent prudently and for the benefit of learners.

School administrators have further been cautioned against imposing unauthorised levies on parents and learners.

Ogamba said the Ministry would take firm action against institutions found to have misappropriated public resources or imposed illegal charges.

“We will deal firmly with any verified cases of misappropriation of resources and the imposition of unauthorised levies,” he said.

The warning comes as schools reopen for the third term, a period that is expected to be particularly demanding for institutions and learners because of the academic activities and assessments scheduled for the school calendar.

The Ministry has maintained that capitation is meant to ease the financial burden on families and enable schools to provide essential services without passing prohibited costs to parents.

Ogamba reiterated that school administrators must remain accountable for the public funds entrusted to them, warning that verified cases of misuse will attract action from the Ministry.

The Government has also reaffirmed that every child is entitled to free and compulsory basic education, placing the responsibility on education officials and school managers to ensure capitation achieves its intended purpose.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro begins nationwide political mobilisation ahead of 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro after attending service at Gathuki-ini ACK Church on August 23, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has said he will take his campaign for national transformation across Kenya as he positions himself for the 2027 presidential race.

Ndindi said he was interested in leadership committed to addressing concerns in education, health, youth and unemployment, among other needs.

Nyoro, who is the People’s Party of Kenya leader, spoke at St Michael Gathuki-ini ACK Church in Kiharu on Sunday, where he called for respect and political maturity.

Addressing residents in Kiria-ini (Mathioya) and Gakira (Kangema), he urged politicians to engage in a responsible manner.

“I trust in God that after next year Kenya will be able to have leadership that will be responsible for improving citizens' standards of living,” he said.

He regretted that hundreds of university graduates in the area were yet to secure employment.

“I plead with Kenyans to support my course that is geared to transform the nation and ensure equality and transparency,” said the PPK leader.

Nyoro said that after engaging Murang'a residents, he will take his transformation campaigns to all parts of the country.

Speaking at Kiria-ini market, he said he would engage the people to seek their blessings.

“All along had been feeling the urge to lead the country, thus the need to come out in the open and fight for position,” he said.

On Monday, the MP announced his exit from the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), declaring that he will join the opposition ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Nyoro, an economist serving his second term as Kiharu MP, said he will work with opposition leaders to push for what he termed real change in Kenya.

The legislator said all opposition presidential aspirants are welcome at rallies organised by the PPK.

His move marks a significant political shift as parties and leaders begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: City Hall in rush to expand drainage system ahead of El Nino
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja during an inspection tour of the ongoing drainage system expansion. [GPS]

Nairobi County has embarked on drainage expansion works aimed at mitigating floodwaters ahead of El Nino rains.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, while calling on city residents to remain alert and proactive, said City Hall has intensified preparations and accelerated identification of hotspots.

The governor on Friday said his administration is taking early and coordinated action to minimise the impact of heavy rains, urging residents to stay calm, pay attention to official information and follow guidance from the multi-agency team established to coordinate the city’s preparedness and emergency response.

“We are working proactively to address the challenges of flooding before El Nino hits the ground. We urge our people not to panic but to be alert and get information from our multi-agency team,” said Sakaja.

The Governor spoke during an inspection tour of several flood-prone areas in Nairobi, including the Mombasa Road-Bunyala Junction corridor and Globe Roundabout, which experienced significant flooding during previous heavy rains.

Sakaja said drainage works are already underway in the affected areas, with teams working to open up and deepen drainage channels, clear obstructions, and improve storm-water flow to prevent a repeat of the flooding witnessed previously.

His remarks come as weatherman warned of increased rainfall in the coming months, with Nairobi among the urban areas requiring heightened preparedness because of its exposure to flooding and the impact of heavy rainfall on roads, settlements and other critical infrastructure.

Sakaja said the county has so far brought together the disaster management teams, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) and Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) under a coordinated programme worth Sh2.4 billion to strengthen Nairobi’s flood resilience.

Of the amount, Sh2 billion has been set aside for drainage and flood-mitigation works targeting 19 roads in flood-prone areas.

The projects are at an advanced stage, with tenders awarded and contractors expected to commence implementation after completion of the necessary processes.

Sakaja reiterated that the programme will complement ongoing county interventions under the Nairobi Regeneration Programme, which includes the rehabilitation and upgrading of critical infrastructure across the city.

“The Sh2 billion will support a comprehensive drainage overhaul that complements the ongoing Nairobi Regeneration Programme. Our goal is to permanently address the flooding challenges that have affected the city for many years,” Sakaja said.

He said the focus is not only on responding to floods after they occur, but on addressing the infrastructure weaknesses that have historically made Nairobi vulnerable to flooding.

To strengthen preparedness, the county has established five specialised sub-committees under the multi-agency framework.

The committees include Infrastructure and Drainage; Emergency Response and Evacuation; Shelter and Relief; Security and Traffic and Communication.

While the Infrastructure and Drainage committee will coordinate the clearing and improvement of drainage systems, rivers and other critical infrastructure, the Emergency Response and Evacuation committee will oversee rapid response, rescue and evacuation operations whenever emergencies occur.

The Shelter and Relief committee will prepare safe shelters and coordinate the provision of food, water, medical assistance and other essential support to affected residents.

The Security and Traffic committee will coordinate security, traffic management and emergency access, while the Communication committee will strengthen early-warning systems, public alerts and timely dissemination of information.

Sakaja said the county is also mobilising personnel, equipment and other resources to clear blocked drains, remove silt and waste and strengthen emergency response systems in areas identified as vulnerable.

He urged residents and their associations, businesses and other stakeholders to play an active role in flood preparedness by keeping drainage areas clear and paying attention to official warnings.

The county chief said residents in high-risk areas will be provided with timely information on emerging weather conditions and the actions they should take when heavy rains occur.

“We don’t want people to panic. We want people to be proactive, to listen to information and to work with us. The multi-agency team is in place, and we are preparing before the rains intensify,” Sakaja said.

According to him, the multi-agency approach will also help eliminate jurisdictional gaps by bringing together national and county agencies to operate as one coordinated team.

He said the combination of drainage upgrades, emergency preparedness, early-warning systems and coordinated response would strengthen Nairobi’s resilience and reduce disruption caused by heavy rains.

The multi-agency team is expected to meet next week to review progress, coordinate ongoing works and further push the city’s El Niño preparedness agenda.

World.title: Public officers eyeing elective posts to resign by February 10 - IEBC
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon addressing the press at a past press conference. [File, Standard]

Public officers seeking to contest elective positions in the 2027 General Election have until February 10, 2027, to resign from office, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has announced.

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon said the deadline falls exactly six months before the August 10, 2027, General Election, which the Commission has confirmed will be held on a Tuesday.

“Any public officer who intends to contest in this election must resign from public office by Wednesday, 10th February 2027, which is exactly six months before the election,” Ethekon said.

The IEBC said adherence to the timelines will be non-negotiable, noting that they are legally binding and essential to ensuring an orderly electoral process.

Under the timetable, political parties must submit their membership lists and details of candidates participating in party primaries by March 16, 2027.

Party primaries and any related disputes must be concluded by May 8, while independent candidates are also required to meet their legal obligations by the same date.

Presidential aspirants will have until May 24 to submit lists of supporting voters drawn from a majority of Kenya’s counties.

Candidate registration will begin on May 29, with specific deadlines applying to the various elective positions.

The official campaign period will commence after candidates are registered, but not earlier than May 29, 2027.

Ethekon warned political parties, candidates and their supporters against breaching the prescribed campaign period, saying any electioneering outside the legal window will be unlawful.

The restrictions cover campaign posters, billboards, political caravans and other forms of campaigning.

Campaigning will close on August 7, 2027, 48 hours before Kenyans head to the polls.

“The law prescribes when election campaigns may commence,” Ethekon said, urging political parties, candidates and their supporters to strictly comply with electoral laws and regulations.

The deadline is among key milestones unveiled by the electoral commission as political parties, aspirants and other stakeholders begin preparations for the next General Election.

World.title: Schools will open on August 24 as scheduled, Ogamba says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Students heading home during recent demonstrations. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Ministry of Education said the official academic calendar remains unchanged.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, August 19, Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba insists that learners will return to school on Monday, August 24, 2026.

The CS has dismissed reports circulating on social media claiming that the reopening of schools for the third term has been postponed, warning parents, teachers, learners and education stakeholders against relying on unauthorised online notices.

“We wish to clarify that the academic calendar for Basic Education institutions and Teacher Training Colleges remains unchanged,” the CS said.

The clarification comes two days before the scheduled reopening of schools, amid reports circulating on social media platforms suggesting that the government had pushed back the start of Term III.

"Our attention has been drawn to misleading information circulating on various social media platforms, purporting that the academic calendar for basic education institutions and Teachers Training Colleges has been changed," he stated.

The Ministry termed the reports “FALSE” and urged members of the public to completely disregard them.

Ogamba said the Ministry had directed Regional Directors of Education, County Directors of Education and Sub-County Directors of Education to ensure strict compliance with the approved academic calendar contained in a circular dated October 9, 2025.

According to the Ministry, pre-primary, primary, junior, senior and secondary schools will begin Term III on Monday, August 24. The term will run for nine weeks and end on October 23, 2026.

The reopening marks the final academic term of the school year, with schools expected to implement the approved programmes as they prepare learners for the end-of-year national assessments and examinations.

Diploma Teachers Training Colleges will also resume academic operations on August 24, with their third term scheduled to conclude on November 6, 2026.

The Ministry further confirmed that the national assessment and examination calendar has not been altered for KPSEA, KILEA, KJSEA, KPLEA and KCSE are scheduled to begin from October 26, 2026, as earlier announced.

The Ministry also reminded schools that extracurricular activities and visits to secondary schools will remain banned during Term III.

The latest clarification is part of efforts by the government to prevent confusion among parents, learners and teachers as schools prepare to reopen.

Ogamba urged education stakeholders to obtain information through official Ministry communication channels, rather than social media posts whose authenticity cannot be established.

“Parents, teachers and learners and members of the public are advised to strictly rely on the Ministry's official communication channels and field officers for accurate information," he said.

World.title: Ruto denies Sh104bn SHA technology contract
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto has dismissed claims that the government entered into a controversial Sh104 billion contract with Safaricom and Apeiro Limited for the Social Health Authority (SHA) technology system.

Speaking on Tuesday evening at the Presidential Townhall held during the National Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto defended the government's investment in digital health, saying the technology was designed to improve transparency and accountability in the management of SHA services.

“There is no Sh104 billion contract. What we have done is design a digital system to make sure that everything is visible. Every treatment must be traceable, and every payment must be accounted for,” Ruto said.

He explained that the government had not purchased the technology outright but had engaged investors who own the equipment, with the State paying for the services provided.

His remarks were echoed by Digital Health Agency Chief Executive Anthony Lenaiyara, who rejected claims that SHA had committed Sh104 billion to technology upgrades.

“It is not correct or true that SHA has undertaken any upgrade or invested Sh104 billion in technology upgrades. What we did is build a digital superhighway comprising 43 systems to support Universal Health Coverage,” Lenaiyara said.

Lenaiyara said the technology infrastructure had been rolled out without requiring health facilities to purchase the devices, adding that the system had transformed the processing and accountability of SHA claims.

He contrasted the new system with the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) model, where claims were processed using physical files that moved between different offices for verification and approval.

Ruto also addressed other government programmes, saying the State had mobilised resources to construct 23,000 additional classrooms to ease pressure caused by shortages of learning spaces.

World.title: 'That was not healthcare, it was theft'- Ruto on old health system
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during the official opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC), Nairobi, August 18,2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has accused the defunct National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) system of enabling theft from sick Kenyans, citing claims for procedures that never happened.

Speaking on Tuesday, August 18, at the opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto described the old system as opaque and vulnerable to abuse.

"We heard of claims for procedures that never happened, fictitious patients and inflated bills. That was not healthcare, it was theft, and theft from sick Kenyans," said Ruto.

He called digital health systems the backbone holding the reforms together and said they would close loopholes that let people profit from the system's weaknesses.

Ruto ranked Universal Health Coverage (UHC) alongside the Affordable Housing Programme as one of the government's most consequential social transformation efforts, crediting collaboration between national and county governments for changes in how healthcare is financed, delivered and accounted for.

The two-day summit, themed "Reforms Delivered, Health as a Right," has drawn more than 5,000 delegates to audit progress under the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) and set priorities for the remainder of Ruto's term, according to Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale.

Ruto said 32.3 million Kenyans are now registered with the Social Health Authority (SHA), which replaced NHIF in October 2024.

Eight million have received treatment, more than 1.2 million mothers have been supported to deliver safely and more than 500,000 surgical procedures have been supported, he added.

He put Kenyans' previous annual out-of-pocket health spending at Sh150 billion ($1.16 billion), saying families had borrowed, sold assets or organised harambees to cover medical costs before the reforms.

"Millions paid out of pocket, borrowed, sold assets, organised harambees or stayed away from hospital because they could not afford care," said Ruto.

Since October 2024, SHA has received more than Sh209 billion ($1.62 billion) and paid more than Sh178 billion ($1.38 billion) to contracted facilities across all 47 counties, Ruto added.

He credited 107,800 Community Health Promoters, deployed under a shared financing arrangement between national and county governments, with reaching more than nine million households and referring over 750,000 people for further treatment.

On supply chains, Ruto said the Kenya Medical Supplies Authority's (KEMSA) fill rate had risen from about 40 per cent to 91 per cent, helped by a Sh1.5 billion ($11.6 million) recapitalisation and a Sh10 billion ($77.4 million) credit line.

The reforms rest on four laws Ruto signed on 19 October 2023: the Primary Health Care Act, the Social Health Insurance Act, the Digital Health Act and the Facilities Improvement Financing Act.

Ruto acknowledged gaps remained in registration, benefit clarity, claims processing and digital systems.

"The ultimate measure of reform is not the laws we pass or the numbers we register, but the experience of the patient in terms of dependable, affordable and dignified care," said Ruto.

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki, Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, Duale and Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja attended the opening session, alongside county governors, principal secretaries, members of Parliament and development partners.

The summit runs through Wednesday.

World.title: Gachagua: Opposition does not need Uhuru's money to send Ruto home
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua during a church service at PCEA Rev. Samuel Marima Memorial Church in Gatundu South, Kiambu on August 16, 2026. [Kimaku Chege, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed claims that former President Uhuru Kenyatta is financing opposition activities against President William Ruto.

Addressing the allegations that Kenyatta was financing opposition campaigns, Gachagua insisted that the movement did not require money from the former President.

Gachagua says the movement seeking political change is driven by Kenyans and does not depend on financial sponsorship.

“Nasikia kwamba Uhuru is sponsoring us to campaign against you. Uhuru is not sponsoring us, we don't need any sponsorship, this is a mass movement for change which does not need funding,” he said.

He was speaking on Sunday, August 16, 2026, during a church service at PCEA Rev. Samuel Marima Memorial Church in Gatundu South, Kiambu County.

Gachagua further said the opposition had sufficient public support to challenge the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election, insisting that Kenyans themselves were the driving force behind calls for a change of government.

He added that the public itself would determine the political fate of the Ruto administration.

“We don't need money but Kenyans will send you home,” Gachagua said.

The comments come against the backdrop of renewed debate over political alliances and the role of former leaders in Kenya's 2027 succession politics. Kenyatta, who served as President from 2013 to 2022, has largely remained outside the day-to-day administration of government since handing over power to Ruto.

Gachagua also defended Kenyatta against what he described as attempts to drag the former President into the current political contest.

“Uhuru Kenyatta asiguzwe na mtu yeyote. Alindwe na atetewe na apatiwe amani. Uhuru alifanya kazi yake na akastaafu,” Gachagua said.

The former Deputy President said Kenyatta should not be treated as a political candidate or blamed for the activities of opposition politicians.

“Nimemwambia Ruto unauliza Uhuru nini na sio candidate in the next election. I am your main opponent,” Gachagua said.
