World.title: Split Port: Passengers Wait in 40 Degree Heat With No Shelter From Sun
World.content:
August the 23rd, 2026 – Split Port is rapidly turning into a proverbial pizza oven as passengers have to wait in 40 degree heat with no shelter from the sun whatsoever.

At Split Port, passengers must wait to board in temperatures above 35 degrees in the shade, while on the scorching asphalt and with high humidity the perceived heat regularly exceeds 40 degrees. Lukrecija Zderic reports for Index that all of this takes place without a canopy under which people could take any form of shelter. With all the belongings they’re carrying on their journey, they must stand on the burning asphalt, exposed to the insufferable strength of the summer sun, with almost no shade available.

Parents with children, the elderly, and those waiting for the ferry try to find at least a scrap of shade under the smaller palm trees. Ferries come and go, the queues move, and passengers wait in the sun with no place to hide from the heat.

The problem becomes even greater when the catamaran or ferry is delayed and passengers don’t know exactly when it will arrive. This is precisely what happened to one of our readers, who wished to remain anonymous. With her family she had to wait in the port, in the sun and without adequate shelter, and she told Index how disappointing the whole situation was.

“It was a working day and we were supposed to travel by catamaran to Korčula. Unfortunately it was late, but that wasn’t the only problem. The biggest problem is that in Split’s port you almost have nowhere to shelter from the sun. The berths for the catamarans are far from the main, and practically the only, canopy in the port,” our interlocutor said.

“There’s often no space in the cafe or bar, and if you don’t know exactly when the catamaran will arrive or which berth it will dock at, which happens frequently, you can’t even move away to look for a shady spot. It was a heatwave, it was extremely hot, and with children it was a truly terrible experience,” the reader told us.

“if i hadn’t found shade, i’d have become unwell in the sun”

So we went to Split’s port to check whether the catamarans were late and how passengers spend their time waiting for them in the sun. Because the fact is that at the berths there is nowhere to shelter from the heat. During our arrival and the following three hours in the port, a large number of catamarans arrived and departed, and almost all of them arrived on time. The biggest delay we recorded was around ten minutes, which can hardly be called a serious delay, and it did not bother the passengers either. But what many would apparently gladly change is a simple thing – that instead of waiting on the scorching sun, they could wait for the ferry in the shade.

“It’s extremely hot, but it doesn’t bother me that much because I’m by the sea. It’s a bit inconvenient standing in the sun waiting for the ferry to Dubrovnik, so I try to find any little scrap of shade. This is more of a shadow, but it will do,” a tourist travelling to Dubrovnik told us.

“I saw that today it’s 35 degrees, and it’s the same in London, but I have to admit it’s much nicer here. Maybe because we’re on holiday, but if I hadn’t found a little shade, I would have gone crazy in the sun,” a tourist from England told us. Catamarans in Split’s City Port don’t all dock in one place; they use different berths along the operational quay. Some of them are located outside the main building of the maritime-passenger terminal. At the same time, works are underway in Split’s port on Sv. Duje Pier, where a new international maritime-passenger terminal is being built.

infrastructure upgrades – but nothing to deal with the issue of ensuring shade

Once completed, the project should take over part of the international traffic and free up Sv Duje Pier for domestic scheduled traffic, i.e. better connections between Split and the islands. But while the port infrastructure is being changed and expanded, the question remains whether the problem of protecting passengers who wait for catamarans in the open will also be solved, especially during the summer months and heatwaves.

While waiting for their catamaran, passengers try in various, and some quite inventive, ways to protect themselves from the sun. Umbrellas, caps and hats become the main defence against the scorching rays, while some hide in long sleeves and others seek refuge in the rare scraps of shade. The benches under the palm trees thus become sought-after spots, and passengers settle into every available bit of shade, however small.

“It’s very hot, we’re not used to this. We’ve put on long sleeves and are protecting ourselves with an umbrella. We hope our catamaran to Dubrovnik will arrive soon because it’s really hard to breathe here,” Japanese passengers told us. There were, however, also those who did not allow the heat to spoil their holiday mood.

“We’re from Germany and we’re only briefly in Split, and now we’re going to Hvar. We don’t have any special way of protecting ourselves from the sun; we simply try to find a little shade, although that’s not exactly easy here. We don’t want to complain – we’ve come on holiday, we’re by the sea and we’re going to one of the most beautiful islands. We won’t let a few minutes in the sun spoil our mood,” a married couple from Germany told us.

During the summer, Split Port is one of the busiest places in the city every day, yet there’s no respite from the intense heat. Back in 2024 alone, more than five million passengers passed through it on ferries and catamarans, of which more than a million on catamarans. This is a huge number of people who pass through the port every day during the season, and some of them wait for their catamarans precisely in the open, exposed to the sun and temperatures that during heatwaves exceed 35 degrees.

World.title: Estonian shooter wins world clay pigeon gold in sporting first
World.content:
Shooter Veikko Tihvan has made Estonian sports history by winning the FITASC Compak Sporting World Championships in Rio Salso, Italy.

Tihvan initially shared first place with multiple European and world championship medalist Charles Bardou of France after both hit 197 of 200 targets in Thursday's competition.

A shoot-off beckoned, which Tihvan won after beating the French competitor by one target, making him the first Estonian to win the title.

Clay pigeon shooting is a type of practical hunting shooting which simulates real-world hunting conditions, instead of having flat and static ranges. Not "pigeons" as such, the targets are saucer shaped, made of pulverized limestone and brightly colored.

Compak Sporting is a discipline of clay pigeon shooting governed internationally by FITASC (Fédération Internationale de Tir aux Armes Sportives de Chasse). As its name suggests, it is held on a compact shooting layout designed for use in a smaller area, compared with standard competitive clay pigeon shooting.

World.title: Nearly 1,900 basic school graduates still lack a school place as year begins
World.content:
A week before the start of the new school year, 1,893 basic school graduates in Estonia are without a school place; of them, 761 live in Tallinn, said Kadi Serbak, adviser at the Ministry of Education (HTM).

According to Serbak, HTM monitors the situation of finding school places daily. Since continued admissions to schools are still underway, HTM does not yet have a complete overview of young people who have not found a new study place after finishing basic school. Schools must enter admitted students into the Estonian Education Information System, from which HTM can see how many students are still without a school place.

HTM's project manager for compulsory education, Külli Solo, said that many schools do not do this during the admissions process, and there are young people who have received a school place but have not been entered into the information system.

The final number of basic school graduates who will not continue their studies will be known around 10 September. According to HTM data, in previous years about 800 basic school graduates have not continued their studies. The forecast is the same for this year.

Serbak said the ministry is trying to find solutions to the current situation in cooperation with local governments.

The ministry is analysing how to make basic school graduation and finding school places smoother and less stressful next year. "We have also informed the city of Tallinn that we would like to discuss options for increasing the number of preparatory study places ordered at Tallinn Applied College," Serbak said.

Continued admissions underway

Ülle Matsin, head of HTM's department of general and vocational education, told ERR last week that schools are conducting continued admissions every day, which means that eventually all students will find a study place.

"There is definitely a study place available to fulfil compulsory education, and if students currently still need counselling, they can confidently contact the schools where admissions are still ongoing," Matsin said.

"All learners will find opportunities to study. Through cooperation between the state and the city, study places in Tallinn should ultimately be available for all students," she confirmed.

Tallinn deputy mayor Andrei Kante said last week that the reason so many young people still lack clarity about their study options at the end of August is that basic school is being completed by young people without learning skills.

Matsin agreed that basic education holds several keys: a basic school graduate should receive guidance on where to continue studying and be aware that vocational fields offer many learning opportunities.

"We have actually pointed this out earlier in our messaging — that career counselling in basic school is important, and preparing the student at the end of the third school stage to move forward is crucial. In that respect, he is undoubtedly right," the ministry official said.

Tartu also has young people without school places

As of Friday, Tartu had around one hundred young people who have not found a school place, have not looked for one, or have left Estonia altogether, such as Ukrainian war refugees. This number is still constantly changing, said Riho Raave, head of Tartu's education department.

He said continued admissions are underway in some upper secondary schools and vocational institutions in Tartu, such as Tartu Applied College and Tartu Art School. "Applications are ongoing and the process is still underway, so I think by 1 September there will be even fewer who have not found a study place," Raave noted.

In connection with compulsory education, preparatory study will also begin for the first time this academic year. It is intended for young people up to age 18 who need support after basic school to move on to the next level of education.

According to Raave, the problem in Tartu is that all state‑funded preparatory study places at both Tartu Art School and the Applied College are already full.

Raave said schools had the option to admit students to preparatory study on their own. "Students applied, schools accepted them, but now there are no preparatory study places left for the most complex group of students — those who cannot find a school place," he explained. Raave believes more places need to be created.

Preparatory study should be an extreme measure

Solo said that ongoing continued admissions may still bring changes to preparatory study places, but negotiations with local governments are underway regarding the number of study places.

"Preparatory study is an extreme measure, intended specifically for those 800 young people who do not continue studying," Solo said.

In early August, it became clear that HTM wants to begin admissions to preparatory study next year starting from 1 September — that is, after basic and continued admissions. This should ensure that preparatory study is offered only to those young people who do not have a study place by 1 September or who need additional support.

World.title: Financial Intelligence Unit awaits restoration of powers by Riigikogu
World.content:
A bill aimed at clarifying the Financial Intelligence Unit's (FIU) access to banking data and restoring its ability to conduct on-site inspections has passed its first reading in the Riigikogu.

The final vote could come as early as October. Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise, now the only formally registered presidential candidate, has endorsed the bill and, if it passes and she is elected president, it could end up on her desk for assent or veto.

The bill would address two major restrictions on the FIU: its ability to access bank account information through the enforcement register and its ability to carry out on-site inspections at banks and other institutions.

The legislation follows concerns raised by Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise about the legal basis for government agencies accessing bank account information through the enforcement register. The unit's access was suspended by Minister of Justice and Digital Affairs Liisa Pakosta (Eesti 200).

The restrictions also affected the Tax and Customs Board (MTA), which was unable to request certain data through the register for tax-fraud prevention and other duties until the government reversed course in May.

The government has since proposed amendments specifying when and how the FIU and MTA may request banking data through the enforcement register. The Finance Ministry has stressed that the amendments do not create new substantive powers to access banking secrecy, but clarify that existing powers may be exercised through the enforcement register, a secure and logged channel.

Under the proposed framework, requests would have to be justified and logged, while people would have the ability to challenge an administrative act authorising access.

The Estonian-founded LHV Pank, for example, has stopped providing bank account statements to the FIU, saying the unit has no legal right to request them. The Tallinn Administrative Court ruled in the bank's favor, although the FIU has appealed.

FIU chief Matis Mäeker said the restrictions are also affecting Estonia's ability to cooperate with its international partners, and that this is harming Estonia in return.

In her role as Chancellor of Justice, Ülle Madise raised concerns which led to a diminishing of the FIU's powers. However, a bill restoring them could end up being signed by her if it passes and if she gets elected president in early September. Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

"If you are a good partner, you get answers more quickly; if you are a worse partner, you get answers more slowly. At the moment, we are in a situation where we cannot answer all questions as we do not have the right to request this data," Mäeker said.

Mäeker gave as an example one case in which fraudulently obtained money was transferred to another country one day, then by the following day had already been moved to accounts at 14 different credit institutions, making recovering the funds increasingly difficult.

The FIU's powers were further restricted by a Supreme Court ruling in January. The body can no longer physically visit, for example, a bank or a gambling company, in order to check compliance with its anti-money-laundering (AML) procedures.

On-site inspections are an "irreplaceable" tool for a supervisory authority, Mäeker added.

"One thing is what happens on paper, another is what happens in real life. To understand whether what is on paper actually corresponds to reality, you can only find out on site," he said.

The bill would address both issues. It would clarify the division and extent of the powers of the FIU and MTA to obtain information needed for their duties, particularly bank account and account data, while also restoring the FIU's ability to conduct on-site inspections.

The opposition parties have signaled support for the bill, though some MPs have questioned its lengthy notification deadlines. Aivar Kokk (Isamaa), a member of the Riigikogu Finance Committee, said he could not understand how it could ever be justified to keep a person unaware for so long that their bank account had been examined. Andrei Korobeinik (Center) warned that notification could potentially be postponed repeatedly.

Under the terms of the bill, a person or company would normally be notified five years after their bank account statement was obtained. In certain circumstances, notification could be postponed for up to another five years — meaning that in some cases, the person or company might not learn about the examination for as long as 10 years.

Maris Lauri (Reform), who is leading work on the bill in the Finance Committee, said she wants to hear further justification from interest groups regarding the time limits. She noted that the current deadlines may be optimal, but discussions are continuing. If consideration proceeds without major obstacles, the Riigikogu could adopt the bill as early as October.

FIU chief Matis Mäeker. Source: ERR

LHV has raised broader privacy and legal concerns about the proposed rules. Ants Soone, LHV's head of compliance, wrote that since 2021 the FIU has no longer been an investigative body and lacks the right to conduct surveillance measures. He argued that treating the examination of bank statements as a surveillance measure could raise questions about whether evidence obtained in this way would be admissible in court.

Soone also objected to the possibility of retaining information covered by bank confidentiality for five to 10 years "just in case," arguing that mass retention of personal data like this could conflict with EU fundamental-rights law.

Madise has also weighed in, saying she did not oppose the bill in principle. She agreed that the FIU and/or the MTA should be able to access bank account statements via the enforcement register when investigating specific suspicions, but said the Riigikogu should carefully consider whether the proposed notification periods are truly necessary or should be shortened.

If the bill passes, it would address concerns Madise raised as Chancellor of Justice. Madise is, at the time of writing, the only formally registered candidate in the presidential elections taking place in the Riigikogu, with a few hours to go until registration closes. If the 74 MPs who signed in favour of her candidacy — or a minimum of 68 MPs — translate that backing into a vote for Madise as president on September 2-3, she will become the next head of state.

If that happened, she would then have the power as president to sign or veto legislation on the same topic herself.

The money laundering bill's final reading may take place in October, as things stand.

World.title: Kaamos art grant to focus on artists over 60
World.content:
The Kaamos art scholarship, awarded for the first time last year, is this year intended for artists over 60. The amount of the scholarship is 25,000 euros.

While the focus in the first year was on women artists, Kaamos has now decided that the scholarship's target group will change each year in order to draw attention to different groups within the Estonian art field and their work, and to keep the scholarship diverse and evolving over time.

The Kaamos art scholarship was established by the Estonian Centre for Contemporary Art and Estonian-owned investment firm Kaamos Group. Candidates are invited to apply until 28 September; artists may apply themselves or be nominated by someone working in the art field or by an art institution.

The recipient will be chosen by a jury consisting of Kumu curator Eha Komissarov, head of Tartu Art House and chair of the Tartu Artists' Union Peeter Talvistu, artist and artist‑salary recipient Marge Monko, one representative of the CCA and two representatives of Kaamos Group. The composition of the jury rotates partially every two years.

Last year, the first Kaamos scholarship was awarded to Anna Mari Liivrand. "The Kaamos scholarship came unexpectedly and at a very right moment for me," said last year's laureate. "With the support of the scholarship, I have been able to fully dedicate myself to both larger and smaller exhibition projects, and I see that it has helped me create more substantial and exciting works."

World.title: Government to begin next year's budget talks on Tuesday
World.content:
The government will begin discussions on next year's budget and the state budget strategy at Stenbock House on Tuesday.

Deputy director of government communications Liis Velsker said that on Tuesday and Wednesday this week, members of the government will start discussions on next year's state budget and the state budget strategy for the next four years.

On Thursday, the Ministry of Finance will present the summer economic forecast to the cabinet.

The economic forecast is used by the government and parliament when making budget‑policy decisions, and by businesses when preparing strategic plans. The explanatory memorandum also gives the wider public an overview of recent economic developments and the outlook for the next four years.

"Over the coming weeks, the government will discuss the budget. At the end of September, the government will approve the revenue, expenditure and other measures of the state budget and the state budget strategy, as well as the Health Insurance Fund's budget position for the next four years, and all draft laws related to next year's state budget. The goal is also to approve the allocation of EU support for the 2028–2034 period — the state plan," Velsker said.

She added that at the end of September, the government must submit the draft state budget for 2027 to the Riigikogu and approve the state budget strategy for 2027–2030. Before that, the government will hear the opinion of the Fiscal Council.

World.title: ISS calls for dedicated law to standardize background checks
World.content:
An internal security advisory to the interior minister urges basic background checks for people in critical posts, a need heightened by recent security developments. Estonian Internal Security Service (ISS) calls for a separate law to resolve the legal issues.

Each year, the security agencies present the interior minister with their view on what the state should do to ensure internal security and public safety.

In this year's advisory, ISS notes that the need to conduct background checks for employees in critical positions has risen sharply due to Russia's aggressive behavior, highlighting the defense‑industry sector as one example. The legal basis for conducting such checks should be set out in a dedicated background‑check law, said ISS spokesperson Marta Tuul.

"A general regulation would help ensure security more effectively. Right now, background checks are carried out under several special laws — the Aviation Act, the Imprisonment Act, the Defence Forces Organization Act, the Police and Border Guard Act, and others. These all cover different fields, meaning their requirements and guidelines differ and are not uniform," Tuul explained.

She added that background checks are already conducted for applicants to higher‑risk positions, and ISS does not see a need to expand that circle.

"In recent years — due to the security situation and the war in Ukraine — the number of background checks has increased year by year, but expanding the scope is not necessary," Tuul said.

Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200). Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Interior minister Igor Taro, however, said that additional positions requiring background checks have emerged.

"We have developed sensitive positions involving state secrets, and we have looked much more closely at whom we hire for critical infrastructure related to essential services — there are certain positions there that also require checks," Taro said.

Amendments to the Emergency Act that took effect in 2024 expanded the list of essential service providers. Estonia now has 22 essential services provided by more than 400 companies. The most recent additions include family‑doctor services, the supply of medicines and food, aeronautical navigation, airports, ports and public railway services. Under the Emergency Act, candidates for critical positions in such services must undergo background checks.

An employer or state institution cannot conduct a background check arbitrarily — there must be a direct legal basis, and the person must be informed that a background check will be carried out.

World.title: Riga and Vilnius outpace Tallinn in flights due to market size
World.content:
Although Tallinn has fewer direct destinations, Tallinn Airport is still the largest airport in the Baltics in terms of revenue, surpassing both Latvia and Lithuania, says airport chief Riivo Tuvike. Last year Tallinn Airport's revenue was 74 million euros.

This success comes from the fact that Tallinn Airport does not rely solely on aviation fees, which make up only about 30% of its income. The company actively earns revenue from terminal retail, parking, aircraft maintenance hangars and commercial real estate in Airport City.

Tallinn Airport has also experienced a historic surge in passenger numbers this summer, driven by expanding flight options and more affordable ticket prices.

The airport shattered its all-time passenger records during June and July. Tuvike noted that in July, the airport welcomed 384,000 passengers, representing a 19 percent increase compared to the previous year. The appetite for travel has not disappeared since the pandemic, and higher local wealth combined with lower prices has fueled this growth.

Looking at history, in 1991 Tallinn Airport had 758,000 passengers, but the following year, 1992, only about 205,000, so there was a large drop. "Looking at the current year, we believe we will reach 3.7–3.8 million passengers, which is quite a noticeable increase," Tuvike said.

The long-term goal is serving five million travelers annually by 2030.

Passenger volume dictates the decisions

When asked why the airport does not aggressively lower its fees to attract even more airlines, Tuvike points out that market demand and passenger volume — not just cheap airport fees — ultimately dictate an airline's route decisions.

"We could lower the fees even to zero, but if there are no passengers, the airlines will not open those routes," Tuvike said.

"Perhaps our concern in Tallinn is that the region we are able to serve is only about one million passengers. In the end, the number of potential passengers dictates how many possible direct routes there can be," he noted.

Riivo Tuvike Autor/allikas: Iris Tähema/ERR

Despite the current positive passenger trends, the regional aviation market faces challenges, particularly concerning the financial health of Latvian carrier airBaltic. AirBaltic remains Estonia's most important airline and operates as a home carrier, but Tuvike believes the Estonian government should not buy a stake in the struggling airline.

The entire Baltic region is a very small area in a global scale, Tuvike said. He added that operating a profitable airline in such a limited market is extremely difficult and suggested there are more reasonable areas for state investment.

The airport chief reassured travelers that even if airBaltic were to exit the market, Estonia's flight connections would not collapse. He explained that Tallinn has actively diversified its airline portfolio, such as by facilitating the expansion of low-cost carrier Wizz Air, to ensure that routes can be replaced if necessary.

The rapid growth in passenger traffic has placed significant strain on the existing airport infrastructure. The current terminal was designed to handle up to three million passengers, meaning the current volume is already causing operational friction, including baggage wait times that can reach an hour.

Major expansion of the Tallinn airport ongoing

To address these bottlenecks, the airport is planning a major physical expansion. Tuvike said that while new check-in kiosks have already been installed, the main construction work is scheduled to begin early next year. The project aims to expand the passenger terminal by 50 percent by the first half of 2029, with a specific focus on enlarging the overcrowded baggage claim and border control areas.

Regarding flight destinations, Tuvike emphasized that major hubs remain the most critical connections for Estonian travelers because they open access to the rest of the world. Currently, Warsaw has emerged as the number one destination, with Frankfurt, Riga, and Helsinki also making up the majority of flights.

Tuvike mentioned that while direct flights largely dictate where Estonians go on vacation, his future target destinations for direct flights from Tallinn include London Heathrow and Madrid.

"London Heathrow is definitely a place where we really want to go, because there are so many flight opportunities and it contributes strongly to Estonia's connection," Tuvike said.

Tuvike also addressed the future of Estonia's regional airports, noting that while airports on the country's islands are fully justified due to the lack of fast land transport, the future of mainland facilities like Pärnu Airport is less certain. He pointed out that once the Rail Baltica railway is completed, Pärnu will be just a 45-minute journey from Tallinn, making the local airport's role highly questionable.

World.title: Iraq to raise oil exports via Turkey’s Ceyhan to 750,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Sunday a proposal to increase oil exports through the Turkish port of Ceyhan to 750,000 barrels per day by using tanker trucks to transport crude oil from southern oilfields.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the plan includes increasing exports through southern ports.

Iraq and Turkey recently inked a one-year short-term deal to continue operations through the critical Iraq-Turkey oil pipeline.

The agreement, reached in Ankara following discussions between Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar and Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair, guarantees the ongoing transportation of at least 750,000 barrels of Iraqi crude oil per day to the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Turkey’s state-owned crude oil and natural gas pipeline corporation (BOTAS) signed an agreement with Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) and the North Oil Company (NOC).

The new deal is now valid for 12 months until both countries develop a new, long-term legislative framework.

The previous agreement, which was reached in 1973, officially expired on July 27.

The short extension of the deal is crucial for Iraq’s revenue from oil exports, as Baghdad seeks alternative export routes to mitigate risks linked to the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Eto’o urges support for embattled FIFA president Infantino
World.content:
Paris – Former Cameroon star Samuel Eto’o has thrown his support behind beleaguered FIFA president Gianni Infantino, saying he “hasn’t done anything wrong” despite facing mounting pressure to step down over a controversial World Cup sell-off plan.

Infantino has come under intense scrutiny since the collapse of a proposal to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup.

UEFA, which oversees European football, has threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions with several continental and national federations also withdrawing their support for Infantino.

However, Eto’o, president of the Cameroonian football federation, dismissed criticism of Infantino’s leadership, suggesting the backlash was driven largely by political manoeuvring ahead of FIFA’s presidential election next year.

“I don’t think that President Gianni Infantino has done anything wrong,” the former Barcelona, Inter Milan and Chelsea striker told CNN.

“I think the timing of all of that is because there’s an election coming out.”

Infantino’s plan, which would reportedly have distributed substantial funding to FIFA’s 211 member associations, faced strong opposition from several confederations and was ultimately abandoned.

The FIFA president remains under pressure, with the possibility of a no-confidence vote being triggered. UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF — which governs North and Central America and the Caribbean — have all voiced concerns over FIFA’s direction in recent weeks.

But the Confederation of African Football (CAF) earlier this month “unanimously reconfirmed its support” for Infantino, and Eto’o’s backing is aligned with that position.

“President Gianni Infantino has changed football,” said Eto’o, urging fellow African countries to support the Swiss official.

“He’s given opportunities to nations that didn’t have those opportunities to take part in the most beautiful tournament, the World Cup. He enabled smaller nations to get seats at these competitions.

“He has helped our continent. He’s helped our federations to develop much more quickly, and we need to acknowledge that. We need to accept and recognise what he’s done, and we should support him for everything he’s done up to now.”

World.title: Trump claims Iran ‘collapsing’ as US threatens ‘economic D-Day’
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said Monday that Iran was “collapsing” as Washington prepared to announce the details of a new economic pressure campaign that Tehran has derided as an admission of defeat.

Almost six months into their war, the two sides are locked in a stalemate, with peace talks stalled, Iran keeping the key Strait of Hormuz shut and Washington persisting with a naval counter-blockade of Iran.

Under political pressure at home over the economic impacts of the conflict, Trump has pivoted away from military action to economic levers.

“IRAN IS COMPLETELY COLLAPSING!!!” the president posted Monday in his trademark all-caps style on his social media platform Truth Social.

His remarks came hours after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in a column for the Financial Times, declared that an “economic D-Day” had begun against Tehran and warned that any country that continued to enable the Islamic republic would become a “global pariah”.

Bessent also claimed on X that the US had “dismantled Iran’s military capabilities, destroyed nearly 100 percent of its military factories, and buried its nuclear programme”.

Iran responded with defiance, saying the latest US measures were an admission of military defeat, and it warned countries against aiding Washington.

Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi posted on X that the US turn to financial warfare proved Bessent’s claims false.

“Your narrative doesn’t add up,” Gharibabadi said, asking why, if Washington had achieved its goals, “there is a need for ‘the largest financial invasion in history’ and the mobilisation of ‘all institutions and powers’ of the United States!

“Is this a victory or an admission of America’s defeat?”

The US and Israel linked the launch of their war in February to Iran’s nuclear programme, but the focus since the early days of fighting has been on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global oil and gas supplies.

Tehran continues to blockade the strait, which it did not restrict before the war, driving up global inflation and heaping domestic pressure on Trump ahead of mid-term elections in November.

– Oil exports plunge –

Bessent was due to set out details of the US plan on Monday, but it is unclear how much more economic pressure Washington can put on Tehran.

The US naval blockade of Iran has seen its oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz fall from two million barrels a day pre-war to just 0.4 million by mid-August, according to maritime tracker Kpler.

Meanwhile, the country has been under crushing international sanctions for decades, with a brief period of easing under a 2015 nuclear deal that Trump later ripped up as part of a “maximum pressure” campaign.

The Islamic republic has weathered those efforts and, before the war, continued to export millions of barrels of oil, mostly to China, and evade sanctions through complex international financial networks.

Bessent and Trump have both warned countries against helping Iran, signalling a shift in their focus, with the Treasury secretary’s FT column dwelling on nations who “appease” and “enable” Iran.

Tehran responded on Monday by warning countries not to cooperate with the US efforts. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said taking part would “definitely have its own consequences”.

For ordinary Iranians, the standoff is likely to bring only more economic pain after years of rampant inflation, which in December and January fuelled massive anti-government protests.

Sarah Hassanbeigi, a 32-year-old pharmacist in Tehran, put it simply: “It’s really very difficult. I don’t think people can really take this much longer.”

On Sunday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian admitted that Iran faced “many problems in society”.

“We are striving with all our hearts to overcome inflation, livelihood problems, unemployment, and to secure the future of the people, so that they can live with dignity and pride,” Pezeshkian said.

– Delegation from Pakistan –

Last week, the Iranian president, considered a relative moderate, said Tehran should “bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity”.

That followed supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei appointing hardliners to key security positions.

Hassanbeigi said she wanted peace. “Naturally, negotiations mean that both sides have to compromise. My personal opinion is that Iran should compromise now,” she told AFP.

Throughout the war, diplomatic efforts, pushed on by mediators, have sought a negotiated end to the conflict.

On Monday, Pakistan’s army chief was expected in Iran. Islamabad was a leading mediator in talks that helped secure an April ceasefire that later fell apart.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi was also due in Iran on Tuesday, as Muscat and Tehran seek a deal on regulating passage through Hormuz.

World.title: Liverpool must improve on ‘unacceptable’ season, says Van Dijk
World.content:
Liverpool – Virgil van Dijk said Liverpool “need to show a reaction” from a bitterly disappointing season that cost Arne Slot his job as manager, but called for patience with new boss Andoni Iraola.

The Reds needed a 99th-minute equaliser from the penalty spot by Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue a 2-2 draw at Newcastle on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

Slot guided Liverpool to glory and a 20th league title in his debut campaign in 2024/25, but paid the price for finishing fifth last season when he was dismissed in May.

Many of the same flaws were in evidence in Iraola’s first outing at St James’ Park as Newcastle sliced open the Liverpool defence on the counter-attack.

But they twice came from behind to avoid a losing start to the new season.

“It’s absolutely normal in any type of profession, work, whatever you do, if you come in new and you have new plans and new ideas, then it takes a bit of time with new players,” said Van Dijk.

“It’s down to us to do it as soon as we can, as soon as possible, because we want to improve, we want to win, we want to be better. That’s what we are going to try to do.

“We need to show a reaction from last year, that we are much better than last year, because this was very unacceptable.”

Iraola has not been aided by a lack of new arrivals in the transfer market.

Despite the departure of club legend Mohamed Salah and a long-term injury to Hugo Ekitike, Liverpool have only added Spanish winger Victor Munoz in attacking areas as well as defenders Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo.

Paris Saint-Germain’s two-time Champions League winner Bradley Barcola has been linked with a move to Anfield, while two bids for Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh have reportedly been turned down.

“Everyone wants to see quality arrive regardless and I fully trust the club and the board to make the right decisions,” Van Dijk added.

“That’s the only thing I can say, so let’s see what we are going to do.”

World.title: Iraq suggests a security council involving Iran, Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has officially suggested forming a joint security coordination council with Iran and Saudi Arabia to address what it calls a severe crisis of trust between the two regional powers.

The Security Affairs Adviser to the Prime Minister of Iraq, Qasim al-Araji, put forward the diplomatic initiative on behalf of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government to stabilize the region where Iraq strives to manage its own turbulent security climate.

Baghdad clearly planned the initiative to reconcile serious tensions between Riyadh and Tehran.

Tensions rose as Saudi Arabia intercepted multiple drones aimed at its oil facilities and capital. Riyadh denounced Iran-backed militias that operate from inside Iraq.

The idea comes during a very unstable period, including recent US-Saudi joint airstrikes targeting Popular Mobilization Forces’ (PMF) sites in Iraq and leading to serious criticism from Baghdad for sovereignty violations.

Baghdad is also pressuring Tehran for waivers for oil tankers from Iran’s navigation restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Additionally, al-Araji underlined Iraq’s transition to ultimate domestic sovereignty.

With the scheduled withdrawal of the US-led international coalition forces from Iraq, Baghdad is adopting a strategy to put all armed factions and weaponry under strict state supervision, consolidating the country’s ultimate authority over war and peace choices.

Neither Saudi Arabia nor Iran has released a formal public response to the Iraqi initiative.

World.title: Iraq foreign reserves decline 11.6% to $86.17B in June 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Official financial statements from the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) show that Iraq’s foreign exchange reserves declined to $86.175 billion at the end of June 2026, marking a decrease of $11.257 billion (-11.6%) compared to the $97.432 billion recorded at the close of 2025.

According to reserve records published on Monday, August 24, 2026, the contraction followed an early-year peak above $102 billion before downward momentum set in through the second quarter.

Monthly Reserve Trajectory (H1 2026)

End of 2025 Baseline: $97.432 billion

January 2026: $101.082 billion

February 2026 (Peak): $102.131 billion

March 2026: $100.341 billion

April 2026: $97.809 billion

May 2026: $93.673 billion

June 2026:$86.175 billion(Month-over-month drop of $7.498 billion)

The overall drop reduced the local currency value of the total portfolio from 126.661 trillion IQD at the end of 2025 to 112.027 trillion IQD by June 30, 2026—a net decline of 14.634 trillion IQD (-11.6%).

World.title: National Security Adviser Al Aboudi meets U.S. Envoy on arms control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi met on Monday, August 24, 2026, with the Chargé d’Affaires of the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad, Joshua Harris, to discuss bilateral security cooperation, regional de-escalation, and Baghdad’s ongoing measures to restrict weapons exclusively to state control.

According to an official statement issued by the National Security Advisory, Al-Aboudi reaffirmed that the Iraqi government remains committed to maintaining national stability, mitigating broader regional tensions, and regulating the state monopoly over arms.

Key Discussion Pillars & Security Priorities

State Monopoly Over Arms: Al-Aboudi emphasized the government’s systematic implementation of regulatory frameworks designed to consolidate all weapons under official state security command.

Institutional Governance & Sovereign Decision-Making: Underlined Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s administrative vision focused on strengthening national defense and security institutions to support independent sovereign policymaking and economic recovery.

Counter-Terrorism & Intelligence Sharing: Reviewed shared security mechanisms between Baghdad and Washington, focusing on counter-terror operations, joint training, and strategic intelligence exchange.

Regional De-escalation: Discussed ongoing diplomatic and security initiatives to defuse regional friction and reinforce stability across the Middle East.

U.S. Diplomatic Backing: Harris affirmed Washington’s support for the Iraqi government’s security roadmap, institutional sovereignty, and regional stabilization initiatives.

The meeting between Al-Aboudi and Harris underscores consistent coordination between Baghdad and Washington on key security priorities, coming shortly after high-level diplomatic discussions on the U.S.–Iraq Strategic Framework Agreement.

By synchronizing counter-terrorism efforts with domestic initiatives to restrict unregulated weapons, Iraqi authorities aim to reinforce sovereign command structures, improve internal stability, and foster a secure environment for long-term economic investment.

World.title: Samarra Drug Company starts first domestic Moxifloxacin Antibiotic output
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The State Company for Drug Industries and Medical Appliances in Samarra (SDI), an affiliate of the Iraqi Ministry of Industry and Minerals, announced on Monday, August 24, 2026, the successful domestic production of Moxifloxacin, a broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic targeting five distinct bacterial infections, marking its first addition to the company’s manufacturing portfolio.

In an official statement received by IraqiNews.com, SDI Director General, Chemist Mohammed Abdul Qader Al-Nuaimi, confirmed that the formulation marks a key step in expanding state pharmaceutical production lines and bolstering domestic medical security.

Clinical Scope & Key Indications

Moxifloxacin is a fourth-generation synthetic fluoroquinolone antibiotic designed to treat severe and complex bacterial infections in adult patients, including:

Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Lower respiratory tract bacterial infections.

Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis: Bacterial flair-ups affecting chronic obstructive airway passages.

Acute Bacterial Sinusitis: Severe sinus and nasal inflammation.

Skin and Soft Tissue Infections: Complicated and uncomplicated bacterial dermatological and subcutaneous infections.

Other Complex Bacterial Invasions: Broad-spectrum systemic coverage against susceptible Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens.

Strategic Importance for National Drug Security

Import Substitution: Domestic manufacturing directly reduces the Ministry of Health’s reliance on foreign imported antibiotics, conserving foreign exchange reserves.

National Pharmaceutical Localization: Aligns with Iraq’s industrial localization roadmap aimed at strengthening the domestic supply chain for critical medications.

Supply Chain Reliability: Ensures stable, high-quality, and cost-effective medical supplies for state healthcare facilities and the local private retail market.

The launch of Moxifloxacin comes as part of the Samarra facility’s broader modernization drive to introduce advanced active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and expand local formulation capacities.

By localizing the manufacture of advanced broad-spectrum antibiotics, SDI continues to scale production lines to meet the clinical procurement requirements of Iraqi hospitals and healthcare centers.

World.title: Surprise protests, GenZ outreach: Rahul Gandhi's new playbook after CJP's success
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

"I will not leave till you lodge an FIR. He has pellet injuries on his body, has lost his eye, and we are demanding an FIR for thisâ¦ I will go outside and sit there until you lodge an FIR.

I will sit for 10 days, 20 days, 30 days, 50 days, six months.

Your government will have a problem."

There is a visible change in how

pushes through issues now. The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha has a new weapon in his political arsenal: impromptu protests.

For the second time in a month, the Congress leader caught the authorities and, to some extent, even his own party, off guard by taking to the streets of the national capital without prior warning.

When Rahul reached the DCP office in Delhi on August 21 demanding an FIR for Sahil Lohchab, who sustained pellet injuries during the July 20 student protest, it was Act 2 of his new playbook of street protest politics.

When the cops dilly-dallied, Rahul refused to budge and staged a sit-in protest outside the police station. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra joined him. Congress leaders began arriving. Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed outside.





A visit to a police office turned into a high-voltage political stand-off and, after six hours of dharna, Delhi Police registered an FIR over the pellet firing.

'Politics of anarchy'

The BJP reacted sharply, calling Rahul's sit-in the 'politics of anarchy'. It argued that an FIR relating to the wider July 20 incident already existed, an investigation was under way and the Congress leader was turning police procedure into a political spectacle.

For Lohchab, however, there was a sense of relief. His family had been trying to get his complaint registered since August 14, shuttling between police stations. The 19-year-old, who underwent surgery after pellets struck his right eye, finally had an FIR registered after Rahulâs intervention.

According to Lochav's lawyer, the police returned the complaint after reading it and made them wait for a long time.

For years, opponents have labelled Rahul Gandhi a 'part-time politician' who would raise an issue and then disappear.

But this incident reinforced something that has changed about Rahulâs tactics over the past year. He is no longer content merely to raise an issue. He increasingly wants to enter it, stay with it and, if necessary, physically occupy the space.

Rahul's new playbook

The first display of this surprise street-politics instinct had come a month earlier during the NEET student protests.

On July 21, a day after police used force to stop thousands of students attempting a 'Sansad Chalo' march over exam irregularities, Rahul suddenly headed towards Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs residence and staged a sit-in.

Police had reportedly made arrangements anticipating a Congress protest at Vijay Chowk. Rahul went to Lok Kalyan Marg instead. The move caught security officials by surprise. Rahul, Priyanka and several other opposition leaders were later detained. The visual that immediately took over the news was hard to ignore: the leader of opposition physically struggling with police officers, being dragged away and getting a nosebleed in the chaos.

Police personnel detained Rahul Gandhi during a sit-in protest near the Prime Minister's residence.

That was Act 1.

It came at a time when the Congress was desperately trying to make its presence felt, with Abhijeet Dipkeâs Cockroach Janata Party and climate activist

already leading a massive student protest against the NEET paper leak.

Congress had initially kept its distance, preferring to run its own youth outreach campaign, 'Chhatron Ki Goonj'. But people asked a simple question: If Congress claimed to support student issues, why was it missing from the biggest student movement in Delhi?

When the July 20 Jantar Mantar protest took place and massive outrage erupted over police action against the student protesters, Rahul's approach changed.

The very next day, he moved to the front lines. He stood outside the Prime Minister's house, Congress leaders visited injured students, and police action became a major national debate. Rahul took the issue to Parliament and continued raising the pitch over injuries suffered by students.

And when the larger protest began to recede from the headlines, Rahul stayed with one part of it: the use of pellet guns. He has affirmed that his party will keep raising the issue and demand accountability.

Rahul's changing style

The first major image makeover was when Rahul Gandhi embarked on the '

' from Kanyakumari to Kashmir in 2022. Sceptics and rivals wondered if he would complete the journey. By the time he reached Kashmir months later, after walking thousands of kilometres in his now-signature white T-shirt, one charge had become considerably harder to make: that Rahul was unwilling to put in the physical grind that it takes in politics.

The yatra, on its own, did not help the Congress much. What it did was change the way Rahul himself was seen as a politician.

For months, people saw him walking with the common public rather than delivering a scripted speech from a podium. He met farmers, labourers and students, stopped for conversations, entered homes and sat and ate with people.

The yatra experience also laid the foundation for his growing social media popularity.

His online presence today increasingly relies on short, conversational exchanges that can easily travel as reels and clips.

The second shift came in 2024, when he became the leader of the opposition.

Since then, we have seen a more combative Rahul Gandhi. Whether one agrees with his politics or the issues he raises, he appears considerably more comfortable with confrontation than he once did.

Congress's protests in the Parliament complex have also become more visual and experimental under Rahul.

He repeatedly joined opposition MPs at Makar Dwar over the Election Commissionâs SIR exercise in Bihar, with MPs carrying 'vote chori' placards and demanding its rollback. The protest later moved beyond the Parliament gates, with Rahul and other opposition leaders marching towards the Election Commission before being stopped and detained.

Rahul provokes ministers across the aisle and stays for the response.

He takes an argument from the street into Parliament and, increasingly, carries it back outside again. This is also a part of his renewed Gen Z outreach.

'Chhatron Ki Goonj'

If Bharat Jodo helped Rahul Gandhi build the image of a politician who was more approachable and willing to listen, 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' took that idea to a more specific audience: Gen Z.

The programme began in Kota, where students spoke about paper leaks, recruitment delays, coaching pressure and the uncertainty around exams and jobs.

The format was less rally and more conversation, with Rahul asking questions, listening, and allowing individual experiences to shape the message. That made the outreach more relatable.

His latest Pune edition further widened that outreach by putting young women at the centre of the conversation.

Rahul's call to 'smash the patriarchy' in a stadium full of women was a strong message that came with its own set of criticism.

He spoke about different social expectations for boys and girls, cited the 'Manusmriti' while attacking the BJP-RSS worldview, and told women that they 'belong' to themselves rather than to fathers, husbands or sons, triggering huge applause from the crowd.

While a large section of people lauded the focus on women, the ruling BJP immediately trained its guns on him and asked him to induct women ministers into the Karnataka cabinet, where Congress is in power.

The Jharkhand dilemma

Even as Rahul attacked the BJP over issues such as NEET and paper leaks, major student protests broke out in Jharkhand, where the Congress shares power in the Hemant Soren government. Soon after the Jantar Mantar agitation ended, aspirants took to the streets in Ranchi over alleged irregularities and paper leaks in JPSC and JSSC examinations.

The BJP MP further dared Rahul Gandhi to take a decisive political stand instead of limiting his activism to social media platforms.

This time, the criticism was closer to home. Protesters targeted not just chief minister Hemant Soren but Rahul as well, pointing to the irony of him speaking for students nationally while Congress was part of the ruling alliance in Jharkhand.

Effigies of both leaders were burnt, and Rahul was accused of not speaking about Jharkhand issues.

Eventually, Rahul was forced to react and intervene. He asserted that Congress supported students protesting peacefully and said that dialogue was the only way forward.

Rahul Gandhi also urged Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren to personally meet representatives of students protesting irregularities in state recruitment examinations and address their remaining concerns.

Rahul wrote an open letter to Soren, requesting the CM to personally meet the students and hear out their grievances. The Jharkhand government later accepted the students' demands.

The episode helped Rahul avoid the charge of being selective on student issues, but it also showed the challenge of claiming an issue as your own: once you do that, you can be questioned even when the government under fire is run by an ally.

Has Rahul evolved as a leader?

For years, Rahul Gandhi was accused of being an inconsistent politician who would raise important issues and then disappear from the conversation. Rivals branded him as an âentitled leaderâ and took âPappuâ digs at him.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

But the old image of Rahul as a reluctant politician is certainly harder to sustain today. From Bharat Jodo to 'Chhatron Ki Goonj', fiery parliamentary confrontations and surprise dharnas, he appears more comfortable playing on the front foot.

However, his latest round of street protests seems to stem from the crisis that the opposition in general and Congress in particular faced as Abhijeet Dipke-led CJP mobilised youth in large numbers and forced the government to make Dharmendra Pradhan resign as Union education minister.

Rahul has made his presence felt, but we will have to wait and see if his new politics translates into electoral success for the Congress.

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Arvind Kejriwal will address a town hall on E20 petrol policy during his two-day visit to Goa beginning Monday.Kejriwal landed at Dabolim Airport in south Goa on Sunday, where he was received by local party leaders.AAP sources said Kejriwal would address a press conference on Monday in Panaji and a town hall a day later on E20 petrol policy.The AAP, which has two MLAs in the 40-member Goa assembly, has announced a campaign against the "forced implementation" of E20 (ethanol-blended) fuel in the coastal state, which will go to polls in 2027.Earlier this month, Kejriwal had demanded the government give the option to choose between pure petrol and E20 at fuel pumps.The Centre introduced E20, a blend of 20 per cent ethanol and 80 per cent petrol, as part of efforts to reduce vehicular emissions and cut dependence on crude oil imports. World.title: Mumbai food safety crackdown: FDA shuts 5 MCA restaurants over hygiene violations
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of five restaurants operating at the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) premises in Mumbai over serious food safety and hygiene violations, officials said.

The inspections uncovered rotten raw food, poor sanitation and improper temperature control.

According to details released by the FDA, the action was taken against the Permit Room, Pavilion, Mediterranean, Oriental Swing, and Clubway & Pastry Counter at the MCA. The establishments were found to have violated several food safety norms, including inadequate hygiene practices and improper handling and storage of food.

During the inspections, officials found rotten raw food, poor general sanitation and improper freezing temperature control. Food handlers were also found not wearing gloves, raising concerns over the risk of contamination.

The FDA has also suspended the licence of Sankalp Mahila Audyogik Utpadak Sahakari Society Limited in Kurla, which operated a mid-day meal canteen. Officials cited poor general hygiene and housekeeping, along with structural and sanitation-related deficiencies.

The inspection reportedly found dirt and grease accumulated on walls and ceilings, cracked floors where water and food waste had pooled, and inadequate pest-exclusion barriers at the premises.

NEW DELHI: Despite the flexibility offered by platform work, womenâs participation in Indiaâs growing platform economy remains constrained by limited access to formal financial services, gaps in digital literacy, safety concerns and restrictive social norms, an ILO-NCAER policy brief said on Monday.The brief, âAdvancing Womenâs Digital Financial Inclusion in the Platform Economyâ, said women need access to a range of financial services throughout their platform-work journey, including start-up capital, short-term credit, insurance, savings and financial planning tools.It highlighted cashflow-based lending as a key lever for inclusion, particularly because women are less likely to own land or property that can be used as collateral. Digital records of platform payments can provide lenders with verifiable evidence of income and repayment capacity.Addressing a Roundtable at the release of the Policy Brief, NCAER director general Suresh Goyal said, âA womanâs best protection is a little money of her own and access to credit and mobility are important conditions for women to have better employment opportunities. Platform economy has given that opportunity.âThe brief identified two ways to leverage womenâs digital footprints: using Indiaâs Digital Public Infrastructure, including the Account Aggregator framework, to make financial data portable, and enabling platforms to partner with lenders to offer loans, savings and insurance through their apps.ILO country director Michiko Miyamoto said, âDigital financial inclusion must enable women to build income security, resilience, and sustainable livelihoods."ILO Senior Specialist Radhicka Kapoor said integrating financial DPI with e-Shram records could further expand access, provided safeguards against algorithmic bias are built in.The brief also flagged device ownership as a barrier, noting that womenâs digital access is often mediated through family members.NITI Aayog estimates Indiaâs platform workforce could rise from 12 million in 2024-25 to 23.5 million by 2029-30.Director of NCAERâs Centre for Gender and Macroeconomy, Prof. Ratna Sahay, summed up the key takeaway, âDigital footprint in platform economies can be a game-changer for women to access credit, underpinned by regulation that encourages innovation while ensuring consumer protection and financial stability.â

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has announced a youth march on September 5 in Delhi, accusing the government of failing to honour commitments that led to the withdrawal of the studentsâ protest at Jantar Mantar on July 25. The CJP said the government had failed to act on its assurance to withdraw FIRs against students and protesting students.The march will begin at India Gate and proceed towards the New Delhi Police Headquarters, according to a statement issued by the CJP National Working Committee, posted on X. The organisation said the protest would be led by families of deceased NEET victims and victims of alleged police brutality, with students and youth organisations expected to join.In the post, the CJP said, âThe Cockroach Janta Party strongly condemns the Union Governmentâs failure to honour the commitments made to Indiaâs youth on July 25, particularly those concerning the withdrawal of FIRs against students and protesters.ââWith the Government continuing to delay and avoid fulfilling its assurances, the CJP National Working Committee has decided to resume peaceful mobilisation,â it said.The CJP said the decision followed a review of the commitments it alleges were made by the government on July 25, after which nationwide youth protests were withdrawn.The statement said the committee had expressed âserious doubts over whether the Government intends to honour its word at allâ, alleging that the government had delayed action and avoided providing clear commitments.It also referred to proceedings before the Supreme Court, saying that on August 18, the court had sought a list of FIRs registered across the country so that it could consider dealing with them together. The CJP alleged that the government had not given a clear commitment on the issue.The organisation also added, âThis cannot continue. Our patience cannot be mistaken for weakness. Our good faith cannot become an opportunity for the Government to betray us.âAnnouncing the September 5 mobilisation, the CJP said, âWe announce a peaceful protest march from India Gate to the new Delhi Police Headquarters on 5 September, led by the families of the deceased NEET victims and victims of police brutality, and joined by students and young citizens from across the country.âThe group said it had returned to the streets because the government âappears determined to commit a âvishwasghaatâ with Gen-Z, the young generation of this country, and the families who have already lost their children.âIt further said, âWe withdrew a nationwide movement in good faith. A government cannot take the trust of an entire generation, use it to send them home, and then quietly retreat from its own word. We will not accept this attempted betrayal.âThe CJP has urged students, youth organisations and young citizens to gather at India Gate on September 5. âThe families who lost their children will walk at the front. Victims of police brutality will walk with them,â the statement said.Earlier, the CJP, that describes itself as a youth-focused movement, had led a 37-day protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, alongside activist Sonam Wangchukâs 26-day hunger strike.On July 25, following talks with Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh, the CJP said the government had accepted its demands, including suitable compensation for families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide and withdrawal of FIRs against protesters. âAll our demands have been accepted, so we request the protesters to withdraw immediately and return home peacefully,â it said.The Supreme Court later directed states to release eligible students detained during the protests and barred coercive action against students for the time being.

World.content:
Kolkata

Since the Bharatiya Janata Party came to power in West Bengal on May 4, its government has cracked down on roadside dwellers, encroachers, hawkers and slum residents. Against this backdrop, Minister Agnimitra Paul’s recent remarks to a homeless woman heating milk for her child on a Kolkata pavement have sparked outrage and criticism in the State.

On Saturday (August 22, 2026) afternoon, Ms. Paul, the Minister-in-Charge for Urban Development and Municipal Affairs, was seen reprimanding a homeless woman on a footpath in Kolkata’s Park Street area. The woman was heating milk in a pot to feed her child. “Heating milk for a child on the pavement? In Park Street? Who gave you permission to set up your household here?” Ms. Paul was heard saying. She then asked the woman to remove her belongings from the road in the presence of several Kolkata police personnel.

On Monday (August 24, 2026), Trinamool Congress chairperson and former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee said she and her party are willing to take complete responsibility for the homeless family and their child.

Ms. Banerjee said poverty is not a crime and urged the current BJP government and its leaders not to “hate the poor.”

“Did you not feel ashamed to throw the milk? A mother’s curse is immensely powerful; remember that. I can take responsibility for this family. I can arrange for them to stay at any Trinamool worker‘s home, eat, and educate their children,” Ms. Banerjee said.

In interviews with local news organisations, the woman questioned whether anyone would “willingly” live on the roads if they had anywhere better to go.

Ms. Paul’s comments have since gone viral, with citizens and politicians criticising her words and several artists responding with satirical cartoons. Since Sunday, social media has been flooded with questions about the State’s responsibility to provide shelter to the homeless.

On Monday (August 24), Ms. Paul defended her comments in a video on social media platforms, stating that unless the condition of the footpaths is improved, investors will not come to West Bengal. “Many are crying over what I said, but no one has come forward with a bowl of milk to help this family. Everyone is just busy doing politics,” Ms. Paul said.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari also reacted to the controversy and appeared to back her Cabinet colleague. He said Ms. Banerjee is welcome to “ keep the [homeless] woman at her residence”.

On Sunday (August 23), Trinamool Congress MLA Kunal Ghosh met the woman. “Thinking about why the poor have to live on footpaths is the state’s responsibility,” Mr. Ghosh said.

Ms. Paul had to face criticism earlier in the week for another remark.

On Friday (August 21), while sitting on a relief boat in a flood-affected area in rural West Bengal, Ms. Paul quoted a few words from the National Song Vande Mataram and described the flood-hit parts of West Bengal as “Sujalam Sufalam“ (abundant water and bountiful harvest) and said even though people may face problems, the beauty of the place is unparalleled.

Ms. Banerjee criticised this comment and asked, “Are you happy when people lose everything in the floods?”

World.title: Worker suffers 40% burns in fireworks unit near Sivakasi
World.content:
A 58-year-old man, identified as Veluchami, suffered 40% burns when he was handling chemicals in a fireworks unit in Virudhunagar district on Monday.

Police said Ramamurthi of Thayilpatti near Sivakasi owned a fireworks unit. Over 50 workers were present on the premises in different sheds/rooms engaged in manufacturing crackers.

At around 11 a.m., when Mr. Veluchami was carrying some fuse, it suddenly went off and there was fire all around. At least three sheds were destroyed in the accident, according to workers.

On information, Fire and Rescue Services personnel from Vembakottai put out the fire. Many other workers, who were injured, were also rushed to the hospital. Doctors said Mr. Veluchami was given treatment for burns by a team.

Vembakottai police have registered a case.

World.title: Puducherry Budget: Financial assistance announced for Karaikal farmers
World.content:
The Puducherry government has proposed to provide financial assistance of ₹1,500 per hectare for farmers in Karaikal undertaking summer crop cultivation, in the wake of uncertainty in Cauvery water supply, Chief Minister N. Rangasamy said on Monday.

According to the Budget for 2026-27 presented by him in the Assembly, agriculture in Karaikal is heavily dependent on Cauvery water, and farmers face severe hardships when water availability is uncertain during the summer months. To address, this the government proposes to provide a financial assistance of ₹1,500 per hectare. This will entail an annual expenditure of ₹1.13 crore.

An Integrated Centre of Excellence for Fruit and Vegetable Processing and a Custom Hiring Centre for Farm Machinery will be established at the Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru College of Agriculture and Research Institute in Karaikal under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana.

The government will also provide assistance for a turmeric processing unit under the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture recognising the demand for organically-grown produce and processed foods in the Union Territory. Farmers will also be supported to purchase solar-powered crop dryers to reduce post-harvest losses and preserve agricultural produce.

Animal Husbandry

The government will provide milking machines to 150 beneficiaries at 100% subsidy at a total cost of ₹75 lakh to improve the quality of milk production and address the shortage of manpower.

World.title: Traffic diversions in Bengaluru on August 26 for Eid Milad procession
World.content:
Traffic has been diverted across several parts of Bengaluru city in view of the Eid Milad procession scheduled for Wednesday.

Members of the Muslim community will arrive at the YMCA Ground on Nrupatunga Road between noon and 11 p.m. With large-scale movement expected, traffic congestion is likely on J.C. Road, R.R.M.R. Road, Kasturba Road, Devanga Road, Mallya Hospital Road, K.G. Road, R.T. Nagar Main Road, Chamundinagar Main Road, Dinnur Main Road, Deve Gowda Road, Jayamahal Road, Church Road, Nagawara Main Road, Tannery Main Road, and Haines Road-Miller’s Road.

According to the traffic police, vehicles travelling from Mysuru Road towards Majestic would be diverted through Nayandahalli Junction, Nagarabhavi Circle, Madduramma Temple, Chandra Layout Junction, R.P.C. Layout Junction, West of Chord Road, Vijayanagar Metro Station, Toll Gate Junction, Prasanna Junction, Hunasemara Junction, Lulu Mall, Okalipuram Junction, and Khode Junction before proceeding towards Majestic.

Vehicles from Mysuru Road can also reach West of Chord Road through Deepanjalinagar Junction and proceed via Vijayanagar and Magadi Road towards Majestic or K.R. Market.

Those travelling from Mysuru Road towards K.R. Market would be diverted through Nagarabhavi, Chandra Layout, R.P.C. Layout, West of Chord Road, Vijayanagar, Toll Gate, Prasanna Junction, Hunasemara Junction, Binny Mill Junction, Goodshed Road, Rayyan Road, Shanthala Circle, Khode Junction, Lakshmanpuri Bridge, Freedom Park Junction, K.R. Circle, Cubbon Park, Library Road, Hudson Circle, Town Hall Junction, and N.R. Road.

When the procession reaches Market Circle, vehicles at A.S. Char Street Junction would be diverted towards B.V.K. Iyengar Road. Vehicles arriving from G.P. Street via S.R. Road would not be permitted to enter S.R. Street and would instead be diverted through G.P. Street towards B.V.K. Iyengar Road, the traffic police said.

Vehicles approaching Market Circle from K.R. Road would be diverted through Prof. Shivashankarappa Circle, L.B.F. Road, J.C. Road and Town Hall. Vehicles reaching K.R. Road through A.V. Road would proceed towards Minto Circle.

Further, when the procession reaches S.J.P. Road, vehicles coming from Mysuru Road would be diverted at City Market Circle towards Kalasipalya Main Road, K.P. Point, Basappa Circle, L.B.F. Road, J.C. Road, and Town Hall.

The traffic police have advised motorists to plan their journeys and use the designated alternative routes to avoid congestion and delays during the procession.

World.title: Dalit body seeks action against discrimination faced by SCs
World.content:
Even after eight decades of Indian Independence, Scheduled Caste (SC) people are still facing discrimination, said V. Srinivasa Rao, national leader of Dalit Shoshan Mukti Manch (DSMM), which organised the ‘Samajika Sankharavam Maha Dharna’, in front of Prakasam Bhavan in Ongole on Monday.

Addressing the media, he said that if the issues plaguing Dalit localities in the State were not resolved within the next three months, ‘Chalo Amaravati’ would be launched in December 2026. This follows a campaign conducted over the past two months by Kula Vivaksha Porata Samithi (KVPS), an organisation for struggle against caste discrimination.

Mr. Srinivasa Rao stated that people in Dalit localities were forced to struggle for basic amenities such as drinking water, roads, housing, education, and healthcare. “The discrimination persists even in the conduct of final rites at cremation grounds. Even in the capital city of Amaravati, there are occurences where houses are not rented out to SCs,” he claimed.

“The SC employees face discrimination at their workplaces as well. The government has failed to implement rights guaranteed by the Constitution and the law. A comprehensive audit must be done on the utilisation of SC/ST sub-plan funds. Dalit entrepreneurs have been forced to take to the streets with their families as the subsidy funds were not released to them,” Mr. Srinivasa Rao added.

World.title: Political controversies make CPI(M) grassroots workers anxious, says FB post of VS’s son
World.content:
A cryptic Facebook post by V.A. Arun Kumar, son of the late communist leader V.S. Achuthanandan, has led to discussions about the ‘crisis’ in the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] engendered by the latest revelations made by the Enforcement Directorate about the inquiry against T. Veena, daughter of Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan.

Mr. Arun Kumar says that the present political controversies and campaigns would have naturally made the grassroots workers of the CPI(M) anxious. “It’s a natural democratic process for the leadership to come forward and speak openly to the people and politically defend itself. But there’s a fundamental truth to be remembered during any crisis: that this movement was not built on the interests of any individuals, but on the faith of generations of poor people who have given it their blood and sweat,” he wrote.

While politically defending the smear campaigns, the party should exercise caution at each stage to ensure that its credibility doesn’t even suffer a scratch in the eyes of ordinary people. The Left movement becomes stronger when it avoids mistakes and is able to move forward transparently, dispelling people’s doubts. “As my father always reminded us, the people are the masters of this political movement, and their trust is its greatest capital,” Mr. Arun Kumar wrote.

World.title: ‘Naa Ramudu, a simplified Ramayanam, book released in Srikakulam
World.content:
Religious scholar and poet Yerrapragada Ramakrishna said that epic Valmiki Ramayanam would continue to make writers to identify new points and present them in a novel way to enable new generation to understand the great values adopted by Lord Rama and Goddess Sita.

He released ‘Naa Ramudu’ book written by academician and executive committee member of Indian Red Cross Society in a programme organised in Srikakulam on Monday.

He lauded Nikku Appana for penning the Ramayanam to enable everyone to understand the ethical values, importance for words of parents, acceptance of people’s opinion in the administration and others.

Mr. Appanna said that the recently constructed Lord Rama’s temple in Ayodhya and his personal attachments with temples located in Srikakulam and other places made him to write ‘Naa Ramudu’ book after careful study of Ramayanam books written by many scholars.

IRCS Srikakulam Chairman P. Jagan Mohana Rao, several writers and poets felicitated both Mr. Ramakrishna and Mr. Appanna on the occasion.

They said that Mr. Appanna had proved that age is not be a barrier for study and publication of books for the benefit of the society.

World.title: SIR leaves out 5.13 lakh voter names in Belagavi
World.content:
The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter list has left 5.13 lakh names of voters out of the electoral rolls in Belagavi district.

This is a reduction of 12.49% from the earlier rolls.

As per the draft list published on Monday, there are 35,93,561 voters in the district.

The earlier rolls contained 41.06 lakh voters. Of these, 18,05,685 are males, 17,87,715 females and 161 gender minorities.

District Election Officer and Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Roshan told reporters in Belagavi on Monday that the SIR has removed 5,13,439 names of voters.
